title: Route each job to an env of its build line, not one global active env
description:
Env resolution ignores the job's target (env_resolver.resolve_env_for_job: job.dev_env, then the active env, then --env, then the sole env). On a host with one env per build line, jobs for every line but the selected env's are held (poly-7pwa.14 HOLD, runner._lines_held_back/_waits_for_its_line), and only the selected env is health-probed. acemagic sat paused on "2 dev-envs exist; select one". Nothing stops the runner from running each job in an env of its own line.

Reviewed 2026-10-05 (Fable, read-only): premise confirmed; plan revised to route by build line first and stamp the source env second.
design:
RULE (resolve_env_for_job takes the job's target):
candidates = envs_by_build_line()[build_line(target)].
1. job.dev_env, if it is a candidate. If it names another line: refuse (7pwa.14). If that env no longer exists: fall through, don't refuse.
2. the active env (per builder, then default), if it is a candidate. It becomes "preferred env for its line".
3. the sole candidate.
4. several candidates, no preference: hold, naming them. No candidate: refuse.
On a one-env-per-line host this routes every job with no schema, hook or UI change. The runner still runs one job at a time.

SOURCE-ENV STAMP (step 4, for two envs of one line):
dsynth strips the environment, so the hook cannot see its env from env vars. hooks-install already writes DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET from state.target into each chroot's dportsv3-hooks.conf (dev-env/dports_dev_env/hooks.py); add DPORTSV3_TRACKER_DEV_ENV=<state.name>, have hook_common.sh write dev_env= into the job and pass --dev-env to job-transition, land it in jobs.dev_env, carry it through _QUEUED_TRIAGE_SQL/_job_meta_from_row. Allowlist it in tests/test_settings_unification.py beside DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET. Fallback without a stamp: PROFILE == sanitize_name(env name) (dsynth.py), only when that env composes the job's line.

KEEP: _check_env_build_line as the job-start backstop, the startup reap keep-set, the verify-request refusal (the operator chose that env).

PLAN (each step testable alone):
1. env_resolver: target-aware rule above; unit tests.
2. Runner claim: per-job resolution replaces _lines_held_back/_waits_for_its_line; hold only on ambiguity or a broken env, reported per line in _idle_stage; process_build_requests pins the line's resolved env. Invert the hold tests in tests/test_env_target_mismatch.py.
3. Gate: probe the env a job resolves to (not one global env); drop the global "no env, no jobs" pause when a job resolves; sweep worktrees in every env (startup sweep is single-env today). Update test_env_gate_unresolved.py, test_runner_env_re_resolve.py.
4. Source-env stamp, as above.
5. Tracker/docs: runner page and index banner show env per line (env_health_status.detail.target, recorded since 2c7f472); verify_fix CLI fallback by bundle line; rewrite docs/AGENTIC_BUILDS.md env section and the resolver docstring.
6. Only if two envs of one line appear: per-line preference storage and UI.

REJECTED: one runner per env. Multi-runner on one state.db is unsupported (global startup sweeps, verify/confirm feeds with no runner filter) and the host-wide dsynth-busy gate (pgrep -x dsynth, ignores env) serialises them anyway; that is poly-fij.10's lease model.

RISKS: hold tests invert; resolver signature change touches test_env_resolver.py, test_env_per_builder.py, test_job_dev_env_recorded.py; per-env health costs one dev-env exec per env per cache period (probe lazily); UI wording "active env" -> "preferred env for its line".
notes:
Landed in d0fce69 (plan steps 1-3, most of 5): target-aware resolve_env_for_job; claim holds only ambiguous lines, broken envs (also for pinned jobs) and targetless jobs with >1 env and no preference; gate probes every routed env and pauses only when all are broken; confirm builds pinned to their line's env; startup sweeps every env; verify-fix fallback routes by bundle line; runner page shows each env's line. Fable re-review findings all addressed.
Left: step 4 (hook stamps DPORTSV3_TRACKER_DEV_ENV), step 6 (per-line preference storage), index banner per line (agentic_index.html still 'Env auto'), cache envs_by_build_line per tick (read 3x per loop), no unit test drives _gate_blocked's partial-broken logging.

title: Verify picker offers dev-envs that compose another build line
description:
The bundle page's Verify env picker lists every env from env_health_status and pre-selects the tracker-wide default env (unset here), falling back to the first env listed (2026Q3). For a @main bundle that sends env 2026Q3, which the runner then refuses (verify_refused_env_target_mismatch, poly-7pwa.14): 2026-10-05, devel/samurai requests 199 and 200.

Fix: the runner records each env's compose target in its env_health_status row; the picker drops envs known to compose another line than the bundle's target and pre-selects a matching one.
notes: Fixed in 2c7f472: runner records target in env_health_status.detail_json; fix_state.verify_env_choices filters/pre-selects. Needs deploy + runner restart so stub/probe rows carry target.

title: the patch playbooks and quickref state four things the engine does not do: scope cures an ambiguous match, writes under ports/ are banned, mk set obeys on-missing for an absent variable, warn is right for cross-line idempotency
description: Filed 2026-10-04 by the poly-7pwa spec review (round 2). DESIGN holds the problem, the evidence and the change; ACCEPTANCE says when it is done.
design:
STATE, 2026-10-04. New, split from poly-7pwa.4, whose 2026-09 notes listed
most of these. Lands after poly-7pwa.21 (on master once the branch is
merged, the epic's D7). Rows 6a-14 do not touch the lines below: every OLD
string is as on master ab725ac plus the seven picks, and occurs exactly
once, so match the strings. Line numbers are after the picks and move
later: row 6a moves flow-patch.md lines below 194 up by 3 (F3 then sits
at 261-263), and row 11 adds a section to docs/dsl-v0.md above M1's line
(166 after the picks, 186 after row 11).

PREMISE, verified 2026-10-04 by running the engine (apply_dsl,
build_plan) and the worker's put_file guards on master ab725ac plus the
seven picks.
1. Scope does not cure an ambiguous match. flow-patch.md:135 ("Narrow it
   with scope (see below)") and :186-188 ("Scope is also a
   disambiguation lever") say it does. mk set FOO in a target @main block
   over a Makefile that assigns FOO twice fails E_APPLY_AMBIGUOUS_MATCH on
   @main, as in @any. The widened remedy matters: text replace-once
   refuses the same way when its from text repeats. On freebsd-ports
   main, dns/bind9-devel and dns/bind920 repeat "PORTREVISION=<tab>0";
   www/angie repeats "PORTREVISION=<tab>${ANGIE_PORTREVISION}" and the
   line above it (it assigns PORTREVISION three times). There only a from
   string extended with the following line applies.
2. Writes under ports/ are not banned. flow-patch.md:264-266 says "to
   ports/<origin>/ it is not" allowed. No guard refuses a patch or
   overlay.dops write under /work/DeltaPorts/ports/<origin>/, the scoped
   dragonfly/@<target>/ lane included. _reject_dports_write
   (worker.py:329) refuses only /work/DPorts/ and /work/artifacts/compose/;
   the only path refused under ports/ is Makefile.DragonFly*
   (_reject_makefile_dragonfly_authoring, worker.py:255).
3. mk set does not obey on-missing for an absent variable.
   dops_quickref.md:61-64 says "on-missing error # default: fail if not
   found". mk set inserts the variable under default, error, warn and noop
   alike, with no diagnostic. on-missing decides only when the Makefile
   itself is absent: the default fails E_APPLY_MISSING_SUBJECT, warn skips
   with W_APPLY_ON_MISSING_WARN, noop skips.
4. warn is not right for cross-line idempotency. dops_quickref.md:232-235
   recommends it "when an op is idempotent across targets". An env builds
   one line, and on-missing error is the only signal another line gets
   that an op no longer fits it (text replace-once with an absent anchor:
   the default fails E_APPLY_MISSING_SUBJECT, warn skips). Its example at
   dops_quickref.md:143, "file remove files/patch-stale on-missing warn",
   is the pattern an agent copies. 163 @any ops in 79 overlays already
   carry warn or noop (159 noop, 4 warn); all plan clean today.
Also verified:
- The comma list, target @2026Q3,@main, is in no agent document. Without
  a space it applies on exactly those lines and on no later one; with a
  space ("@2026Q3, @main") build_plan fails E_PARSE_EXPECTED_NEWLINE.
- docs/dsl-v0.md:166 says mk add and mk remove "still require an existing
  assignment". mk add on an absent variable creates "<VAR>= <token>"; only
  mk remove fails (E_APPLY_MISSING_SUBJECT).
- No playbook or prompt mentions on-missing; the agent learns it from the
  quickref, which reaches it only through dops_reference (how often that
  is called is UNVERIFIED).

title: the patch agent edits overlay.dops only through the edit commands
description:
Point the patch agent at the edit library.

  - Tools wrap the library host-side, the way install_patches already works.
    No file content passes through the model: a patch is still produced into
    genpatch-out and installed by name.
  - The worker refuses edit_file and put_file on overlay.dops. An edit the
    library refuses hands the attempt to an operator, not back to hand
    editing -- otherwise every hazard the library removes comes back through
    the fallback. Every merged agent overlay change so far is expressible as
    the commands (148 pure op edits; the rest comments and header).
  - Scope defaults to @any. Every merged agent fix so far was @any, and a
    wrongly shared change fails loudly on the other build line where a
    wrongly scoped one is silent (poly-7pwa.4's notes). Scoping is an
    explicit argument.
  - Each tool returns the per-build-line plan diff, so the agent sees when an
    edit changes build lines it cannot build.
  - The playbooks' mechanics prose (where to put a line, apply order, payload
    folders) is deleted, not rewritten.

Depends on the library.
notes:
2026-10-04 (poly-7pwa round 2). Start only after poly-7pwa merges to master
(poly-7pwa D7). This bead deletes the playbooks' mechanics prose that
poly-7pwa.21 rows 1, 6, 12 and 13 bring (apply order, where to put a line,
payload placement), and with it 4af6339's four prose-pinning tests in
tests/test_apply_order_is_by_scope.py:
test_the_playbook_no_longer_claims_plain_declaration_order,
test_the_playbook_states_the_rule_and_that_only_one_target_is_built,
test_the_tool_description_states_apply_order_not_declaration_order and
test_the_quickref_states_the_ordering_rule. It does not delete scope_check.py
or the harness-notes channel: poly-7pwa.8 deletes scope_check.py (moving
payload_identity to dportsv3/engine/models.op_identity) and keeps
attempt_loop.run's state_notes list as the channel. If this bead starts before
.8 has landed, leave scope_check.py alone. .8's MISSED note stays after this
bead: it also covers payload-only misses the editor does not see.

title: dportsv3 dsl edit: the CLI over the overlay edit library
description:
A CLI over the edit library so people get the same placement, comment
handling, checks and refusals the agent gets -- e.g.

    dportsv3 dsl edit add-op ports/dns/dnsmasq --comment "..." 'mk eval CFLAGS "..."'

Prints the line diff and the per-build-line plan diff; exits non-zero on a
refusal with the reason. Also the cheapest way to try the library on real
overlays before the agent depends on it.

Depends on the library.

title: overlay edit library: commands, placement, comment ownership, post-edit plan check
description:
The library the parent describes: line splicing by parser span, the commands
(create_overlay, add_op, remove_op, replace_op, set_header), the placement
rule, comment ownership, the post-edit re-plan check, and refusals with a
reason.

GATES.

  - Round trip: load and save every one of the 5087 overlays with no edit;
    byte-identical.
  - Replay: express each of the 183 merged agent overlay.dops changes as
    commands, apply them to the overlay as it was before that commit, and
    compare plans with the delivered overlay on every target. Same plan for
    all 183. Placement may differ from where the agent put a line (dns/dnsmasq
    put its op before an independent heredoc; the rule puts it after); the
    plan may not.

Depends on the span fix and the emit.py gaps.
notes:
2026-10-04 (poly-7pwa round 2). The post-edit per-build-line check is
dportsv3/build_lines.diff_build_lines (contract in poly-7pwa.8 CHANGE 1):
diff_build_lines(before, dataclasses.replace(before, dops=edited_text)), then
compare each line's added and removed op identities with the command and check
that untouched ops keep their relative order. Related to poly-7pwa.8, not
blocked by it: if .8 has not landed, build .8's CHANGE 1 here (the
engine/models.py helpers file_effect, first_later_touch and op_identity,
dportsv3/build_lines.py and tests/test_build_lines.py) and nothing else from
.8; .8's report classes and its ONLY LOST OPS rule are agent-side, not part of
the contract. A line view drops a file materialize that a later whole write on
the same line replaces without reading it first, so an op that lands nowhere
on a line is absent from that line's added set. The plan check also gets
E_SEM_DEAD_OP from the semantic layer (poly-7pwa.3): placement must never put
a second writer into the existing op's own block. If the editor writes target
lines, a repeated selector is E_SEM_INVALID_TARGET_SCOPE (the poly-7pwa
repeated-selector bead).

title: emit.py cannot render everything the parser accepts: no target, text or patch builders, no heredoc tag, and it quotes @ paths
description:
emit.py is the serializer every programmatic producer uses, but it cannot
render everything the parser accepts. The editor writes new lines through it,
so these gaps become the editor's.

GAPS.

  - no builder for `target` lines (only inside header()), for the three text
    ops, or for `patch apply` -- 857 statements in the tree;
  - mk_set cannot take on-missing (8 statements use it);
  - the heredoc tag cannot be passed in: emit always writes MK, while 906
    heredocs in the tree use another tag (MK1 in every sample checked);
  - `_SAFE_PATH` (emit.py:27) excludes `@`, so emit quotes every scoped
    payload path, while all 31 in the tree are written bare.

GATE. Re-render every statement of all 5087 overlays and compare with its
source text. Today 137 overlays differ, and those differences are recorded,
not rewritten:

    102  bare vs quoted (201 bare `mk add` tokens; the 31 scoped paths)
     26  text ops continued over several lines with `\`
     25  a literal tab inside a quoted string
      2  spacing
      2  the heredoc span bug (sibling bead)

Decide bare-vs-quoted so emit matches what the tree already writes.

title: a heredoc that ends a file without a final newline has a span one line short, leaving its closing tag outside
description:
A heredoc op that ends a file with no final newline gets a span one line
short: the closing tag line is outside it.

    port a/b / type port / reason "x" / target @any
    mk target set foo <<'MK'
    	echo hi
    MK

    with a final newline:   span lines 5-7   (closing tag is line 7)
    without one:            span lines 5-6

Two overlays have that shape today: graphics/vulkan-loader and www/w3m.

Nothing edits by span yet, so nothing is affected. The overlay editor will:
replacing or removing such an op by its span would leave a stray `MK` line
and a broken file.

VERIFY. Both forms report the closing tag's line as line_end; the two real
overlays' last statements end on their tag line.
notes:
2026-10-04 (poly-7pwa): the one-line-short heredoc span also shortens the
'lines S-E' range of poly-7pwa.3's E_SEM_DEAD_OP message by one line, for a
heredoc op that ends the file.

title: overlay editor: callers say what to change in overlay.dops, the tool decides where it goes
description:
Agents change overlay.dops by hand: read it, `edit_file` the text, then
validate_dops (dportsv3/agent/prompts.py:301). The DSL is positional -- a
`target` line applies until the next one -- and scope, not file position,
decides which op wins. Much of poly-7pwa (.1, .2, .3, .11, .13) compensated
for that with prose and after-the-fact checks. This epic moves the mechanics
into a tool: callers say what to change, the tool decides where it goes.

SURVEY, 2026-10-01 (go.mod / go mod edit, buildozer, meson rewrite,
cargo add / toml_edit, portfmt, debmutate / lintian-brush, Homebrew
bump-formula-pr, nix-update, Renovate, hclwrite, tomlkit, ruamel.yaml / kyaml,
LibCST / rowan, recast). The ones that work agree:

  - commands name WHAT changes, never where; placement is the tool's, by a
    declared rule (after the last item of the same kind; sorted if already
    sorted; explicit anchor);
  - the result is re-parsed and checked (Renovate re-extracts, debmutate
    demands a byte-identical round trip, Homebrew audits and reverts);
  - when unsure they refuse and say why, rather than guess;
  - who owns a comment is decided explicitly -- most of their bugs are a
    comment that moved with, or was left behind by, an edited neighbour;
  - whole-file reprinting is tolerated only where a formatter is house style
    (Go, Bazel). A line-oriented DSL fits line splicing.

MEASURED.

  - 4950 of 5087 overlays: every statement already renders identically under
    emit.py's rules (keeping the file's heredoc tag). 67 carry comment lines.
  - Merged agent fixes: 196 commits, 183 overlay.dops changes. 80 new
    overlays; ops added in 140, removed in 58, modified in place in 11;
    comments changed in 31, header in 4; zero reorders, zero moves between
    scopes. 148 of 183 are pure op add/remove/modify; the rest are exactly
    the comment and header changes. All 291 added ops went into @any.
  - Where the 116 ops added to existing overlays went: 40 end of block, 41
    next to ops of the same kind, 21 elsewhere mid-block, 14 before a later
    op on the same file or variable (order may matter; an upper bound).
  - Agents write a "why" comment block directly above the op they add.

SHAPE. One library, two front ends (a CLI for people, tools for the agent).

  - Splice whole lines located by the parser's spans. Untouched lines stay
    byte-identical; new lines come from emit.py.
  - Commands: create_overlay, add_op(op, scope, comment, before/after),
    remove_op, replace_op, set_header.
  - Placement: after the last op of the same kind in the block whose scope
    matches exactly; else at the end of that block; else a new `target`
    block at end of file. A comma-list block is not a match for one target.
    Existing lines are never reordered.
  - A comment block directly above an op belongs to that op; above a
    `target` line, to the target. "End of block" is after its last op and
    before the comments leading into the next `target`.
  - After every edit, re-plan every build line and refuse unless only the
    intended ops changed. Return that per-line diff -- it is poly-7pwa.8's
    first tier.
  - Ambiguity (same target in several blocks, a heredoc it cannot place)
    is a refusal with a reason.

If the folder-install epic lands first, payload ops drop out of this one.

Designed during the poly-7pwa.3 review.

title: a materialized file is invisible to later ops in the same apply, so a text edit on it edits the upstream file and the overlay's file is silently discarded
description:
A file that `file materialize` wrote is invisible to every later op in the
same apply. A text op on it edits the upstream file from disk instead, and its
write replaces the materialized one: the overlay's file is silently gone and
the apply reports ok.

MEASURED on master 6b04280 (apply_dsl, target @main; the port already ships
files/x containing UPSTREAM; dragonfly/a contains AAA):

    target @any
    file materialize dragonfly/a -> files/x
    text replace-once file files/x from "UPSTREAM" to "EDITED"

    -> ok=True, files/x = "EDITED"     (AAA never reaches the tree)

Same first op, other followers:

    text replace-once ... from "AAA" to ...   failed: pattern not found (it read the disk copy)
    file copy files/x -> files/y, no upstream failed: E_APPLY_MISSING_SUBJECT
    file remove files/x, no upstream          failed: E_APPLY_MISSING_SUBJECT
    file remove files/x, upstream present     applied (removes it)

CAUSE. FileTransaction stages materialize writes as bytes (`_writes_bytes`,
fsops.py:53 -- byte staging exists so non-UTF-8 payloads survive). read_text
(fsops.py:41) consults `_writes` and `_removes` only, then reads the disk.
exec_file_remove checks `target.exists()` on disk (file_text_patch.py:118).
So for every later op a byte-staged file does not exist; and a text op's
stage_write pops the pending byte write (fsops.py:50), which is the silent
case. Present since the initial import (3414779).

REACH TODAY. Zero. No overlay among 5087 has an op that edits, copies or
removes a path an earlier op materialized. The scan was checked against a
positive control that catches all three shapes. Latent, not live -- but it is
exactly this epic's class: an op that does nothing and reports success.

FIX. read_text falls through to staged bytes, decoded the way the disk read
would decode them (a non-UTF-8 payload then fails the same way it does from
disk); file remove consults staged writes before the disk. About ten lines in
fsops.py and file_text_patch.py. No tool, prompt or agent surface changes.

VERIFY. The five shapes above become: edit applies to AAA; copy copies AAA;
remove removes the staged file in both cases. Full suite.

Found while reviewing poly-7pwa.3. poly-7pwa.20's premise ("remove is
last-wins against materialize") rests on this behaviour and is half true
until it is fixed.
close_reason: Fixed in 0af69f8: read_text falls through to staged bytes (decoded as a disk read would), FileTransaction.exists gives file remove the same view. 7 tests in tests/test_materialized_file_is_visible.py; fail without the fix. Suite 4451 passed, 1 skipped, 2 failed (the known 127.0.0.1:8080 tracker CLI tests).

title: the suite is order-dependent: pytest-randomly gives 17 failures on one run and 5 on the next
description:
Observed by a reviewer during poly-7pwa.12's review, across
tests/test_slave_port_patch_origin.py, tests/test_tail_follows_the_build.py and
tests/test_worker_edit_file.py. With pytest-randomly active: 17 failures on one
run, 5 on the next; deterministic order (-p no:randomly) is stable.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: it makes 'the suite is green' unverifiable, which is the one
claim every bead in poly-7pwa leans on. Every fix in that epic was verified by
breaking it and re-running -- that discipline is worth much less if the baseline
moves on its own.

LIKELY CAUSE, worth checking first: module-level mutable state in the agent
package. worker._TARGET_CACHE is a module global written by set_env_target and
read by peek_env_target, and several test files set it without popping (a teardown
writing None leaves an entry). worker also carries _WRKSRC_CACHE,
_MATERIALIZE_STATE and the port-relation cache. Any test that leaves one populated
changes what a later test sees.

worker.reset_attempt_caches() already exists for the runtime equivalent; a fixture
that calls it, or an autouse fixture that snapshots and restores the module
globals, may be most of the fix.

NOT introduced by this epic's work as far as the observation goes -- the named
files are pre-existing -- but this epic added several tests that write
_TARGET_CACHE, so it is worth confirming they are not contributors before blaming
older code.

title: no playbook declares flows:[convert], so the flow that authored the one live @any PORTREVISION op cannot read any of this guidance
description:
playbooks.py hard-rejects any playbook whose flows list omits the job's role, and
every file in dportsv3/agent/playbooks/ declares [patch] or [triage, patch].
convert is a real job type (runner.py). So none of the scoping, ordering or
payload-lane guidance this epic has written reaches the convert flow.

NOT HYPOTHETICAL. graphics/gdal's overlay header says 'auto-converted from compat
(Makefile.DragonFly + dragonfly/)' and it carries the single live @any
'mk set PORTREVISION 3' op in the tree -- the one poly-7pwa.12 is about. The flow
that wrote it is the flow that will never see .12's correction.

This is poly-7pwa.11's lesson repeating a third time: guidance landed where the
model reading it was not the one that needed it. .11 was a tool description in
context every turn; this is a whole flow with no guidance at all.

FIX SHAPE, either: give convert its own playbook (or add 'convert' to the flows
list of the ones that already apply -- flow-patch.md's scoping, ordering and
payload-lane sections are all relevant to authoring a fresh overlay), or put the
minimum rule where convert authoring reads it. The first is probably right: an
overlay written from nothing is exactly when scope decisions are made.

Check the same question for triage while there: which playbooks does it actually
receive, and is any of this epic's guidance among them.
design:
CLOSED AS PREMISE-REFUTED, 2026-10-04. Both legs are false.
- convert is not a job type. The runner dispatches patch, triage, verify
  and confirm (master runner.py:4822, :4854, :4862, :5034); anything else
  ends as "unknown job type" (:5190). The convert agent was retired in
  Step 48 (runner.py:3806). Nothing enqueues a convert job, and
  process_convert_job is defined nowhere since the polytropos import
  (3414779).
- graphics/gdal's @any mk set PORTREVISION "3" came from the patch flow:
  DeltaPorts 2112942abbe (2026-09-16, "graphics/gdal: fix build failure
  on DragonFly"). The "auto-converted from compat" header came from the
  deterministic Step 48 mass-convert fef107ea6d5 (2026-06-09), whose gdal
  output had no PORTREVISION. The patch flow reads flow-patch.md, where
  221c4eb (poly-7pwa.12, .21 row 6) corrects the PORTREVISION advice.
- Triage: it runs with classification None (runner.py:2501), so no

title: operator context is not keyed on the job's run, so an older run's row promotes MANUAL, and pardons the patch cap when newer than the last failed attempt, on guidance the prompt never carries
description:
PRE-EXISTING, found by the adversarial review of poly-7pwa.10 and deliberately
left out of that fix: the same flag, on a different axis.

PortHistory.load's user-context lookup (agent/decision.py) has no time window and
no run bound. failed_patch_attempts, in the same method, is cut off at `cutoff`
(window_hours). The context query is not, and it does not restrict to the job's
own run.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both verified by the reviewer against the real code:

1. A context row 400 DAYS OLD sets has_fresh_user_context as soon as the last
   patch failure falls out of the window -- because with failed_patch_attempts
   back to 0, `if not last_failed_patch_at: has_fresh_user_context = True`
   short-circuits. So the MANUAL->ASSIST promotion and the patch-cap pardon come
   back for free at every window rollover, forever, for that origin+target.

2. A context row from a DIFFERENT, OLDER RUN on the same target sets the flag for
   today's run -- while the text the agent then reads,
   runner.get_user_context(run_id, origin), is keyed on the CURRENT run and
   returns None. The promotion fires and the prompt's "## User Context" section
   is empty. A patch attempt is launched on the strength of guidance the prompt
   never contains.

(2) is poly-7pwa.10's own framing -- "a decision made on the wrong evidence,
which is why nothing downstream looks wrong" -- on the run/time axis instead of
the target axis. Target turned out to be a proxy for run: the tight scope is
`uc.run_id = <the job's run_id>`, which load() is not currently passed.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY rather than folded into .10: .10's fix is a narrowing
that cannot make the flag fire where it did not before, so it is safe to land on
its own. This one changes WHEN the flag fires in the single-target case that runs
in production today, which is a behaviour change for everyone and wants its own
decision about the window. It is also arguably the larger of the two.

FIX SHAPE, and the choice is real: either pass the job's run_id into load() and
scope the lookup to it -- tightest, and it makes (2) impossible by construction
-- or add `AND uc.updated_at >= ?` with the same cutoff as the sibling query,
which fixes (1) and only narrows (2). The first is better; the second is smaller.
Whichever lands, the empty-User-Context-section case in (2) deserves its own
assertion, because that is the one an operator would never diagnose from the
outside.

RELATED, same method, same review: every block in load() ends in
`except sqlite3.Error: pass`, so a real schema fault silently suppresses
promotions with nothing in the activity log. A first-failure log line would be
cheap. Out of scope here; noting it so it is not lost.

WHY THE RUN KEY LOSES NO LEGITIMATE PROMOTION. What a run is:
  - hook_run_start mints run-<PROFILE>-<UTC time>-<pid> once per dsynth
    invocation that runs hooks; per-port hooks read it back
    (dev-env/dports_dev_env/dsynth-hooks/hook_common.sh:133-140).
  - Attempts never mint one: agent and verify builds create
    /work/.dports-agent-hooks-disabled and the hooks exit
    (hook_common.sh:15-58).
  - One run is one profile, so one env and one target: runs.target, the
    bundle's target and the job file's target= all come from the hook's
    one DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET (hook_common.sh:263, :411-417).
  - Triage jobs carry the bundle's run (hook_common.sh:267), the context
    row's run for a retry (process_user_context_updates,
    runner.py:1890-1945, run_id written at :1102), or bundles.run_id for
    a job claimed from the DB (runner.py:2738). Patch jobs copy the
    triage job's (runner.py:2978).
  - The tracker's two writers key context on a run that a bundle or a
    manual request already names: the retry route
    (dportsv3/tracker/routes/bundle_actions.py:1110, :1138) and the
    manual-queue submit (dportsv3/tracker/routes/pages.py:1751-1777,
    gated on a user_context_requests row the escalating triage wrote
    with its own run, steps.py:778-787). /v1/user-context
    (dportsv3/tracker/routes/ingest_api.py:137-152) takes the caller's
    run_id unchecked and has no in-tree caller; it writes no request
    row, so on its own it never enqueues a retry. In every case the
    prompt reads the same (run_id, origin) key.
  So "context written against run N, retry in run N+1" does not happen. A
  failure in run N+1 is a new job whose prompt cannot carry run N's
  text; promoting it is the defect.

WHY NO TIME WINDOW AND NO TARGET PREDICATE. Measured over nine
scenarios (method as in PREMISE). Each cell is "flag / the patch prompt
carries the context":

    scenario                        master  +.10  run key  2h window
    (2)  other run, older           T/F     T/F   F/F      F/F
    (2b) other run, after failure   T/F     T/F   F/F      T/F
    (1)  400 days old               T/F     T/F   F/F      F/F
    delayed retry, same run, 3h     T/T     T/T   T/T      F/T
    retry, same run                 T/T     T/T   T/T      T/T
    legacy run, job target @main    T/T     F/T   T/T      F/T
    legacy run, job target ''       T/T     T/T   T/T      T/T
    legacy run's row, later run     T/F     F/F   F/F      F/F
    blocked retry (OUT OF SCOPE)    F/T     F/T   F/T      F/T

  ("+.10" is the post-carry tree; "2h window" is .10's query plus
  updated_at >= the attempt-window cutoff.)
  - The run key is the only variant where every T flag has the context
    in its prompt, and it keeps every promotion master makes with the
    context in the prompt.
  - A window on updated_at (runner.attempt_window_hours, default 2,
    dportsv3/settings.py:279) leaves (2b) promoting with no context,
    and drops a retry that waited longer than the window. Retries do
    wait: the enqueue is skipped while an active same-origin job exists
    on the context run's build line or with no target
    (_has_active_same_origin_job, runner.py:1862-1887, used at
    :1912-1921; QUEUED counts as active). poly-ov2b records about two
    hours for three rounds of one attempt, and poly-7pwa.14's hold keeps
    a job QUEUED until an env of its line is selected.
  - Run key plus window: the run key leaves only same-run rows, so the
    only rows a window adds to drop are same-run rows older than the
    window: delayed retries, and same-run triages of other flavors.
  - .10's target predicate on top of the run key: a run has one target,
    so it changes a result only when runs.target disagrees with the
    job's target for the job's own run, and there it suppresses a
    promotion whose prompt carries the context (legacy run, job target
    @main: F/T under .10, T/T under the run key).

PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, single target, as deployed. Only TriageStep
acts on the flag (steps.py:703 into decide): rule 2 promotes a MANUAL
tier to ASSIST (decision.py:341-359), rule 3 pardons the cap
(decision.py:390-400). Let L be the newest gave-up or budget-exhausted
patch job for (origin, target) inside the window (decision.py:114-133;
unchanged).
  - BEFORE (post-carry tree): the flag is set when the newest context row
    for the origin, from a run whose target is the job's (or, for an
    untargeted job, a run with none), exists and either L does not exist
    or the row is newer than L.
  - AFTER: the flag is set when the job has a run_id, a row exists for
    (that run_id, origin), and either L does not exist or the row is
    newer than L.
  - What changes: a failure in a new dsynth run of a port the operator
    guided in an earlier run. A MANUAL classification used to become an
    attempt with no User Context section; now it escalates:
    manual_handoff.md and a new manual request for the new run
    (steps.py:751-810). A capped port with context newer than L in
    another run used to get another attempt; now it escalates
    (patch_cap, or sticky_signature).
  - Unchanged: the retry-with-context loop, however long it waited; the
    prompt text; failed_patch_attempts, recent_failures and the
    signature; hand-fired patch jobs; non-MANUAL decisions below the cap.
  - How often this happens in production: UNVERIFIED; no production
    state.db was reachable. Size it with MEASURE BEFORE LANDING.

MEASURE BEFORE LANDING. Optional, read-only, and it does not gate the
change (D6 decided it). On the builder, open the runner's state.db (the
file the paths.state_db setting names; default
/build/synth/logs/evidence/state.db) with "sqlite3 -readonly" and run:

    SELECT a.ts, j.origin, b.run_id,
           json_extract(a.extra_json, '$.promoted_via'),
           json_extract(a.extra_json, '$.cap_reset_via')
      FROM activity_log a
      JOIN jobs j ON j.job_id = a.job_id
      JOIN bundles b ON b.bundle_id = j.bundle_id
     WHERE a.stage = 'decision'
       AND 'user_context' IN (json_extract(a.extra_json, '$.promoted_via'),
                              json_extract(a.extra_json, '$.cap_reset_via'))
       AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_context uc
                        WHERE uc.run_id = b.run_id
                          AND uc.origin = j.origin)
     ORDER BY a.ts;

    SELECT COUNT(*), MIN(ts) FROM activity_log WHERE stage = 'decision';

  Each row of the first query is a decision this bead would change: a
  promotion or a pardon for a job whose own run has no context row for
  the origin. The second gives the span the sample covers. It is a lower
  bound: activity_log keeps only the newest runner.activity_log_max rows
  of all stages (default 5000, runner.py:2004), and a decision whose own
  run also holds an older, stale row is not counted. Verified against
  rows TriageStep itself wrote (process_job on a scratch tree): before
  the change it returns the run-2 promotion and nothing for the same-run
  retry; after it, nothing. Record the counts in this bead's notes.

EDGE CASES.
  - No run_id on the job: False. Only hand-written job files lack one;
    the hook falls back to run-<PROFILE>-unknown (hook_common.sh:139).
  - Context in the job's run, older than L: False (unchanged rule).
  - Context in the job's run, L absent: True whatever its age. Reached
    by a retry of that run, its transient requeue (the same job file),
    or another triage of the same origin in the same run, such as a
    second flavor's first failure after the operator answered the first
    flavor's request. Context is keyed (run_id, origin), not by flavor
    or bundle, so each of those prompts carries it (measured: flag and
    prompt both True).
  - A run with no recorded target: counts for its own run's jobs;
    runs.target is never read.
  - run-<PROFILE>-unknown is shared by every run of a profile whose hook
    cannot read .current_run. Context written against it applies to that
    profile's later failures, but the prompt carries it too, so flag and
    prompt still agree.
  - A failed jobs query still makes any row of the job's run fresh; now
    only in the run whose prompt carries it. The logging bead reports it.

  Helpers, verbatim:

    def _ago(**kw) -> str:
        return (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(**kw)).isoformat()

    def _plant_run(conn, run_id: str, target: str | None = "@test"):
        conn.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO runs (run_id, profile, target) "
                     "VALUES (?, 'test', ?)", (run_id, target))
        conn.commit()

    def _plant_context(conn, run_id: str, when: str, origin="foo/bar",
                       text="link against the system zstd"):
        _plant_run(conn, run_id)
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO user_context (run_id, origin, "
                     "context_text, updated_at, context_rev) "
                     "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 1)", (run_id, origin, text, when))
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO user_context_history (run_id, origin, "
                     "context_rev, submitted_at, text) "
                     "VALUES (?, ?, 1, ?, ?)", (run_id, origin, when, text))
        conn.commit()

    def _plant_gave_up_patch(conn, job_id: str, when: str):
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO jobs (job_id, origin, target, type, "
                     "state, retire_reason, last_transition_at) "
                     "VALUES (?, 'foo/bar', '@test', 'patch', 'dead', "
                     "'patch_gave_up', ?)", (job_id, when))
        conn.commit()

    def _triage_in_run(queue_env, tmp_path, monkeypatch, run_id: str,
                       classification: str = "missing-dep"):
        """missing-dep is MANUAL in the default policy. Returns (the
        patch job it enqueued, or None; the bundle dir)."""
        from dportsv3.agent import triage as triage_module
        monkeypatch.setattr(triage_module, "run",
                            lambda *a, **kw: _StubTriageResult(
                                classification=classification,
                                confidence="high"))
        queue_root = queue_env["queue_root"]
        bdir = _make_bundle_dir(tmp_path)
        job_path = _drop_synthetic_job(queue_env, bundle_dir=bdir,
                                       extra_fields={"run_id": run_id})
        inflight = queue_root / "inflight" / job_path.name
        job_path.rename(inflight)
        runner._apply_transition(job_path.name, lifecycle.JobEvent.CLAIM)
        runner.process_job(queue_root, inflight, [],
                           dry_run=False, playbooks_dir=None)
        pending = sorted((queue_root / "pending").glob("*-patch.job"))
        assert len(pending) <= 1
        if not pending:
            return None, bdir
        return runner.parse_job_file(pending[0]), bdir

    def _prompt_carries_context(patch_job, bdir) -> bool:
        payload = runner.build_patch_payload(bdir, None, patch_job)
        return "## User Context" in payload

title: operator context is looked up without a target filter, so guidance for one build line promotes and cap-resets jobs on another
description:
dportsv3/agent/decision.py, PortHistory.load(). Every history query in this
method is carefully target-scoped with the same idiom --

    AND (target = ? OR (? = '' AND (target IS NULL OR target = '')))

-- including failed_patch_attempts, immediately above (lines ~118-128). The
user-context query is not (lines 137-141):

    SELECT updated_at FROM user_context
     WHERE origin = ? ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1

No target filter and no run_id filter: it takes the most recent operator-context
row for the origin across every run and every target ever recorded. The
asymmetry between two adjacent queries in the same method is the tell that this
is an oversight rather than a decision.

THERE IS A TARGET DIMENSION TO IGNORE. user_context's primary key is
(run_id, origin) (db/schema.py:316-323) and runs carries target
(db/schema.py:27-34), so context left against a @2026Q3 run and context left
against a @main run are genuinely different rows. The query flattens them.

TWO EFFECTS, both policy decisions rather than display:

- MANUAL -> ASSIST PROMOTION (decision.py:317-325). A classification that
  resolves to MANUAL is promoted to auto_patch when fresh context exists. So
  operator guidance written for a @2026Q3 failure can silently launch an
  automatic patch attempt on @main for the same origin.
- PATCH CAP RESET (decision.py:366-374, extra "cap_reset_via": "user_context").
  This is the sharper one, because failed_patch_attempts IS target-scoped while
  the reset trigger is not: the count of failures is per-target, the thing that
  forgives them is global. One context submission on either build line grants
  another attempt on both.

WHY IT MATTERS UNDER THE ONE-TARGET-PER-ENV CONSTRAINT. Operator guidance is
frequently build-line specific -- for lang/rust and ports-mgmt/pkg the whole
reason those ports are target-scoped is that the upstream source differs between
versions, so advice about 2.8.4's configure.def is wrong for 2.7.5's auto.def.
Acting on it for the other target is not merely wasted budget; it is an attempt
launched on advice known to be inapplicable.

NOT AFFECTED, checked: the context TEXT the agent reads is fetched by
get_user_context (runner.py:989-999), which filters correctly on
(run_id, origin). So the prompt is not cross-contaminated -- only the
promote/cap-reset decision is. The agent therefore runs on correct context for
a decision that was made on the wrong evidence, which is why nothing downstream
looks wrong.

FOUND BY an independent adversarial audit of poly-7pwa's analysis, in a layer
the original pass did not look at (policy rather than compose/worker). Verified
directly: both queries read in place, schema confirmed, both effect sites read.

FIX SHAPE: give the user_context query the same target predicate as the
failed_patch_attempts query directly above it. Test surface:
tests/ has decision-policy tests; the fixture needs two runs on two targets for
one origin.

title: an attempt cannot show which build lines its overlay change reaches: diff each line's input closure after every attempt
description:
An attempt cannot show it left the other build lines alone. Two checks do that,
and only one of them is available where the agent runs.

An env has exactly one target (dev_env state.target -> DPORTS_TARGET ->
DPORTS_COMPOSE_ROOT=/work/artifacts/compose/<target>) and every agent tool is
bound to it: reapply is compose --target "$DPORTS_TARGET" --origin ...,
make_extract/make_patch/dupe/genpatch all work against that one compose root,
dsynth builds that tree. So a change to an @any op is a change to build lines
this job can never exercise.

WHY THE ORIGINAL FRAMING OF THIS BEAD DIED. Its title said compose is cheap
and its body said compose needs a freebsd-ports checkout already on the
matching branch. Both were written here and never reconciled; the title is
the wrong one. The code is unambiguous:

  * compose_stages.py:385 _check_freebsd_git_state HARD-GATES compose on the
    upstream checkout's branch matching target_branch
    (E_COMPOSE_FREEBSD_NOT_GIT / E_COMPOSE_GIT_BRANCH_CHECK_FAILED).
  * compose_stages.py:754 upstream_origin = freebsd_root / ctx.origin -- every
    port is seeded from that branch-matched tree.

A dev-env has one FREEBSD_DIR, on its own branch, and switching it would
corrupt the tree being built in. So composing a second target is not cheap
from inside a job -- it is UNAVAILABLE unless the host already carries the
other target's env. That is a precondition, not a cost.

THE FINDING THAT SPLITS THE PROBLEM. The engine is branch-free.
build_plan(text, source_path) is pure text -> plan, and
`grep -rn freebsd dportsv3/engine/` returns nothing. Upstream enters only at
apply_plan(..., port_root=...). Therefore:

    composed(T) = apply( plan_for(T), upstream_T )

plan_for(T) is computable for ANY target from the overlay text alone, with no
checkout of any branch. And an attempt writes neither upstream_T nor
lock-root. So for any target the job is not building, composed(T) changes if
and only if the attempt changed something inside the port's own input closure.

=== TIER 1: the input-closure diff. Always available, needs nothing. ===

Snapshot the closure before the attempt, diff it after, and evaluate
plan_for(T) for every other target the tree uses.

  INVARIANT: if the ordered op list for T is byte-identical and every file
  those ops read is byte-identical, T's composed output is unchanged.

That is a proof, not a heuristic, and it needs no upstream tree, no second
dev-env and no build. Use order_ops_for_target (engine/models.py, poly-7pwa.11)
so the ordering is the engine's, not a fourth copy of the scope rule.

THE CLOSURE, measured across 5087 planned overlays:

  * overlay.dops -- the text itself.
  * overlay.toml -- type and removed_in; removed_in alone disables the whole
    overlay for a target (poly-7pwa.6) and compose writes into this file
    itself (poly-7pwa.16), so it is both an input and mutable.
  * every file.materialize / file.copy `src`: 4473 ops, first path component
    `dragonfly` in 4473 of 4473 -- no exceptions in the tree.
  * every patch.apply subject: 117 ops, all under `diffs/`.
  * COMPAT MODE ONLY: the whole dragonfly/ and diffs/ trees, because
    compat_*_script_parity walks them recursively and a file with no op is
    still an input (poly-7pwa.9).

Everything else compose reads -- upstream, lock-root -- the agent cannot
write, so it is unchanged by construction.

Not in the closure: the `path`/`file` of a text or mk op (pkg-plist, Makefile,
distinfo, files/*). Those name the composed DESTINATION, not an overlay input.

WHAT TIER 1 PROVES, AND THE TWO THINGS IT DOES NOT.

  * It proves NO NEW cross-target damage. It says nothing about damage that
    was already there -- an op whose anchor is missing on the other branch was
    broken before the attempt and is equally broken after, and the diff is
    clean either way. That gap is exactly what Tier 2 covers.
  * It does not judge correctness. "You did not perturb @main" is not "@main
    is right". Nothing short of a build gives that, and we are not building.

THE NOISE PROBLEM, which decides whether this is usable. Only 2 of 5087
overlays carry a non-@any scope, so on the other 5085 every edit is an @any
edit and touches every build line unavoidably. Reporting that per attempt
would be pure noise, and "this port has one build line" is already in the
brief (poly-7pwa.5). The signal worth surfacing is narrower:

  * GREEN, and this is the valuable case: the fix was scoped, the other
    lines' op lists and inputs are byte-identical, so the attempt provably
    did not touch them. Nothing in the epic can currently say this.
  * FINDING: the attempt meant to make a scoped change and collaterally
    altered shared input. The live shape is a re-cut that lands on a flat @any
    source (poly-7pwa.2 decides that lane per file, and when it resolves to
    the flat op BOTH build lines change with nothing saying so), a deleted op
    scoped elsewhere, or an overwritten file another target's op reads.
  * SILENT on an all-@any port where there is no scoped alternative.

HOOK: poly-7pwa.1 already takes a baseline -- overlay_before =
_overlay_text(env, origin), in attempt_loop before the retry loop. Widen it
from one file to the closure above and Tier 1 is mostly plumbing that exists.
Report it the same way .1 does, into the next attempt's notes rather than
after the loop, for the same reason.

=== TIER 2: compose the other target. Conditional, catches what Tier 1 cannot. ===

This is the original bead and it stands, with its precondition promoted from
a caveat to a gate. Compose is file-level -- no distfiles, no compiler, no
dsynth -- and the single-origin incremental form runs in well under a second
(--origin requires an existing output tree, compose_stages.py:70):

  dportsv3 compose --target @main --origin <origin>
    --delta-root ... --freebsd-root <ON main> --lock-root ... --output <seeded>

WHAT IT CATCHES that Tier 1 cannot, given on-missing defaults to error
(apply_common.py:44): an @any text replace_once / line_insert_after whose
anchor is absent from the other branch's upstream (hard
E_APPLY_MISSING_SUBJECT); an @any mk replace-if whose condition string moved
between branches; a materialize source that is absent; and for lang/rust and
ports-mgmt/pkg the version-pinned distinfo and configure anchors that are the
whole reason those two are scoped.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CATCH -- carried forward from this bead's own audit
correction and still binding. mk.var.set INSERTS when the variable is absent
(engine/executors/mk_ops.py:172-200) and emits no missing-subject row;
likewise mk add. So Tier 2 covers replace-if / disable-if / unset / remove /
text ops / file remove / patch apply, and NOT mk set or mk add. That excludes
poly-7pwa.12 (PORTREVISION in @any), the most damaging cross-target case
known. Do not advertise this check as covering it. Also measured: 79 of 5087
overlays already carry on-missing relaxations and ports-mgmt/pkg's own @any
block uses both warn and noop, so the error default is weaker in practice
than the code suggests. And no live broken @any anchor exists today -- rust's
'${OPSYS} != FreeBSD' and pkg's jail.h anchors are present on both main and
2026Q3. Tier 2 is preventive; scope and sell it as such.

AVAILABILITY, cheapest first: (a) run it only when another env for the other
target exists on the host, and SAY SO when it does not -- a skipped check
that reports "skipped, no @main env here" is honest, a silent skip is the
current behaviour and the thing to avoid; (b) a second freebsd-ports git
worktree per target, cheap in space next to a buildbase; (c) never silently.

=== WHY BOTH ===

They catch disjoint classes. Tier 1 proves the attempt introduced nothing and
is always available; Tier 2 finds breakage that predates the attempt and is
available only sometimes. Neither judges correctness on a line we cannot
build. Ship Tier 1 first: it is unconditional, it is the stronger statement
where it applies, and it is the only thing in this epic that produces a proof
rather than a warning.

WHERE IT BELONGS. Tier 1 in the attempt loop, per attempt, feeding the next
attempt's prompt. Tier 2 at the end of a patch attempt alongside the existing
proof gate, and in the delivery path -- the bundle already carries its target,
and "composes clean on @2026Q3 as well" is a fact a reviewer cannot otherwise
obtain.

RELATED: poly-7pwa.1 is not this. An op filtered out of its OWN target's plan
is a same-target problem. This bead is the other direction -- an attempt
reaching build lines it was not written for.
design:

GOAL. After every patch attempt, compare what each build line composes
from ports/<origin>/ before and after the attempt, from the overlay text
and files alone: no upstream tree, no second env, no build. The agent is
told only when part of its change misses the line it is building
(MISSED). The operator is told, in patch_audit.json, the activity log and
proposed_fix.md, when the change stayed on this line (GREEN), changed
other lines unlike this one (FINDING) or missed. One mechanism: this
replaces scope_check.scope_drift (.1, carried as row 4/4a) and its SCOPE
note.

   - overlay.dops does not plan: unplannable.

     drop the file.materialize at index i when (1) its src normalises to a
     path inside the overlay dir that is present in files, (2) its dst
     normalises to a path inside the port, and (3) first_later_touch
     returns a j whose write is "replace" and whose reads do not contain
     the dst (a file copy of the dst onto itself reads it first, so it
     does not shadow; 0 copy ops exist today). Only materialize ops are
     dropped and only a later materialize or copy drops them: a present
     src cannot fail and a whole replace does not depend on the file's
     earlier state, while a remove's success, a copy's source and a text
     op's anchor depend on upstream. Measured: letting a later remove
     shadow, or dropping a materialize whose src is missing, each makes
     one soundness row unsound. ops = OpRef of the rest. inputs = for each
     kept file.materialize src and patch.apply path, the normalised
     relpath inside the dir mapped to files.get(rel, "missing"), or
     (raw, "invalid") when absolute or escaping; plus, for type dport,
     every file and dir under newport/.

CHANGE 2, THE REPORT. New module dportsv3/agent/build_line_report.py:

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class BuildLineReport:
        origin: str
        target: str            # C, the job's line
        cls: str               # none | missed | green | silent | finding
                               #   | unavailable
        changed: tuple = ()    # lines whose key changed
        affected: tuple = ()   # finding: lines that changed unlike C
        detail: tuple = ()     # (line, tuple of items) per changed line
        missed: tuple = ()     # missed: the items that do not reach C
        unavailable: str = ""
        def note(self, *, prefix: str = "", limit: int = 500) -> str
        def summary(self) -> str
        def message(self) -> str
        def to_dict(self) -> dict

    def build_line_report(diff: BuildLinesDiff, target: str, *,
                          origin: str) -> BuildLineReport

   Classes, C being the job's target (worker.peek_env_target(env)),
   decided in this order:

    unavailable  diff.unavailable is set
    none         no line changed
    finding      C's key did not change, and every other changed line
                 only lost ops (ONLY LOST OPS below): an op moved into
                 C's block, or deleted from another line's block. Those
                 lines are the affected ones.
    missed       (a) C's key did not change and another line's did in
                 any other way; or
                 (b) C changed, no op was added on C, and an op was added
                 on another line. (b) is scope_drift's rule, kept so that
                 an op stranded in another block is still reported when a
                 payload edit in the same attempt did reach C.
    green        only C changed
    silent       every other changed line has the same
                 (before.body(), after.body()) as C, and its own
                 listed_removed did not flip
    finding      C changed and at least one other line changed
                 differently; those lines are the affected ones

   ONLY LOST OPS, a private helper _only_lost_ops(d: LineDiff) -> bool in
   build_line_report.py, true when all of these hold:
   - d.added is empty and d.removed is not;
   - before's op identities with d.removed taken out (one occurrence
     each) equal after's, in order (the kept ops keep their order);
   - set(d.after.inputs) <= set(d.before.inputs): an input may go with
     its op, none is added or changed;
   - state, plan_type, bad and listed_removed are equal before and after.
   Why: moving a port's LAST @any op into a new target C block leaves
   C's view unchanged (identity excludes scope, C's apply order is the
   same), so rule (a) alone calls it missed and the note tells the agent
   to put the op under target C, where it already is. Requiring equal
   inputs instead of a subset is not enough: a moved file materialize
   also takes its src out of the unnamed lines' inputs.

   Missed items: for (a), the items of every changed line, lines with
   identical items grouped and named once ("@main and other lines:
   <item>; <item>"; no line prefix when one line changed); for (b),
   "added <label>" once for each op added on another line. A rule keyed
   on line names is wrong: moving an all-@any port's op into a new target
   block must be a finding whether it changes C's apply order (any op
   but the last) or nothing on C (the last op), while the unnamed lines
   lose it (measured on a gdal-shaped fixture).

   note() is the only text the agent sees, and only for missed; every
   other class returns "". Exact text, one paragraph with single spaces,
   remedy first:

    {prefix}BUILD LINES: part of this attempt's overlay change misses {C},
    the only build line this env builds. An op belongs to the last target
    line above it, and {C} reads a payload only if its last op for that
    file names it. Check with get_effective_overlay, then put the op under
    target @any (or target {C}) or edit the file it shows. Missed:
    {ITEMS}.

   The fixed text is 348 characters for @2026Q3 and 342 for @main. ITEMS
   joins items with "; ", adding items while the whole note stays at or
   under limit, then "; and N more"; when no item fits, "N changes".
   ITEMS counts individual items: a group's line prefix ("@main and
   other lines: ") is part of its first item, and N counts items, not
   groups. prefix is "ports/<o>: " only when the job has more than one
   origin.

   summary(), one line for proposed_fix.md; "" for the other classes:
    green    only {C} changes; every other build line reads byte-identical
             inputs from ports/{origin}/
    finding  also changes what composes on {AFFECTED}, which this env did
             not build
    missed   part of the overlay change does not reach {C}; it changes
             {CHANGED}
   AFFECTED and CHANGED: named lines joined with ", ", then OTHER_LINES
   written "every build line this overlay does not name", joined with
   " and ". message(): the operator's uncapped form: summary(), then for
   each changed line "<line_name>: <items joined with '; '>", all joined
   with ". "; "" for none and silent; "build lines not compared:
   <unavailable>" for unavailable. to_dict(): {"class", "target",
   "changed", "affected", "detail" (line name -> items), "summary",
   "message", "unavailable"}, every line written with line_name, so
   OTHER_LINES is "other lines".

EDGE CASES.

- Overlay unplannable before or after: unavailable, no note; validate_dops

- No overlay at baseline: the view moves from none or compat to dops on
  every line; no special case.
- Slave jobs: invariant_origins gives [origin, patch_origin]; each origin
  is reported on its own, with the prefix.
- Comment or blank-line edits, block reordering: none.
- A file under dragonfly/@T/ that no op reads: none today; an input on T
  once poly-u9n4.2 makes the folder the install.
- The agent writes removed_in C itself: C's key changes, the class is
  green or finding, and the operator item reads "overlay.toml removed_in
  now lists this line". Under poly-7pwa.6 compose ignores such a marker
  while the port exists upstream on C, which it does for any job that
  builds there, so no note.
- Single-line ports: an @any edit is silent; an override added in a new
  target C block, the @any op kept, is green; an @any op moved into a
  new target C block is a finding (operator only), the last op too; a
  per-line split (a C value and another line's) is a finding; an op
  written into another line's block is missed.
- An op deleted from another line's block (C unchanged): finding, no
  note. It is cross-line damage the operator must see; the agent's
  remedy text would not fit it.

OUT OF SCOPE.
- Composing another line: the deferred Tier 2 bead.
- Gating on any class. @any is the default for new work (S5),
  and a shared change on rust or pkg is often intended. Report only.
- A note for finding: the change reached this line, so a note saves no
  attempt, and its only remedy would ask the agent whether other lines
  need the change, which it cannot measure (S5).
- Writes outside ports/ of the origin set (special/, other ports).
- The delivery PR body and manual_handoff.md.

RISKS.
- line_view restates compose's read rule. A compose change that reads a
  new overlay input must change line_view in the same commit, or GREEN
  becomes a false proof. poly-u9n4.2 is the known one;
  test_an_unchanged_view_means_an_unchanged_compose is the guard.
- C is the scope cache, worker.peek_env_target(env). On the post-carry
  tree process_patch_job sets it to the job's target (runner.py:4687,
  set_env_target(env, job.get("target"))). From poly-7pwa.14 on, it is
  the line the env composes, read from its env.json, or the job's
  target only when the env's state cannot be read, and .14's job-start
  check refuses a job whose line differs; so "the only build line this
  env builds" in the note holds by enforcement.
- Conservative: an op moved between the @any and target phases reports
  "apply order changed" even when nothing interacts with it, and a compat
  edit compose ignores reports a change. Noise is safe; a miss is not.

title: a removed-for-target port is reported as stale and in compat mode, so the only record of the skip misdirects twice
description:
The per-port compose report cannot distinguish "this overlay is deliberately
removed for this target" from "this port context is stale", and reports the
wrong mode for the former. Both observed in one real report.

MEASURED. devel/plasma (overlay.dops present, 2 ops, removed_in ["@main"])
composed for @main:

  "mode": "compat",
  "mode_reason": "legacy-overlay",
  "notes": ["removed-for-target", "stale-skipped", "stale-skipped"],
  "warnings": 0, "errors": 0

TWO DEFECTS.

WRONG MODE. compose_stages.py:549-552 sets removed_for_target and `continue`s
BEFORE _record_preflight_mode_notes runs, so mode is never resolved and keeps
its default. A dops port with a valid overlay is reported as compat /
legacy-overlay. An operator auditing conversion progress from these reports
counts it on the wrong side of the migration, and 1093 ports carry removed_in.

COLLAPSED NOTE. The apply stages (686-689, 828-831) both note "stale-skipped"
for a removed-for-target port, because the guard is
`is_stale_port_context(ctx) or ctx.removed_for_target` and the note is written
from the combined condition. The preflight note "removed-for-target" is
correct and present, so the report contradicts itself twice over in the same
list. Two skipped stages produce two identical wrong notes.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. This report is the only place the
skip is visible at all -- compose exits 0 with zero warnings (poly-7pwa.6).
Anyone diagnosing "my overlay does nothing on @main" reads this, and what it
says is that the port is stale and in compat mode, neither of which is true.
The one note that would explain it is buried between two that misdirect.

FIX SHAPE: resolve mode before the removed_in check, or record it on the
context regardless; and give the apply stages a distinct note per cause rather
than one note for a disjunction. Cheap, and it is the diagnostic surface
poly-7pwa.6's fix will want to build on.

title: the job brief never states which build line the agent is fixing, so it has no reason to ask whether a fix is target-specific
description:
The job's compose target reaches the model almost only as a path component.
context.py:534-542 uses job["target"] to build the literal compose root it
tells the agent to read files under:

    /work/artifacts/compose/<target>/<origin>/files/ and .../dragonfly/

and prompts.py mentions the same path shape (lines 187-190). Nowhere does the
brief say "this job is for build line @main", and nowhere does it say that
which build line it is can change what the fix should look like.

WHY THAT IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. The other children in this epic are
mechanisms -- a destination, a scope, a diagnostic, a playbook section. This
one is whether the agent ever forms the thought. A model that is not told it
is working one of several build lines has no reason to ask whether its fix
belongs to all of them, and will write the shape the playbook shows, which is
flat and unscoped (poly-7pwa.4).

WHAT EXISTS ALREADY, so this is wiring rather than new machinery:
- runner.py:4687 calls worker.set_env_target(env, job["target"]) at attempt
  start, and worker.peek_env_target(env) reads it back
- get_effective_overlay returns {"target": ..., "effective_ops": [...],
  "filtered_out": [...]} with a per-op reason for each exclusion
- delivery and issue identity are already keyed by target (the bundle digest
  is sha256(target NUL origin NUL fingerprint)), so the target is a first-class
  fact everywhere except in what the model is told

WHAT TO ADD, roughly: name the target in the brief as a fact, and where the
port's overlay carries ops for other targets, say so -- "this port's overlay
also carries ops scoped to @2026Q3; a fix that is specific to this build line
belongs in the @main block". The second half only matters for ports that are
actually multi-target, which build_plan can answer cheaply from the overlay
the brief is already assembling context about.

SIZED SEPARATELY FROM .4 on purpose: .4 is guidance the agent reads when it
goes looking, this is a fact it is handed whether it looks or not. Doing only
.4 leaves the agent correct-if-prompted; doing only this leaves it aware with
nowhere to put the file.

title: a shared dragonfly/ patch that stops applying on one build line has no rule for which line changes what
description:
`grep -rn 'dragonfly/@' dportsv3/agent/playbooks/ dportsv3/agent/dops_quickref.md`
returns nothing. The convention DeltaPorts now uses in ports-mgmt/pkg and
lang/rust is absent from every document the patch agent reads.

Two halves, and the second is worse than the first.

ABSENT MECHANISM. flow-patch.md's "Creating a static source patch
(dragonfly/*)" section (line ~191) says: stage it with `file materialize
dragonfly/X -> dragonfly/X`. That is the only form given, in the playbook and
in dops_quickref.md's op reference (lines 127, 204-205, 240, 269). The scoped
form `file materialize dragonfly/@<target>/X -> dragonfly/X` -- source scoped,
destination flat -- appears nowhere, so an agent that correctly concludes "this
fix cannot be shared between build lines" has no mechanism to reach for and
will write a flat patch under a scoped block.

WRONG STEER. flow-patch.md:163-189 then argues against scoping:

  "Most fixes are universal. DragonFly-vs-FreeBSD differences are
   platform-level -- they apply regardless of which quarterly snapshot
   you're on. Keep them in the @any scope. Scoping a universal fix to one
   build line over-restricts it: the same failure re-surfaces next quarter."

Sound for framework and platform differences, and the opposite of what these
two ports need. DeltaPorts commit c030e103838 states the case for pkg: 2.8.4
renamed auto.def to configure.def and rewrote it from Tcl to shell, so one
patch cannot cover both versions. lang/rust's own overlay states it for rust:
"none of the fourteen patches common to both sets is identical across 1.96.1
and 1.98.1." A source patch against a versioned distfile is the DEFAULT case
for scoping, not the exception.

The section does have an escape hatch -- "upstream source that diverges
between quarterly snapshots so one patch can't cover both" -- but it names no
mechanism and sits under a heading that spends four paragraphs discouraging
its use. It also tells the agent to read its target from get_effective_overlay,
which is right and should be kept.

WHAT THE GUIDANCE NEEDS TO SAY, roughly:
- an op's scope is the last `target` block above it, so where the op goes in
  the file decides what it applies to (see poly-7pwa.1)
- a patch cut against upstream source in a versioned distfile is target-
  specific by default; a framework or platform fix is universal by default
- the mechanism: put the file under dragonfly/@<target>/, materialize it to
  the flat destination, and put the op under that target's block
- reading the current shape: get_effective_overlay returns filtered_out, which
  is how the agent sees that a sibling target already has its own copy of the
  file it is about to write
- PORTREVISION stays in @any (already correct in the playbook, keep it)

PRIOR ART IN THE TREE: ports-mgmt/pkg's overlay.dops carries a worked comment
explaining why dfly-patch is repeated verbatim in the @main block (a later `mk
target set` replaces the whole recipe, and @any ops run first regardless of
block order). lang/rust's carries one explaining why the cargo crate patches
stay flat while the rust source patches are scoped -- they pin crate versions,
not rust versions. Both are better explanations than anything currently in the
playbooks and should be mined rather than rewritten from scratch.

Test surface: tests/test_playbooks.py and
tests/test_playbook_patch_repair_guidance.py already assert on playbook
content.
design:
STATE, 2026-10-04. Open, not started. The 2026-09 attempt was reverted, and
its false-claim half moves to a new P2 bead ("the patch playbooks and
quickref state four things the engine does not do"). What remains is the
rule for a shared dragonfly/ patch that stops applying on one build line.
D4 chose the rule. Write this bead AFTER poly-u9n4.3, when the dragonfly/
folder is the install and a per-line copy is a file in dragonfly/@<target>/
with no op. Written earlier, its recipe would be an op that u9n4.3
deletes. Decision labels (D4, S5, S7) are the epic's.

THE RULE (D4). A file in plain dragonfly/ is shared: every build line
installs it. When a shared patch stops applying on one build line, THAT
line takes its own copy, dragonfly/@<target>/<name>, and the shared copy
stays. The same holds on every line, @main included. When FreeBSD
supersedes the patch on one line (its own files/patch-* does the same
there), that line removes it for itself only.

WHY, recorded because this bead's 2026-10-01 note chose differently.
- That note decided by "does the other build line need the old patch or
  the new one?". An env cannot answer it: it has one freebsd-ports
  checkout, on its own branch (poly-7pwa.8), and never sees the other
  line's source. The line it is on is the only fact it has.
- Round 1 proposed re-cutting the shared copy in place on @main. That
  ships a patch cut against main's source to the live quarterly, which
  rejects it at its next build: one production failure and one agent job
  per drift event. Under this rule no live line changes untested (the
  epic's invariant), and the reject on this line is the measured
  divergence S5 asks for.
- Divergence runs one way. Of 342 patched ports whose sources differ
  between main and 2026Q3, 314 moved on main only, 28 on both and 0 on
  2026Q3 only. Method: DeltaPorts overlays matching
      ^\s*file\s+materialize\s+dragonfly/(?!@)\S*patch-\S+
  whose <origin>/Makefile exists on freebsd-ports main and on 2026Q3
  (1582 ports); a port differs when "git diff --name-only 2026Q3 main"
  lists one of its */distinfo or */files/* paths, and it moved on a
  branch when the diff from the merge-base de72fdf44581 (2026-07-08) to
  that branch lists one. So most per-line copies will be @main's.
- Precedent: DeltaPorts c030e103838 (ports-mgmt/pkg 2.8.4 on @main):
  "@any keeps the autosetup form for every quarter and only main
  diverges". The line whose build broke took its own form. The same
  commit moved patch-auto.def.c under dragonfly/@2026Q3/, because the
  file it patches no longer exists on main: the renamed-file case below.
- Cost: per-line copies accumulate, and a new quarterly inherits the
  older shared copy until it is promoted at bring-up (new P3 bead
  "promote per-line patch copies to the shared folder at quarter
  bring-up").

PREMISE, verified 2026-10-04 on master ab725ac plus the seven picks;
re-check on the tree after u9n4.3.
- The resolver u9n4.3 plans for install_patches (explicit op src, else an
  existing @T or flat file, else the genpatch header key, else flat)
  never chooses dragonfly/@<target>/ for a file that exists only flat. So
  without CHANGE 1 the first per-line copy of a shared patch overwrites
  the file every line reads.
- A scoped file remove overrides a shared install on its own line only:
  verified with materialize ops on master after poly-bz7n.1 (@main:
  absent, @2026Q3: present). With the folder install it is UNVERIFIED

With line_copy true:

With line_copy false the behaviour is unchanged.

CHANGE 2. New file
dportsv3/agent/playbooks/error-shared-patch-stops-applying-here.md, loaded

    A file in plain `dragonfly/` is shared: every build line installs it. A

    there instead of a shared file of the same name. When a shared patch

    - **Upstream renamed the file it patches:** your patch gets a new

    - **FreeBSD now does the same here (superseded, Step 1):** remove it

    - **It is already this line's own copy:** re-cut it in place;

    To remove a shared file for this line only, put
