notes:
SECOND PASS, re-reading the patching paths with 'no build can validate another target' as the lens.

ON-MISSING IS THE SILENT-SKIP DOOR, AND THE QUICKREF RECOMMENDS IT. Default
on-missing is 'error' (apply_common.py:38-44), which is the good news: an @any
op whose subject does not exist on another target HARD FAILS that target's
compose. Loud, discoverable at the other line's next compose.

But dops_quickref.md:224-227 says:

  'warn is the right choice when an op is idempotent across targets
   (e.g. removing a fix that's already been upstreamed in some branches)'

That is precisely a cross-target instruction, and it converts the loud failure
into a skipped op plus a W_APPLY_ON_MISSING_WARN nobody reads. With no build on
the other target, 'warn' means the op may or may not have applied there and
nothing will ever say which. The guidance is not wrong in principle -- an
upstreamed fix genuinely is idempotent -- but it is written as though a build
would catch the case where the author guessed wrong.

What the revised guidance needs: on-missing error is the default BECAUSE it is
the only cross-target oracle we have; reach for warn only when the op's absence
on another target is a fact you have checked, and say in a comment which target
you checked and when. An unverified 'warn' in @any is an untestable claim.

Related: poly-7pwa.8 (compose the other target -- the check that makes an
on-missing error actually fire somewhere a human sees it).
ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED. The review rejected it and I agree with the rejection;
the analysis underneath was wrong in DIRECTION, not in detail, so there was
nothing to patch.

THE MECHANISM I DOCUMENTED IS REFUSED BY poly-7pwa.3, WHICH I WROTE. Adding
'file materialize dragonfly/@main/patch-X -> dragonfly/patch-X' on top of an
existing flat @any op for that destination returns E_SEM_DUPLICATE_DESTINATION --
verified. That is the situation an agent is actually in: 4280 @any dragonfly
payload ops across 1665 ports, against 31 scoped ops in 2 ports. So the first
thing my guidance told the agent to do fails for every port but rust and pkg.
The correct move -- REPOINT the existing op -- appeared nowhere in my section.

THE COUNTERWEIGHT OVER-STEERS, and this is the part worth keeping in mind for
whoever retries. I imported 'the @any scope is the one nothing can check' from
poly-7pwa.12, where it is true because mk set inserts and never fails. It does
NOT transfer to source patches, where the asymmetry runs the other way:

  - a wrongly-SHARED @any source patch announces itself on the other line --
    'FAILED Applying dragonfly patch-X', N of M hunks failed -- which is a
    classified patch-error with a playbook and a documented re-cut path. That
    is how rust and pkg came to be scoped, AFTER measuring divergence.
  - a wrongly-SCOPED patch is the silent one: the other line composes without
    it and reproduces the original failure.

So for source patches @any should stay the default and scoping should answer a
MEASURED divergence (a reject, a renamed file, a different version string), not
a presumption. My table asserted the presumption.

THE TABLE WAS ALSO WRONG ON THE LIVE CASES. Of 22 non-@any mk/text ops in the
tree my 'framework/mk value -> @any' row misroutes all 6 that are not
version-pinned, including pkg's @main 'mk target set dfly-patch' (2.8.4 renamed
Makefile.autosetup) and rust's ARG_MAX vendor-glob text ops -- and the bead had
explicitly told me to mine pkg's comment for exactly that. Rows 1 and 3 also
collide on the modal case: a DragonFly platform fix is usually IMPLEMENTED as a
dragonfly/patch-* against distfile source, so the table gave one answer twice.
And a row was missing that the tree demonstrates: rust's 57 flat crate patches
pin CRATE versions, not rust versions, and reach every cargo port in the tree
via CARGO_EXTRA_PATCHDIR -- scoping those would strip them from every other
build line's cargo ports. Highest blast radius in the tree.

IT ALSO BROKE TWO OF .12'S SENTENCES in the same file ('PORTREVISION is the
exception', 'the one place the rule inverts') by adding three more rows that go
the same way.

WHAT DID LAND SEPARATELY, because it is a defect in shipped work rather than
part of this bead: .11's 'the scoped one wins on its own target and loses on
every other' was made FALSE by .3 refusing that pair. Corrected to name the
diagnostic and the real remedy, and pinned to engine behaviour by
tests/test_ordering_section_matches_the_engine.py so the two cannot drift apart
again.

STILL OPEN FOR A RETRY, in priority order, from the review:
1. the sentence that unblocks the whole path: if an @any op already fills that
   destination, repoint IT; two writers is E_SEM_DUPLICATE_DESTINATION.
2. how the file reaches the scoped lane the FIRST time --
   _dragonfly_payload_dir returns the flat lane when no scoped source exists
   yet, so install_patches will not do it and put_file is the only route.
   flow-patch.md:311 currently reads as forbidding a write under ports/<origin>/
   although _reject_dports_write allows it.
3. scope_note is conditional; do not promise it unconditionally.
4. the comma-list 'target @A,@B' form is absent from the whole agent corpus.
5. the on-missing clause this bead's own notes asked for: 165 @any ops already
   carry warn/noop, and the quickref still recommends warn for cross-target
   idempotency -- which opts out of the only cross-target oracle there is.
6. put the minimum rule in dops_quickref.md too: flow-patch.md is flows:[patch]
   only, so none of this reaches convert or triage (poly-7pwa.19).

Also from the review, worth fixing whenever touched: 'DragonFly has no libelf
at all' in flow-patch.md is false -- devel/libelf is a live overlay and 12
overlays reference it. It was my one worked example of 'an argument you can
state'.
THE REVERT REASON IS VOID (2026-10-01). The blocker recorded above --- "the
mechanism I documented is refused by poly-7pwa.3, which I wrote" --- was real,
but .3 is the thing that is wrong. See .3's notes: adding a concrete-scoped
op on top of a flat @any op for one destination is a NORMATIVE OVERRIDE
(docs/dsl-v0.md:122-132), observed working on master, and .3's own notes
described those semantics correctly before refusing them. So the mechanism
this bead documented was sound. I reverted the correct commit of the two.

WHAT A RETRY MUST STILL KEEP, because not everything here was wrong:

1. THE COUNTERWEIGHT CRITICISM STANDS. The "@any is the scope nothing can
   check" framing was imported from poly-7pwa.12, where it holds because
   mk set inserts and never fails. It does NOT transfer to source patches,
   where the asymmetry runs the other way: a wrongly-SHARED patch announces
   itself as a patch reject on the other line's next compose, while a
   wrongly-SCOPED one is silent. Guidance that pushes toward scoping by
   default therefore trades a loud failure for a quiet one. Do not
   reintroduce it.

2. THERE ARE NOW TWO CORRECT MOVES, AND THAT IS THE THING TO TEACH. The
   original section named only one and it was the rarer one.

   * REPOINT the existing op --- when the patch should change on EVERY build
     line (a re-cut against drifted upstream that drifted the same way
     everywhere). Touches one op, no new scope, and this appeared nowhere in
     the reverted text.
   * OVERRIDE with a scoped op --- when only THIS line's patch changes and
     the other lines must keep what they have. Legal per .3's corrected rule,
     and the flat @any op remains the fallback every other line gets.

   The choice is decided by one question the agent can actually answer: does
   the other build line need the old patch or the new one? Not by which
   construct looks safer.

3. THE POPULATION MATTERS FOR WHICH MOVE IS COMMON. Measured 2026-09-28
   across 5087 planned overlays: 1802 carry a flat @any src under
   dragonfly/ (criterion: an @any file.materialize/copy whose src starts
   "dragonfly/" and not "dragonfly/@"). 2 carry a concrete scope at all.
   The earlier note above cites 1665 ports / 4280 ops on a criterion I did
   not record; treat 1802 as the measured figure and re-measure before
   quoting either. Either way REPOINT is the modal case and OVERRIDE is the
   exception, so the guidance must lead with repoint.

title: an op whose file a later op replaces or removes on every build line it runs on is accepted, so the overlay carries a write no build ever sees
description:
Two `file materialize` ops may name the same destination with different
sources and the engine says nothing.

MEASURED. ports-mgmt/pkg's real overlay plus one appended op materializing to
a destination the overlay already fills:

    build_plan ok: True   diagnostics: 0
      scope=@main  src=dragonfly/@main/patch-configure.def
      scope=@main  src=dragonfly/patch-configure.def

Two sources, one destination, same effective scope, no diagnostic. Which file
the build ends up with is decided by op order inside the compose stage -- a
detail no overlay author is reading -- and the losing source sits in the tree
looking installed.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE RATHER THAN IN GENERAL. This is the exact shape that
poly-7pwa.2 produces: install_patches drops a flat patch, the agent adds an op
for it, and the port already had a scoped op filling that destination. So this
is the backstop that turns .2 (and a hand-edit making the same mistake) from
silent into loud. It is worth having even after .2 is fixed, because the agent
hand-writes overlay.dops and an operator can write the same collision.

SCOPE OF THE CHECK. A collision only matters between ops that can be effective
TOGETHER: two ops in the same scope, or one in @any and one in a specific
target, collide. Two ops in @2026Q3 and @main respectively do NOT -- that is
the whole point of the convention, and lang/rust has 29 such pairs by design,
so a naive "same dst twice" check would reject every correctly written
multi-target port in the tree. The check must be per-effective-target.

WHERE. Semantic check in dportsv3/engine/semantic.py, so `dsl check` and the
agent's validate_dops both get it. dportsv3/common/validation.py already has
the target predicates needed to enumerate which targets an overlay mentions.

VERIFICATION SHAPE: lang/rust's and pkg's real overlays must still plan clean
(they are the negative case, and a regression here breaks the tree), while the
appended-collision text above must produce a diagnostic.

THE RULE. An op is dead when, on every build line it runs on, a later op
on that line replaces or removes the file the op leaves its result in,
and no op in between reads that file. A dead op is an error.
- Where each op leaves its result. Paths are relative to the port and go
  through posixpath.normpath, because apply_common._resolve_path resolves
  ./x and a/../x to x:
      file materialize, file copy   dst        replaced whole
      file remove                   path       removed
      text ...                      file       edited in place
      mk ...                        Makefile   edited in place
      patch apply                   -          never a victim
- What each op reads. file copy reads src. A text or mk op reads the file
  it edits. patch apply counts as reading every file, because its
  subjects are inside the patch (conservative). file materialize reads its
  src from the overlay dir, not the port tree, so it reads nothing here.
- Build lines. Each distinct selector of a statement is one line. @any is
  one line that only a later @any statement reaches: every @any op runs
  before every T op (docs/dsl-v0.md:129-132, order_ops_for_target), and
  @any also runs on lines that have no block of their own. A T op is
  checked against later statements whose selectors include T.
- Results. Allowed: an @any+@T override; a comma-list default followed by
  a per-line op; an @any materialize with an @main remove; a text or mk
  edit written after the write that replaces its file (since poly-bz7n.1
  the edit sees the written file). Rejected: "@main b" then
  "@main,@2026Q3 a" (b never lands); two @any writers; materialize then
  remove on the same lines; remove then materialize on the same lines (the
  materialize replaces the file whole, and with no upstream file the
  remove fails the apply); a text or mk edit written before a write that
  replaces its file.
- Out of scope, measured: two "mk set VAR". The tree has 3 such pairs,
  each "mk set IGNORE" twice in @any (dns/mDNSResponder_nss,
  www/baculum-api, www/unit-ruby, from the Step 48 mass conversion). As
  errors they would compose those ports without their overlay, and
  flow-patch.md tolerates a re-emitted mk set.

    def _file_effect(
        op: OperationNode,
    ) -> tuple[str | None, bool, frozenset[str] | None]:
        """What ``op`` does to the port tree, for the dead-op rule.

        Returns (the file the op leaves its result in, whether it replaces
        or removes that file whole, the files it reads first). The reads are
        ``None`` for ``patch apply``: its subjects are inside the patch, so it
        counts as reading every file. Paths go through posixpath.normpath,
        because apply_common._resolve_path resolves ``./x`` and ``a/../x``
        to ``x``.

        This is the effects table poly-7pwa.8 lifts into a shared engine
        helper; extend it here rather than re-encoding it there.
        """
        if isinstance(op, FileOpNode):
            target = op.path if op.action == "remove" else op.dst
            reads = {op.src} if op.action == "copy" and op.src else set()
            return (
                posixpath.normpath(target) if target else None,
                True,
                frozenset(posixpath.normpath(p) for p in reads),
            )
        if isinstance(op, TextOpNode):
            path = posixpath.normpath(op.file_path) if op.file_path else None
            return path, False, frozenset({path} if path else ())
        if isinstance(op, MkOpNode):
            return "Makefile", False, frozenset({"Makefile"})
        return None, False, None


    _FAMILY = {FileOpNode: "file", TextOpNode: "text", MkOpNode: "mk"}


    def _lines(span: SourceSpan) -> str:
        if span.line_end > span.line_start:
            return f"lines {span.line_start}-{span.line_end}"
        return f"line {span.line_start}"


    def _validate_dead_ops(
        op_scopes: list[tuple[OperationNode, tuple[str, ...]]],
        source_path: Path | None,
    ) -> list[Diagnostic]:
        """E_SEM_DEAD_OP for an op no build line ever sees (poly-7pwa.3).

        ``op_scopes`` is every operation in file order with its distinct
        selectors. On a build for T the engine runs every @any op, then every
        T op, each in file order (docs/dsl-v0.md, "Target scope rules";
        models.order_ops_for_target), so a T op can only be replaced by a
        later op whose selectors include T, and an @any op -- which also runs
        on lines that have no block of their own -- only by a later @any op.
        A change to that order is a change to this rule.
        """
        effects = [_file_effect(op) for op, _ in op_scopes]
        diagnostics: list[Diagnostic] = []
        for i, (op, lines) in enumerate(op_scopes):
            path = effects[i][0]
            if path is None:
                continue
            killers: dict[str, int] = {}
            for line in lines:
                for j in range(i + 1, len(op_scopes)):
                    if line not in op_scopes[j][1]:
                        continue
                    written, replaces, reads = effects[j]
                    if reads is None or path in reads:
                        break
                    if replaces and written == path:
                        killers[line] = j
                        break
            if len(killers) != len(lines):
                continue
            by_killer: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
            for line in lines:
                by_killer.setdefault(killers[line], []).append(
                    "every build line" if line == "@any" else line
                )
            clauses = []
            for j, where in sorted(by_killer.items()):
                killer = op_scopes[j][0]
                verb = "removes" if killer.action == "remove" else "writes"
                clauses.append(
                    f"line {killer.span.line_start} {verb} {path} after it "
                    f"on {' and '.join(where)}"
                )
            later = ("that later op was" if len(by_killer) == 1
                     else "one of those later ops was")
            here = _lines(op.span)
            diagnostics.append(_diag(
                "E_SEM_DEAD_OP",
                f"{here} ({_FAMILY[type(op)]} {op.action}) never takes "
                f"effect: {'; '.join(clauses)}, so no build line ever sees "
                f"its result. If {later} meant for another build line, move "
                f"it into that line's target block. Otherwise delete {here}, "
                f"or, to keep it instead, move it to the end of the file "
                f"under its own 'target {','.join(lines)}' line.",
                op.span, source_path,
            ))
        return diagnostics

THE DIAGNOSTIC.
- Code E_SEM_DEAD_OP, new; severity error. One diagnostic per dead
  statement, anchored at the dead (earlier) op, however many lines or
  blocks the overlay has.
- "line N", or "lines S-E" for a statement over several lines (backslash
  continuations, heredocs), so deleting what it names deletes the whole
  statement.
- Text as dportsv3 dsl check prints it (exit 2):
      ERROR E_SEM_DEAD_OP: line 5 (file materialize) never takes effect:
      line 6 writes files/x after it on every build line, so no build
      line ever sees its result. If that later op was meant for another
      build line, move it into that line's target block. Otherwise delete
      line 5, or, to keep it instead, move it to the end of the file
      under its own 'target @any' line. [<dir>/overlay.dops:5:1]

  in the file's last block (poly-7pwa.1). lang/rust ends in "target

  "Delete line N" alone would then hand @main the @2026Q3 re-cut, so the
  message offers moving the later op first. It never claims deleting is

FIXTURE (shared component; this bead owns its spec). tests/conftest.py
gains one dataclass and two session fixtures for every test that reads
the real DeltaPorts tree. Everything is derived from the plan, so a
quarter rollover (@2026Q3 -> @2026Q4) or a renamed patch neither breaks
nor silently empties a test. Add "from dataclasses import dataclass" to
the imports and append, verbatim:

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The real DeltaPorts tree, for tests that read it (poly-7pwa.3)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------


    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class MultiLinePort:
        """A DeltaPorts port whose overlay names two or more build lines.

        Every field is read from the overlay's plan, never written down, so
        a test built on it survives a quarter rollover (@2026Q3 -> @2026Q4)
        and a re-cut that renames a patch.
        """

        origin: str                  # "lang/rust"
        overlay: Path                # <delta>/ports/lang/rust/overlay.dops
        lines: tuple[str, ...]       # concrete targets its ops name, sorted
        last_lines: tuple[str, ...]  # where an op appended at EOF lands
        materializes: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...]  # (scope, src, dst)

        def scoped(self, line: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
            """(src, dst) of the materializes bound to ``line`` itself."""
            return [(s, d) for t, s, d in self.materializes if t == line]

        def flat(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
            """(src, dst) of the ``@any`` materializes."""
            return [(s, d) for t, s, d in self.materializes if t == "@any"]


    @pytest.fixture(scope="session")
    def delta_ports() -> Path:
        """DeltaPorts' ports/ dir, through paths.resolve_delta_root.

        Skips when no checkout is configured ($DPORTS_DELTA_ROOT or the
        paths.delta_root setting): a hardcoded path would run these tests
        on one machine and silently skip them everywhere else.
        """
        from dportsv3.paths import resolve_delta_root

        try:
            root = resolve_delta_root() / "ports"
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            root = None
        if root is None or not root.is_dir():
            pytest.skip("DeltaPorts checkout not present")
        return root


    @pytest.fixture(scope="session")
    def multi_line_ports(delta_ports: Path) -> list[MultiLinePort]:
        """Every port whose overlay names at least two build lines.

        Skips when none does: below two lines there is nothing multi-line
        to test, and a test that passed over an empty list would claim
        coverage it does not have.
        """
        from dportsv3.engine.api import build_plan

        found: list[MultiLinePort] = []
        for overlay in sorted(delta_ports.glob("*/*/overlay.dops")):
            text = overlay.read_text()
            if "target @" not in text:
                continue
            planned = build_plan(text, overlay)
            if not planned.ok or planned.plan is None:
                continue
            ops = planned.plan.ops
            lines = tuple(sorted({o.target for o in ops} - {"@any"}))
            if len(lines) < 2:
                continue
            sep = "" if text.endswith("\n") else "\n"
            probe = build_plan(text + sep + 'mk set FIXTURE_PROBE "x"\n',
                               overlay).plan
            last = probe.ops[-1].span
            found.append(MultiLinePort(
                origin=str(overlay.parent.relative_to(delta_ports)),
                overlay=overlay,
                lines=lines,
                last_lines=tuple(o.target for o in probe.ops
                                 if o.span == last),
                materializes=tuple(
                    (o.target, o.payload["src"], o.payload["dst"])
                    for o in ops if o.kind == "file.materialize"
                ),
            ))
        if not found:
            pytest.skip("no DeltaPorts overlay names two or more build lines")
        return found

    HEAD = 'port devel/thing\ntype port\nreason "fixture"\n'  # lines 1-3

    def _m(src: str, dst: str = "files/x") -> str:

    def _dead(text: str):
        result = build_plan(HEAD + text, None)

    def test_an_append_to_a_real_overlays_last_block_kills_that_lines_op(
        multi_line_ports,

        The copy lands in the same block, so the original never takes
        effect: one E_SEM_DEAD_OP, at the original. The same op under its
        own `target @any` line is the override, and is allowed.

            if len(port.last_lines) != 1:
                continue
            line = port.last_lines[0]
            own = [(s, d) for s, d in port.scoped(line)

            if not own:

            src, dst = own[-1]
            text = port.overlay.read_text()

                for op in build_plan(text, port.overlay).plan.ops
                if op.target == line and op.payload.get("src") == src
                and op.payload.get("dst") == dst

            appended = f"file materialize {src} -> {dst}\n"
            result = build_plan(text + sep + appended, port.overlay)
            assert [d.line for d in result.diagnostics

            result = build_plan(text + sep + "target @any\n" + appended,
                                port.overlay)
            assert result.ok is True, (port.origin, result.diagnostics)
            checked.append(port.origin)

title: a table-rebuild migration copies under FK enforcement, so an orphan row fails a service start rather than being reported
description:
_add_build_flavor_dimension copies rows into the rebuilt table with
foreign key enforcement ON, because init_db sets PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON
before it runs. SQLite's own documented procedure for a table rebuild
says the opposite: disable foreign keys for the rebuild, and run
PRAGMA foreign_key_check afterwards.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is worse than it was before poly-5d58: the copy is
"INSERT INTO build_results_flavored (...) SELECT ... FROM build_results",
so one orphan row raises IntegrityError, the migration phase rolls back
(it is now one transaction), init_db raises, and in the tracker that is a
failed startup lifespan -- the service does not start. A rebuild is
therefore STRICTER than the steady state, and can fail on data the
application itself was able to write.

FOUND, not theorised: writing a test fixture for poly-5d58 with a
build_results row whose build_run_id had no build_runs row produced

  sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed
  dportsv3/db/schema.py:747, the INSERT ... SELECT

and it took a minute to see it was the fixture and not the lock work.

CAN ORPHANS ACTUALLY EXIST? Not from anything writing today, as far as
this goes: FK enforcement is PER CONNECTION and artifact_store.py:137
opens one WITHOUT it (only tracker/db.py:80 and db/schema.py set the
pragma), but the tables that store connection writes -- runs, bundles,
issues, jobs, blob_objects, artifact_refs -- carry none of the four
declared foreign keys, which are build_runs.build_type,
build_results.build_run_id and port_status.last_{attempt,success}_run_id.
So this is latent, not live, and the bead is P2 for that reason.

What makes it worth fixing anyway is that the gap is structural: the
enforcement a row was written under is not the enforcement it is later
copied under, and the place that discovers the mismatch is a service
start on a production host.

TWO THINGS TO DECIDE, and they are separate:
1. Should the rebuild follow the documented procedure -- foreign_keys=OFF
   around the copy, foreign_key_check after, and report what it finds
   rather than refuse to start? A migration that names its orphans is a
   very different morning from one that says "FOREIGN KEY constraint
   failed" during boot.
2. Should every writer open with foreign_keys=ON, so the four declared
   keys mean the same thing on every connection? Today they are enforced
   by whoever happens to have set the pragma, which is most of the reason
   1 is a question at all.

title: Pre-provider delivery failures leave accepted bundles without a retryable delivery row
description: Discovered during poly-86t closure review. In tracker/routes/bundle_actions.py, _accept_delivery_step returns create_failed for DeliveryConfigError, changes.diff read errors, and escaped orchestrator exceptions without inserting bundle_review_requests. Accept has already persisted accepted. The /deliver endpoint requires a latest create_failed review-request row, so a first delivery failing here cannot be retried even after configuration or storage is repaired; the Delivery card has no row and no retry button. Reproduce with a verified bundle and a GitHub delivery config missing clone_dir: accept returns create_failed, latest review request is absent, and deliver returns 409 nothing to retry. Preserve acceptance while making these failures durably visible and recoverable; test repaired configuration followed by successful delivery. Distinct from poly-86t, whose implemented contract starts with an existing create_failed row.
notes:
Revisited against code: three explicit create_failed returns in _accept_delivery_step lack durable rows (configuration validation, diff read OSError, escaped orchestrator exceptions). Reproduced all three with endpoint tests: accepted response reports failure but latest_review_request_for_bundle is None. Existing schema permits an unknown provider when config cannot resolve; use that truthful sentinel rather than guessing a provider from invalid config. Persist these failures through one helper; preserve skipped outcomes and existing retry gate. Tests will repair each injected fault and exercise real local-patch delivery, rendered retry action, and unchanged acceptance history.
Implemented and re-reviewed: record_failure persists all three explicit early create_failed outcomes with operator, error signature, error and request ID; unknown provider only when configuration cannot resolve. Existing skips and retry eligibility remain unchanged. Regression tests first failed for all three absent-row cases, then passed; configuration case now uses a real malformed TOML file and repairs it, other cases inject filesystem/setup errors. Each recovers through real local-patch provider, checks rendered retry button and preserves accepted_at plus single acceptance event. 473 tests passed across accept integration, retry endpoint, configuration wiring, clone locking and state gates. No historical backfill or production deployment.
close_reason: Early delivery failures now persist retryable records; three failure-to-recovery integration cases pass, 473 targeted tests passed.

Two hundred lines above it, and matching the same element:

    .turn-stream .tool-call pre {      /* 0,2,1 */
      color: var(--code-fg); background: var(--code-bg);
    }

The tail is a <pre class="tool-tail"> INSIDE a .tool-call, so the second rule
wins on specificity -- one element selector beats nothing -- and the tail has
rendered as a code block ever since. In the light theme that is #253039 on
#f6f8fa, which is exactly the treatment poly-qqx9.17 was filed to replace.

MEASURED, not inferred. getComputedStyle on the job page:

    BG=rgb(246, 248, 250)   FG=rgb(37, 48, 57)     i.e. --code-bg / --code-fg

and raising the tail rule to `.turn-stream .tool-call pre.tool-tail` flips it
to the terminal the design asks for -- verified by screenshot, white on black,
in the light theme.

IT IS BROKEN IN PRODUCTION TOO, not only locally: a screenshot of the running
builder's job page shows the same light block behind the tour overlay.

WHY IT SURVIVED. The bead's tests assert on the STYLESHEET -- that
.turn-stream .tool-tail names var(--term-fg) and not --code-*, and that the
tokens are dark in every theme. All of that is true. None of it can see that
another rule wins. A stylesheet assertion cannot test the cascade; only a
rendered page can.

FIX: one selector, `.turn-stream .tool-call pre.tool-tail`. Do not rely on
source order instead -- .tool-tail already comes later in the file and still
loses, and a rule that depends on where it sits breaks the next time the file
is reorganised.

WORTH ADDING WITH IT: a rendered check for this one element. The repo's rule
is that screenshot diffs are noise and pictures are for a person to read, and
that stands -- but "the build log is white on black" is one computed value on
one element, not a diff, and it is the kind of thing the stylesheet tests
provably cannot catch.
notes:
Reported by the operator 2026-09-25T09:30:08Z, in the same message as poly-qdy7: "it still does not look like the dsynth tail has the terminal colors, at least in light theme". Not first found by me today -- the earlier session was compacted before either half became a bead.
FIXED 2026-09-26. .turn-stream .tool-tail -> .turn-stream .tool-call
pre.tool-tail (0,2,0 -> 0,3,1), exactly as the bead prescribes, with the
reason in the sheet next to the rule so the next reorganisation does not
flatten it back.

MEASURED IN CHROME, not resolved on paper. Headless Chrome over CDP,
getComputedStyle on pre.tool-tail, a seeded job with dsynth_build running
and a tail published:

  before, light   BG=rgb(246, 248, 250)  FG=rgb(37, 48, 57)    --code-*
  after,  light   BG=rgb(14, 22, 29)     FG=rgb(200, 212, 220) --term-*
  after,  dark    BG=rgb(5, 9, 13)       FG=rgb(200, 212, 220) --term-*

The "before" line reproduces this bead's own numbers to the digit, which
is what makes the other two worth anything. Both rules match the element
in all three runs; only the winner changes.

THE RENDERED CHECK IS IN tests/test_tail_terminal_cascade.py, and it is not
a browser. It renders the job page through the test client, walks the real
ancestor chain to the <pre>, collects every rule in the document -- linked
sheet plus the page's own inline <style>, in document order -- and resolves
color and background by specificity. Reverting the selector fails two of
its six tests with "the tail's ground comes from .turn-stream .tool-call
pre: var(--code-bg)". Checked in both directions, and checked against the
browser numbers above.

  WHY NOT A REAL BROWSER IN pytest. It would mean a driver dependency and a
  chrome binary on the test host, and [dev] already does not install on a
  DragonFly builder (poly-170). The CDP rig that produced the table above
  lives in the session scratch, not the repo: it is how the resolver was
  validated, not how it runs.

  WHAT KEEPS IT HONEST. The resolver reads descendant and child
  combinators, classes, tags and `*`, and nothing else -- about a hundred
  selectors in this sheet it cannot read, plus every @media body. Those are
  not skipped quietly: each one that declares a colour or a ground at all
  is WEAKENED into a selector matching a superset of itself (pseudo-classes
  and attribute selectors dropped, everything left of a sibling combinator
  dropped, :root -> html) and tested against the tail. Anything that still
  reaches it fails the run. A rule that sets neither property cannot decide
  either contest however it matches, which is how :focus-visible stays out
  of it.

TWO THINGS THE BEAD DID NOT SAY, both found in the code:

1. THERE IS A SECOND COMPETING RULE. .turn-stream .tool-call.state-bad pre
(progress.css:2567) is also (0,3,1) -- it TIES with the fix and wins or
loses on source order alone, which is the thing the bead says not to rely
on. Left alone deliberately: it cannot co-occur with a tail. A tail is
attached only by attach_tool_tail -> running_tailable_tool, which requires
tool["running"], and a running tool is given state "run"
(render/activity.py:242, 261), never "bad"; the template reinforces it by
rendering the tail only in the branch for a tool with no diagnostic body.
Today the fix also happens to sit later in the file, so even the tie goes
the right way. If a failed dsynth_build ever grows a tail -- poly-pvs2
floats linking a failed row to its errors.txt, which is a LINK and not this
-- that rule needs a look before the tail is shown on it.

2. THE OLD TEST PASSED ON PROSE. test_the_tail_uses_the_terminal_tokens
anchored with CSS.index(".turn-stream .tool-tail"), which is a PREFIX of
".turn-stream .tool-tailbar" -- and after the rename it matched the new
comment's text instead, read to the next }, and passed while reading a
sentence. Two ways to pass without reading the rule, in the one test
guarding it. It now strips comments and matches the full selector.

WHAT IS STILL NOT COVERED, and is the honest limit of all of it: nothing
here would notice if .turn-stream .tool-call pre itself were changed to the
terminal tokens, collapsing the design's distinction between the build log
and a tool's captured stdout -- except that the cascade test now also
asserts the winning selector names .tool-tail, which catches that one
shape of it. A second <pre> on the page and a two-element comparison would
close it properly; not worth the fixture for one bead.
close_reason: Fixed: .turn-stream .tool-call pre.tool-tail. Verified in Chrome via getComputedStyle in both themes, with the pre-fix control reproducing the bead's own rgb(246,248,250)/rgb(37,48,57). Rendered cascade check added in tests/test_tail_terminal_cascade.py.

title: jobs.flavor holds the origin, and the tail's flavor match silently falls through to the newest log
description:
Job 20260925-091002Z-2026Q3-print_qt6-pdf-905127-patch.job stores

  origin  print/qt6-pdf
  flavor  print/qt6-pdf

The job page renders it as "Origin print/qt6-pdf @ print/qt6-pdf". A flavor is
a dsynth flavor name -- "default", "bootstrap", "qt5" -- never an origin, and
nothing downstream expects one to contain a slash.

WHAT IT BREAKS. dsynth_tail.log_path() builds the filename dsynth would have
written for that flavor:

    stem   = _dsynth_log_stem(origin)             # print___qt6-pdf
    wanted = f"{stem}@{flavor.lstrip('@')}.log"   # print___qt6-pdf@print/qt6-pdf.log

A filename containing "/" can never match a directory entry, so the loop falls
through to `return candidates[0]` -- the newest log by mtime for that stem. On
a port with one log that is accidentally right. On a FLAVORED port it is the
wrong flavor's log whenever another flavor was built more recently, and the
page then shows an operator the last lines of a build they are not looking at,
with nothing saying so.

Found while diagnosing poly-5qtr, where this was the competing explanation for
a job that looked stuck: it had to be ruled out (by the log's mtime) before
the real cause could be named. That is the cost of it -- not a wrong pixel, a
wrong answer during an incident.

TWO THINGS TO DECIDE, and they are separate

1. WHERE THE BAD VALUE COMES FROM. Whatever writes jobs.flavor put the origin
   in it. Walk back from the enqueue -- the queue filename
   (...-2026Q3-print_qt6-pdf-905127-patch.job) carries target and origin and no
   flavor at all, so something is filling the field from the wrong variable.
   Until that is found it is unknown how many rows carry it.

2. WHAT log_path SHOULD DO with a flavor it cannot use. Silently falling
   through to "newest" is the part that makes this invisible. A flavor that
   matches no candidate is a fact worth returning -- the tail's own error
   channel already exists and the page renders it ("dsynth has written no log
   for X yet" comes back the same way).
notes:
FIXED 2026-09-26. ITEM 1 OF THIS BEAD IS A MISDIAGNOSIS, and correcting it
is most of the work.

"Something is filling the field from the wrong variable" -- no. DSYNTH
EXPORTS FLAVOR=$ORIGIN FOR A PORT WITH NO FLAVOUR. A row reading

  origin  print/qt6-pdf
  flavor  print/qt6-pdf

is correct data carrying dsynth's unflavored sentinel. The hooks state the
rule and honour it in both places they build a name from it:

  hook_common.sh:125   "dsynth sets FLAVOR=$ORIGIN when no flavor; only add
                        @ when different"  (logfile_for_origin)
  hook_pkg_failure:23  the same guard, building the bundle id

hook_pkg_failure:137 then calls enqueue_job with the RAW "$FLAVOR", which
is how the sentinel reaches the queue file and jobs.flavor. So nothing
wrote a wrong value and no walk-back is needed; the field is
un-normalised, not corrupt, and every row that carries it is carrying the
truth in dsynth's spelling.

The tracker learned this independently and TODAY: _port_identity
(tracker/db.py:56, landed in 3bfecca) collapses `flavor in (origin, base)`
to "". Two of the three consumers already knew. The tail was the one that
did not.

WHAT WAS CHANGED

1. dsynth_tail.real_flavor(origin, flavor) -- the rule in one place on this
side, matching logfile_for_origin and _port_identity, handling the @ and a
suffixed origin.

2. log_path uses it, and NO LONGER FALLS THROUGH. A real flavour that
matches no candidate returns None instead of candidates[0]. That is item 2
of this bead and it is the half that made the defect invisible.

3. read_tail names the flavour it could not find: "no log for
devel/glib20@bootstrap yet" rather than "no log for devel/glib20 yet".
Different facts, and only the second explains an empty page during a
running build.

4. agentic_job.html no longer renders "print/qt6-pdf@print/qt6-pdf".

A TRAP WORTH RECORDING, because the obvious fix causes it. building_origin
hands the SAME flavour to every origin in the run. Resolve the sentinel
per-origin and it collapses to "" beside the job's own port and stays a
real-looking flavour beside the master -- no www___qt6-webengine@print/qt6-
pdf.log can exist -- so with item 2 in place the master is SKIPPED, the
tail sits on the finished slave, and that is exactly the freeze poly-quu3
fixed. The sentinel is only recognisable next to the origin it was
reported for.

So it is resolved ONCE, in runner.set_tail_target, against origins[0] --
the job's own port, every other entry being a sibling this invocation also
builds. log_path keeps its own normalisation for direct callers.
test_the_sentinel_is_resolved_once_against_the_jobs_own_port and
test_the_master_is_still_reachable_under_a_sentinel_flavor exist for this
and nothing else.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, and why. The hooks could normalise before enqueue, so
new rows carry "". Not done: it needs a hooks redeploy to take effect, it
does not touch the rows already written, and the consumers have to
understand the sentinel regardless because dsynth will keep sending it.
Fixing the consumer covers every row that exists; fixing the source
instead would have covered none of them. Worth doing as tidy-up, not as
this fix.

TESTS: tests/test_tail_flavor_sentinel.py, 12 of them. Four fail against
the old code -- the fallthrough, the error text, the one-time resolution,
and a real flavour narrowing the sibling search. The other eight pin
behaviour that was accidentally right, including the single-log case this
bead notes is "accidentally right"; they are there so the accident cannot
be mistaken for the guarantee.

SEPARATE AND NOT MINE: tests/test_progress_logfile_link.py::
test_the_entry_shape_is_dsynths_plus_what_the_tracker_knows fails on
master as of 3bfecca -- the progress entry grew a "flavor" key and that
test asserts an exact key set. Verified pre-existing by stashing this
work. Filed separately.
REOPENED 2026-09-27: THE FIRST PASS WAS INCOMPLETE AND I CLOSED IT ANYWAY.
The operator opened the job page after the deploy and the origin line was
still wrong.

WHAT I MISSED. This bead's own description quotes the rendering:

  "The job page renders it as 'Origin print/qt6-pdf @ print/qt6-pdf'"

That is _job_summary.html:8 -- it has the "Origin" label and spaces around
the @. I changed agentic_job.html, the heading, which has neither. Both are
on the same page, I had both in a grep result in front of me, and I picked
the one I already had open instead of the one the bead described.

THE REAL FOOTPRINT, measured on the builder rather than guessed at this
time -- six templates, not one:

  _job_summary.html      jobs     the one this bead quotes
  agentic_job.html       jobs     the heading (fixed in the first pass)
  _bundle_summary.html   bundles
  agentic_artifact.html  bundles
  agentic_session.html   bundles
  agentic_bundles.html   bundles  a Flavor COLUMN of its own

  jobs    with flavor == origin:  802 of 1480
  bundles with flavor == origin:  476 of 581
  bundles with a real flavour  :  105   (these must keep rendering)

So agentic_bundles.html printed "print/qt6-pdf" under a heading reading
Flavor, for 476 rows. build_results and port_status are unaffected -- they
go through _port_identity on the way in, and 0 of 2749 / 0 of 1731 carry a
flavour at all.

THE FIX IS ONE RULE IN ONE PLACE, not six conditions. db.port_label() and
db.real_flavor() delegate to _port_identity -- the writer's own rule, so a
view cannot disagree with the writer about what a flavour is, which is the
whole defect -- and are registered as Jinja globals. Six templates call
them. The separator is the caller's, because the heading wants it tight
inside a <code> and the tables want it spaced; that difference was one of
the reasons six conditions had already drifted.

_port_identity CORRECTED while wiring it up: it stripped the "@" AFTER
comparing against the origin, so a flavour spelled "@devel/glib20" beside
origin "devel/glib20" survived as a real-looking flavour equal to the
port. It strips first now, as dsynth_tail.real_flavor already did. Two
write-path callers, no behaviour change except that bogus case.

TESTS: tests/test_port_label.py, ten. The two that matter are
test_no_template_reimplements_the_sentinel_check, which reads every
template and fails on a raw job.flavor/bundle.flavor that is not being
handed to the helper, and test_the_rendered_job_page_shows_no_port_twice,
which renders the page and asserts on what comes out. Reverting
_job_summary.html alone fails BOTH.

THE LESSON IS THE ONE poly-atq9 ALREADY PAID FOR. A source-level check
cannot see a template it did not think to look at, exactly as a stylesheet
assertion could not see another rule winning. I wrote that sentence four
beads ago and then shipped a fix verified only by reading source. The
rendered test is the part that makes this closable.
close_reason: Completed. First pass fixed one of six renderings — and not the one this bead quotes. port_label/real_flavor now delegate to _port_identity and are registered as Jinja globals; all six templates use them. _port_identity corrected to strip the @ before the sentinel check. Ten tests including a rendered-page check, which is what the first pass lacked.

title: Latent: the heartbeat thread resolves the env through an untimed subprocess, so a stalled dev-env would stop the runner's only liveness signal
description:
The runner stopped heartbeating at 2026-09-25T09:57:08 on the builder, mid-job,
with print/qt6-pdf's dsynth_build showing "running" since 09:20:13 and the
published tail already ending in "SUCCEEDED 00:00:00". Over two hours of
silence from a signal that ticks every 5s. The job is still `patching`, the
runner row still says `processing`, and nothing in the tracker can tell that
the process behind it stopped answering.

THE THREAD THAT CANNOT BLOCK, BLOCKS

    def _heartbeat_loop():
        """Say we are alive every 5s, from a thread that keeps ticking while
        the main thread blocks in ``subprocess.run`` during a build."""
        while not _heartbeat_stop_event.is_set():
            _state_store.store().heartbeat(runner_id(), _heartbeat_tail())

Its docstring states the contract: this thread exists BECAUSE the main thread
blocks in subprocess.run during a build. The tail feature then put a
subprocess.run on it:

  _heartbeat_tail()                 runner.py
    -> dsynth_tail.read_tail()
    -> dsynth_tail.log_path()
    -> worker._dsynth_log_candidates()
    -> worker.env_paths()
    -> worker._run_dev_env("path", env)
    -> subprocess.run(...)          worker.py:115 -- NO TIMEOUT

Two things make it worse than one slow call:

1. _heartbeat_tail() is an ARGUMENT. It is evaluated before heartbeat() is
   called, so a blocked tail read does not cost a tick of tail -- it costs the
   heartbeat itself. Exactly what the tracker shows.

2. `except Exception: return None` reads as a guard and is not one. Its
   docstring promises "a log that vanished mid-build must cost a tick of tail,
   not the liveness signal the same call carries". An exception is caught; a
   HANG is not an exception.

AND A SUBPROCESS STORM BEHIND IT. env_paths is @lru_cache'd, so in the happy
path the resolve is paid once. lru_cache does not cache EXCEPTIONS, and
env_paths raises RuntimeError whenever `dev-env path` returns non-zero. So the
moment the resolve starts failing, every tick spawns it again -- two
`dportsv3 dev-env path` invocations per tick, 24 fresh Python interpreters a
minute, on a host that has just finished compiling qt6-pdf.

BOTH PROVEN LOCALLY, against the real call chain with a resolvable dev-env
entry point:

  five heartbeat ticks spawned 5 `dev-env path` subprocesses
  heartbeat tail returned within 3s: False   (against a hanging dev-env path)

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It does not yet say WHY `dev-env path` stopped
answering on the builder at 09:57. That needs the host: a `dportsv3 dev-env
path` process still sitting in the process table would settle it. But the
defect stands either way -- an unbounded subprocess on the liveness thread
turns any stall in dev-env into a runner that is silently gone while every
surface still reports it working.

THE FIX, three parts, smallest first

  * a timeout on _run_dev_env. It is the only thing between a slow dev-env and
    a dead runner, and every caller already handles a non-zero return.
  * write the heartbeat FIRST, then the tail. Evaluate _heartbeat_tail() into
    a local after the liveness write, or publish the tail on its own tick, so
    the tail can never cost the signal.
  * cache the failure. env_paths should remember that the resolve failed for a
    short while rather than re-forking 24 times a minute.

Consider also whether the tail path should touch dev-env at all on every tick:
the env_dir is immutable for the life of the env, so the heartbeat could be
handed a resolved log path once at set_tail_target() and never resolve again.

FOUND: operator, 2026-09-25, from the job page showing a finished build still
running.
notes:
CORRECTION, SAME DAY. This bead was filed asserting the runner had been silent
for over two hours. That was wrong, and the error was mine: I read the page's
UTC heartbeat against my own local clock, two hours ahead. Measured properly,
the heartbeat is HEALTHY -- sampled every 15s it came back 1s old each time,
ticking on its 5s interval throughout.

So this did NOT cause the 2026-09-25 print/qt6-pdf hang. That is poly-6q1u:
the main thread blocked in dsynth_build, with the heartbeat thread ticking
beside it exactly as designed.

WHAT SURVIVES, unchanged and still worth fixing. The defect is latent, not
hypothetical, and both halves were proven locally against the real call chain:

  five heartbeat ticks spawned 5 `dev-env path` subprocesses
  heartbeat tail returned within 3s: False  (against a hanging dev-env path)

The liveness thread reaches subprocess.run with no timeout, the result is
computed BEFORE the heartbeat it is an argument to, and `except Exception`
catches raises rather than hangs. The day dev-env does stall, the runner goes
silent while every surface still reports it working -- which is precisely what
I mistakenly believed I was looking at, and is a good argument for fixing it
before it happens for real.

Lowered to P2: nothing observed has triggered it.
The live incident is poly-5qtr (the id guessed in the note above was written before the bead existed -- poly-5qtr is the real one).

title: Job detail: no header action row, and sections have no panel chrome
description:
The job-detail page against the mock, 2026-09-25 (artifact
88bZw6sd4ZmokTb26oqQXu, both rendered at 1400 and 1920). Operator-identified;
each item verified in the code.

1. NO HEADER ACTION ROW. The mock gives the job a heading strip: the id as a
short title, a human subtitle ("patch job for databases/postgresql17-server on
@main"), and on the right a LIVE pill with Pause and Abandon as real buttons.

The built page has none of that shape:
  agentic_job.html:54   <h1>{{ job.job_id }}  -- the raw 60-char queue
                        filename, with the origin appearing only inside the
                        facts panel further down
  agentic_job.html:70   the live indicator is INSIDE the h1, and its pause is
                        a bracketed text link, "[pause]", not a button
  _job_summary.html:36  Abandon is a button labelled "Abandon job (mark dead)"
                        buried at the bottom of the facts panel

So the two controls an operator actually reaches for are a text link inside a
heading and a verbose button inside a panel that should not exist at all.
Note what the mocks Pause is NOT: poly-0e02.8 established that a runner has no
operator pause worth writing, and the runner pages [pause] was renamed for
exactly that reason. The JOB pause here is the live-poll toggle in both mock
and build; it just needs to look like the control it is.

2. THE FACTS AND LIFECYCLE TABLES ARE NOT IN THE MOCK. Already filed as
poly-qqx9.14 and not duplicated here -- but the side-by-side is what makes the
cost legible: they sit between the attempt strip and the turns and push the
turns roughly 500px down the page. Abandon moving out of the facts panel
(item 1) is a prerequisite for that bead, not a separate job.

3. SECTIONS HAVE NO PANEL CHROME, and one has none at all.

  .wt-band { margin: 16px 0 0; }        <- the ENTIRE rule for the working
                                           tree. No surface, no border, no
                                           header: it sits directly on the
                                           page background
  .turn-stream { display: flex; ... }   <- a bare column. Each card has its
                                           own border, but the STREAM has no
                                           panel and no header
  .wf { background: var(--surface);     <- has a card, but no header, so
         border: 1px solid var(--line);    nothing on screen names what the
         border-radius: 4px; }             bars are

The mock wraps each of these in .content-panel (surface + border + shadow)
with a .content-head that names it and carries a right-aligned fact:
"Attempts ... 3 of 3", "Turns  last 5 of 14 ... newest first",
"Working tree  2 files changed +39 -1 ... live". 32 uses of .content-panel in
the mock; the job detail is built out of them.

The border-radius: 4px on .wf is also an instance of poly-x3pg.15.

SCOPE: this bead is the job-detail page only. The font (poly-x3pg.13), the
width cap (poly-x3pg.14) and the corners (poly-x3pg.15) are global and are
filed separately so the remaining per-page beads do not each re-report them.
notes:
DONE, items 1 and 3. Item 2 stays poly-qqx9.14, which this now unblocks. 1. HEADING STRIP. `.page-heading` + `.heading-actions` already existed -- every other page in this console has had them since M1; job detail was the page that never got one. So this is markup, not new CSS:

the job id, alone

"patch job for devel/llvm19@default on @2026Q3", built from job.type / origin / flavor / target -- what the job IS lived only in the facts panel further down live indicator moved out of the

and into the action row Pause
close_reason: Closed

title: Content is capped at 1400px where the mock is a full-bleed application shell
description:
Found in the first side-by-side of this epic, 2026-09-25.

One rule:

  .tracker-page { padding: 16px 24px 40px; max-width: 1400px; margin: 0 auto; }

The mock has no equivalent. Its .app is a 100vh grid that fills whatever
viewport it is given -- the shell IS the window, which is the structural idea
poly-x3pg.1 (M1, "the shell is a document where the mock is an application")
already landed for the chrome. The PAGE BODY never got the same treatment.

MEASURED at two widths on the job-detail page:
  1400px   the two agree; the cap is exactly the viewport
  1920px   the mock still fills; the built page keeps its top bar and
           breadcrumbs full width but centres the content at 1400, leaving
           roughly 260px of dead gutter each side

So this is invisible on a laptop and obvious on the monitor an operator
actually watches builds on, which is why it survived every audit.

NOT SIMPLY "REMOVE THE CAP". A cap exists for a reason on text-heavy pages --
a 2560px line of prose is unreadable. The mock solves that by being an
APPLICATION: panels and tables that use the width, not paragraphs that run
across it. So the fix is per-surface, and the question for each page is
whether its content is a document (keep a measure) or a working surface
(fill). The job detail is the second: its turn cards, attempt strip and
working-tree diff all want the width.

GLOBAL: filed once here rather than repeated in each per-page bead, though
the per-page decision above is genuinely per page.
notes:
SHARPER THAN FILED. The bead reads as "the page body never got M1's
treatment"; the code says HALF of it did. There are two page containers:

  .page-body     13 templates, padding only, no cap  -> already full-bleed
  .tracker-page  12 templates, capped at 1400px      -> the ones left behind

So above 1400px the console disagreed with ITSELF -- Builds, Pipeline and
Repairs filled the monitor while Job detail, Jobs, Activity and the rest sat
centred with ~260px of dead gutter each side. That is a worse defect than the
one filed, and it explains why it was never noticed on a laptop.

THE CAP'S STATED REASON WAS ALREADY HANDLED ONE LEVEL IN. It existed so prose
would not run 2560px wide. Every prose block already measures itself:
.pipeline-note (74ch, 108ch in the scrolling variant), .notes-in (820px),
.t-pane p (62ch). The mock does the same and nothing else -- its only px
measure anywhere is `max-width: 900px` on .repair-summary, one paragraph. So
the per-surface question the bead asks ("document or working surface?")
answers itself for all 12: they are working surfaces whose paragraphs are
already measured.

DONE
  .tracker-page  max-width and margin:0 auto removed; padding kept

  .tracker-page.bundle-page { max-width: 1180px }  DELETED. It had matched
  nothing since 1a1f9cc ("repairs: one view, with the queue still beside the
  work") moved the cockpit to `.page-body bundle-page`. Its comment claimed
  the bundle page "reads as a composed column rather than a full-bleed
  stretch" -- 1a1f9cc decided the opposite and the rule was left behind
  asserting a design that had already been reversed. Nothing changes on
  screen; a misleading comment goes.

VERIFIED headless Chrome, job detail at 1920x1100: the attempt strip,
lifecycle table and activity cards now reach both edges. No gutters.

Mutation-checked: restoring the 1400px cap fails it.

title: Rounded corners throughout where the console's own language is square
description:
Found in the first side-by-side of this epic, 2026-09-25.

Counted, not eyeballed:

  mock            3 uses of border-radius
  built console  74 uses of border-radius

The mocks three are one 2px audience pill and two 50% circles (the token
gauges added by poly-qqx9.20). Everything else in it -- .pill, .control,
.panel, .content-panel, .data-table, .seg, .band-chip, the buttons -- is
SQUARE. That is not an accident of the drawing; it is the consoles visual
language, and it reads as instrument rather than web app.

The built console rounds nearly everything, which is the single largest
reason a screenshot of it does not look like a screenshot of the mock even
when the structure matches. It is also the cheapest of this epics findings to
fix and the easiest to verify: the count goes to roughly the mocks.

CARE NEEDED ON THREE OF THE 74, which are legitimately round and must stay:
- the token gauge rings (border-radius: 50%), which are circles
- anything drawing a dot or status glyph as a circle
- the live-indicator dot
So this is not a blanket delete; it is a pass with a count at the end.

GLOBAL: affects every page, filed once here.
notes:
THE BEAD WAS WRONG ABOUT DOTS, and the mock says so. As filed this reads:
"CARE NEEDED ON THREE OF THE 74, which are legitimately round and must stay:
the token gauge rings, anything drawing a dot or status glyph as a circle,
the live-indicator dot." That was written from OUR stylesheet. The mock draws
every one of those square:

  .live-dot::before      8x8 square
  .status::before        7x7 square
  .health-item.ok::before 7x7 square
  .wt-sub .dot           6x6 square
  .occ-dot               9x9 square, rotate(45deg) -- a diamond

Shape is carrying meaning there, which is the same reason this console never
lets colour carry state alone. So the state markers went square too.

COUNT, BOTH SIDES, AND IT WAS BIGGER THAN FILED. The 74 was the stylesheet
alone; six templates carry inline <style> blocks with 18 more.

  before  92 = 74 progress.css + 18 templates
  removed 80
  after    6, every one a circle by shape

The six: .now-bar .gauge-ring and its ::before hole, .token-pie, two list
bullets (.t-gates li::before, .notes li::before) and .t-dots i, the tour's
page dots. The last three have no counterpart in the mock at all -- a bullet
and a carousel dot are typographic idioms, not console instruments -- so they
were left rather than invented against.

ALSO REMOVED, as fallout rather than by rule:
  .result-filter:last-child { }   left holding nothing once its 0 3px 3px 0
                                  came off; the :first-child border-left it
                                  pairs with is still there
  two comments claiming corners that no longer exist ("a single rounded
  strip", "small rounded pills")

The rule now sits at the top of the primitives block, where the next person
adding a component reads it: square, and round only where the shape IS a
circle.

VERIFIED headless Chrome, job detail at 1400x1300 with the tour dismissed:
pills, cards, buttons, inputs, the attempt strip, turn cards and the live
indicator are all square.

GUARD tests/test_mock_visual_language.py -- every border-radius in the
stylesheet AND in every template's inline styles must be 50%, and its selector
must be one of six named shapes, so a new circle fails as loudly as a new
rounded rectangle. Plus a named check that the six state markers stay square.
close_reason: Closed

title: The console names Inter and never ships it, so the typeface is whatever the viewer owns
description:
Found in the first side-by-side of this epic, 2026-09-25 (artifact
88bZw6sd4ZmokTb26oqQXu).

Both the mock and the built console declare the SAME stack:

  --sans: Inter, ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI"

The mock loads the font -- a fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet link. The built
console loads NOTHING: no link, no @font-face, no .woff or .woff2 anywhere
under dportsv3/tracker/. So Inter is used only when the VIEWER happens to have
it installed locally, and otherwise the stack falls through to the system UI
face.

CONSEQUENCES
- two operators on two machines see two different consoles, and neither
  necessarily sees the face the design was drawn in
- every side-by-side against the mock is unfair in a way that has nothing to
  do with the thing being compared. The 2026-09-25 screenshots were taken on a
  machine without Inter, so every proportional glyph in the built column is a
  fallback and the comparison flatters the mock
- it is silent: nothing errors, nothing logs, and on a developer machine that
  has Inter the built page looks correct

THE FIX IS A DECISION, NOT A PATCH. Two honest options:
- SELF-HOST. The tracker serves on a private LAN and cannot reach Google
  Fonts, so a link would fail there anyway -- it has to be a woff2 under
  static/ with an @font-face. Costs ~100KB per weight and one more file the
  cache-buster covers (static_v hashes the whole tree since poly-3o3o).
- DROP INTER from the stack and design for the system face, accepting that
  the mock and the built console will never match on type.

Either is defensible. What is not is naming a font and not shipping it.
GLOBAL: this affects every page, so it is filed once here rather than repeated
in each per-page bead.
notes:
DECIDED: self-host. Dropping Inter would make the epic's most pervasive
property permanently un-matchable, and the mock's fonts.googleapis.com link
cannot work on a tracker with no egress -- so a woff2 under static/ was the
only option that gets Inter at all.

SHIPPED
  static/fonts/inter-latin-var.woff2   48,432 bytes, Inter v20, variable
                                       100-900, latin subset
  static/fonts/Inter-LICENSE.txt       SIL OFL 1.1, as the licence requires
  progress.css                         @font-face at the top, font-display:
                                       swap, unicode-range = Google's `latin`

One variable file rather than six static instances: the stylesheet asks for
350/400/500/600/650/700/750/850/900, and six files would cost ~600KB to serve
weights one file covers. Latin only because Google's `latin` range is
U+0000-00FF plus punctuation -- every accented character an origin, a
maintainer name or a commit subject puts on this console. Past it the stack
still falls through to the system face.

DIVERGENCE, KEPT DELIBERATELY. The mock's URL is `wght@400;500;600;700;800;900`
-- a discrete list, so Google serves six STATIC instances and the mock's own
350, 650, 750 and 850 declarations snap to 400, 700, 800 and 900. Our variable
face honours them as written, so ~15 labels (the wordmark at 850, panel
headings at 650, the big numerals at 350) render marginally lighter in the
build than in the mock. Left as authored: re-rounding those 15 declarations
would reproduce an artefact of how the mock's font happens to be DELIVERED,
not a decision the design made.

VERIFIED headless Chrome against the served static tree: document.fonts
reports `Inter 100 900 loaded`, and one string measures 262.69px in Inter vs
255.92px in the fallback -- so the face is being used, not merely requested.

GUARD tests/test_font_shipped.py (7). Written general rather than
"Inter is present": every family named in --sans or --mono that no OS provides
must have an @font-face whose file exists in the static tree. Also asserts no
stylesheet or template fetches from a remote font host. Mutation-checked --
deleting the @font-face fails 3 of the 7.
close_reason: Closed

title: The context window is declared by hand when the provider already advertises it
description:
poly-qqx9.20 shipped llm.patch.context_window as the denominator for the
now-bar context gauge. It is a number an operator maintains by hand, and it
silently desyncs the moment the model is swapped -- which this deployment does
routinely (muse-spark / kimi-k3 / deepseek-v4-flash are all commented in and
out of the same config block).

THE PROVIDER ALREADY TELLS US, AND WE ALREADY ASK. runner.py:1462 calls
llm.validate_model at every startup, for both the triage and patch roles, with
the real key -- the runner is root and reads secrets/patch.key. That goes
through llm.list_models, which fetches the full model objects and then throws
everything away:

    return {m.id for m in client.models.list().data}

Many OpenAI-compatible endpoints carry a context length on those objects
(context_length, max_model_len, max_input_tokens are the spellings seen in the
wild). If this one does, the denominator is already arriving on the builder
once per runner start and being discarded.

TIER 1, ten lines: keep the object, look for a context-length field, log what
was found at startup. The operator reads one line and sets the setting once,
knowing the number. It also settles empirically whether this provider
advertises it at all, which nothing currently knows.

TIER 2, the actual fix: the runner publishes the discovered window and the
tracker uses it as the denominator, so swapping models cannot desync the
gauge. llm.patch.context_window demotes to an override for providers that
advertise nothing. The channel exists -- POST /v1/runners/presence, added by
poly-fij.12 -- and the fact is per-runner, which is the shape that endpoint
already carries.

A THIRD SOURCE, worth recording and NOT worth using alone: a context-overflow
error names the real limit in its message. That is exact but only arrives
after a failure, so it is a correction to tier 2, not a first source.

AND ONE THAT LOOKS TEMPTING AND IS WRONG: the highest prompt_tokens ever
accepted (232,509 here, over 1,837 turns) is a proven LOWER BOUND, never the
window. A ring against a watermark reads near 100% forever. Useful only to
sanity-check the other sources.

WHY THIS WAS FILED: asked for the number to put in the setting, the operator
asked why we do not get the actual context instead. The setting is a copy of a
fact the provider owns, and copies drift.
notes:
MEASURED AGAINST THE LIVE PROVIDER 2026-09-25. Meta advertises NOTHING. The
operator ran the models endpoint; the object for the configured model is the
bare OpenAI minimum:

  {"id":"muse-spark-1.3-contributor","object":"model","created":0,"owned_by":"meta"}

No context_length, no max_model_len, no max_input_tokens. So:

- TIER 1 finds nothing HERE, and tier 2s primary source does not exist for this
  provider. Neither is wasted: nvidia/NIM and deepseek are both configured in
  the same file (commented out) and NIM does publish model metadata, so the
  discovery is still worth having -- it just cannot be the only mechanism.
- llm.patch.context_window is therefore the RIGHT primary mechanism for this
  deployment, not a stopgap. poly-qqx9.20 shipping it was correct.
- THE OVERFLOW ERROR IS NOW THE ONLY AUTOMATIC SOURCE for a provider like this,
  which promotes it from "a correction to tier 2" to the main automatic route.
  It still only fires on a failure.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE THE NUMBER TODAY, one request: send a deliberately oversized
prompt and read the rejection, which states the limit. Cheap, one-off, and
exact -- a request rejected for length is normally not billed. That is also
precisely the error-capture path above, run by hand once instead of waiting for
a real job to trip it.

KNOWN BOUND meanwhile: 232,509 prompt tokens have been ACCEPTED here across
1,837 turns, so the window is at least 256k and is not 200k.
THE OVERFLOW ERROR ROUTE ALSO FAILS HERE, 2026-09-25. The operator sent a
~6M-character prompt. The provider answered:

  {"error":{"code":null,"message":"The request contains invalid parameters.
   Check the request body for any errors or inconsistencies.",
   "param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"}}

No limit named, and generic enough that it does not even confirm the LENGTH
was what it objected to. So for this provider all three automatic sources are
out: no metadata on /v1/models, no limit in the error, and a watermark is only
a lower bound.

RESOLVED FROM THE DOCUMENTATION INSTEAD. dev.meta.ai/models/muse-spark states
1M tokens and says the contributor variant does not differ; llm-stats
corroborates (1.0M in). Set on the builder as 1048576 (2^20, the usual
spelling of a 1M window), with the source and the reasoning in a comment
beside it. Backup at polytropos.toml.bak-before-context-window.

SO THIS BEAD NARROWS: discovery is still worth building for providers that
DO advertise -- nvidia/NIM and deepseek are both configured in this same file
-- but it cannot replace the setting, and for Meta the setting is the only
mechanism there is. Tier 2 (the runner publishes what it discovered) should
therefore treat the setting as an OVERRIDE that wins, not as a fallback that
loses.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH RECORDING: at a 1M window the observed peak of 232,509 is
22%, so the context ring will read green permanently on this deployment. That
is a finding rather than a disappointment -- context is not what ends attempts
here; the turn cap and the budget are (see the operators own config comment:
"Both 100-turn attempts died at exactly T100 mid-tool-call... the turn cap,
not the budget, decided when they ended"). The ring earns its place when a
smaller-window model is swapped in, and two are already parked in that config.

title: The now-bar states tokens as bare figures: no gauge, and no context fill at all
description:
Operator request 2026-09-24: the attempt line at the top should carry better
visuals for token spend, and -- since each row IS a specific attempt -- should
also show how full the context got.

WHAT IS THERE NOW. _attempt_strip.html renders a right-hand column per row:

  {{ "{:,}".format(a.billable) }}   and   {{ a.n_turns }} turns

Two bare numbers, no bar, no scale, no denominator. 869,213 beside 40,362 tells
you one attempt cost 21x the other only if you read both and divide.

TWO OF THE THREE PIECES ALREADY EXIST.

1. SPEND: attempt_turn_totals already aggregates per attempt, preferring
billable_tokens and falling back to total_tokens. Nothing new needed to draw a
bar -- only a denominator, which is the tier budget the now-bar already knows
(now.budget).

2. CONTEXT: every llm_turn row carries prompt_tokens, completion_tokens,
total_tokens, cached_tokens and billable_tokens in extra_json (tool_loop.py
emits all five). Context occupancy at a turn IS prompt_tokens. So the numerator
needs a query, not a runner change.

  peak    MAX(prompt_tokens) over the attempt
  final   the last turns prompt_tokens

They differ, and the difference is meaningful: masking old tool output
(commit a012685) SHRINKS the context mid-attempt, so a peak well above the
final value is the compaction working, and a final value near the limit is an
attempt that ran out of room. Probably worth showing peak, with final in the
title.

3. THE MISSING PIECE: THERE IS NO CONTEXT WINDOW SIZE ANYWHERE. Not in
settings.py, not in agent/llm.py, no model registry. "Fillage" has no
denominator today. It has to be declared per model -- a setting, not an
environment variable (settings: declare it, dont read the environment), and it
belongs with whatever else is per-model when poly-r1g/poly-ajd sort the
provider layer out.

THE DESIGN SOURCE ALREADY SOLVED THE SPEND HALF, elsewhere. Artifact "Five Ways
to Watch a Job" v9, specimen 04, has a budget visual in the NOW-BAR:

  .budget-top   "Billable"  "284,430 / 400,000"
  .budget-bar   8px track, .budget-fill cyan, .budget-fill.warn amber
  .budget-note  "71% of the job budget · ~40,000 per rebuild"

Reuse that treatment. Note what it implies: the design puts the budget on the
JOB in the now-bar, not per attempt in the strip, and shows NO context fill
anywhere. Both halves of this request therefore EXTEND the design rather than
implement it, and that is a deliberate divergence to record when it lands.
What was built from that specimen is text only -- _now_bar.html:28 renders
spend / budget with a title and no bar.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT MATTERS MOST -- see poly-0g0. Two quantities are already
both called "tokens" and differ by 21x on a real job (86,141 billable against
1,817,637 total on audio/cdparanoia). Context fill introduces a THIRD:
prompt_tokens, which INCLUDES the cached prefix and so moves with total, not
with billable. Putting a second number on this row without naming which
quantity it is makes poly-0g0 measurably worse rather than adding information.
Every figure here needs its name visible, not only in a title attribute.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Spend reads as a proportion at a glance, not as a number to divide.
2. Context fill is shown per attempt, against a declared window size.
3. Each figure names which quantity it is on screen -- billable, total or
   context -- without hovering.
4. A job whose model has no declared window shows spend and omits fill,
   rather than inventing a denominator.
notes:
CLARIFIED BY THE OPERATOR 2026-09-24: "improve the visuals" does NOT mean add
another number. It means a circular gauge that fills, green when ok, yellow
warning, red almost full. Sketched in the operations console mock rather than
argued in text -- artifact 6UXFSQDntZKwsrwC1rLjgM, version 12, the Job detail
view. That mock is the canonical source for this surface since poly-qqx9.10
ported specimen 06 into it.

WHAT THE SKETCH DOES
- two rings per attempt row, replacing the two bare numbers that were there
  (869,213 / "165 turns"). The row already says WHICH attempt, so the question
  the rings answer is how close to an edge it came.
- SPEND: this attempts billable against the job budget.
- CTX: the attempts PEAK prompt_tokens against the context window.
- conic-gradient ring, no library, one registered @property so the fill
  animates from zero on load; the consoles global prefers-reduced-motion rule
  already kills it.
- thresholds green < 75, amber 75-89, red >= 90. The 75 is not arbitrary for
  spend: an attempt needs a quarter of the budget still free to be worth
  starting (runner.min_attempt_budget_fraction = 0.25), so past 75% the next
  attempt cannot begin at all.

TWO CONSTRAINTS THE SKETCH HONOURS, both of which would be easy to lose.
- The percentage stays ON SCREEN, in the ring. This console never carries
  state by colour alone (tests/test_ui_quality.py, "state is never colour
  alone"), and a ring whose only signal is hue fails that. The absolute
  figures move to the title and aria-label, so the row shows FEWER numbers
  than it does today, not more.
- Each ring is captioned with the quantity it measures. Billable and total
  already differ by 21x on a real job and are both called "tokens"
  (poly-0g0); context is a THIRD quantity and tracks total, not billable. An
  uncaptioned second ring would make that confusion worse rather than adding
  information.

DIVERGENCE RESOLVED. The earlier note recorded that "Five Ways to Watch a Job"
specimen 04 draws the budget as a horizontal .budget-bar in the now-bar, and
shows no context fill anywhere. The operators call supersedes it for this
surface: rings, per attempt, both quantities. Recorded here rather than left
for someone to rediscover by comparing.

SAMPLE DATA IN THE SKETCH exercises all three colours on the context ring
(48 / 76 / 93 percent) because that is the ring that actually reaches the
edge; per-attempt spend against a job budget sits in the green on a healthy
job, which is itself the honest picture.

STILL THE BLOCKER: no context window size is declared anywhere in the
codebase, so the ctx ring has no denominator outside the mock. It has to
become a per-model setting.
PLACEMENT CORRECTED 2026-09-24, version 13 of the mock. The rings belong in
the NOW-BAR -- the "attempt 3/3 · turn 14 · ASSIST · dsynth_build · 264,110 /
400,000" line -- not on the waterfall rows. Version 12 put them on the
waterfall; that is reverted, the strip is back to billable + turns.

The now-bar is the right home for the reason this bead was filed: that line
already names the attempt and the turn, so the only thing it could not say was
how close either budget is to its edge. And it is sticky, so the answer stays
on screen while the reader is anywhere in the page.

WHAT IS THERE NOW, per ring: a 26px conic-gradient ring with the percentage
inside it, then the figures, then the quantity spelled out.

  [66] 264,110 / 400,000  BILLABLE
  [93] 186,300 / 200,000  CONTEXT

The absolute figures are KEPT rather than replaced. The operator asked for
better visuals for the numbers already on that line, not for the numbers to
go: 264,110 / 400,000 is what someone quotes, and the ring is the glance. On
the waterfall the same rings would have been a second unlabelled number per
row, which is the thing they said they did not want.

Context is the ring that actually reaches the edge -- prompt_tokens at the
newest turn, which is what the window holds right now. Billable against a tier
budget sits green on a healthy job, and that is the honest picture rather than
a dull demo.

SO THE SCOPE OF THIS BEAD IS SMALLER THAN FILED: _now_bar.html and its
context, not render/attempts.py or _attempt_strip.html. The blocker is
unchanged -- no context window size is declared anywhere, and it has to become
a per-model setting before the second ring has a denominator.
RETITLED 2026-09-24. Was "The attempt strip states tokens as bare numbers and
shows no context fill", which described where the first sketch put the gauges
rather than where they belong. The scope is the NOW-BAR. Nothing in
render/attempts.py or _attempt_strip.html is in this bead.

SCOPE, in one place so it is not spread across the notes above:
  surface    _now_bar.html and whatever feeds it
  add        two conic-gradient rings, percentage inside, figures kept beside
             them, quantity captioned -- BILLABLE and CONTEXT
  thresholds green < 75, amber 75-89, red >= 90
  sketch     artifact 6UXFSQDntZKwsrwC1rLjgM version 13, Job detail view
  blocked by poly-0g0, and by there being no declared context window size
             anywhere in the codebase
CODE READ 2026-09-24, before implementing. Five things.

1. THE REPO ALREADY HAS A CONIC-GRADIENT, BUT IT IS NOT THIS COMPONENT.
_job_token_usage.html:38 draws .token-pie, and agentic_job.html:12 carries the
rationale ("conic-gradient keeps it dependency-free -- no chart library"). That
is a PIE: three slices of a distribution summing to a total. A gauge is one
value against a CEILING. Same technique, different component; the argument for
the technique is already made and settled, so this follows it rather than
reopening it. No library either way.
