non-empty even when the attempt failed. So:

  phase 1  a finished job renders its tree from rescued/<job_id>.diff —
           already per-job, already durable, nothing new to record
  phase 2  a RUNNING job needs worker.emit_diff(env, origin, relpath), which
           needs poly-qqx9.12 for the env

PER-ATTEMPT ATTRIBUTION IS A QUERY, NOT A SCHEMA CHANGE. Once poly-qqx9.13
puts a write tool's args on its row, the attempt a file first appeared in is
the first attempt whose write-tool row names that path. attempt_loop.py:109
already defines _WRITE_TOOLS as that set. No separate bead, no new storage.
AFTER READING THE CODE (second pass):

1. BOTH PHASES SHIPPED, not just the terminal one. The notes phase this
   because phase 2 needed poly-qqx9.12 for the env -- which has since
   landed, so a running job reads worker.emit_diff(env, origin, ".") live
   and a finished one falls back to analysis/rescued/<job_id>.diff. The
   live read wins when it has anything to say: the rescued artifact is a
   snapshot of the end and a running job has moved on from it.

2. THE ATTRIBUTION QUERY WORKS AS THE NOTES PREDICTED, with one wrinkle.
   A write tool is called with whatever relative path the model chose
   ("files/patch-x", "./files/patch-x", sometimes the basename) while
   the diff carries the full in-tree path, so the match is on the tail
   rather than on equality. And _WRITE_TOOLS needed widening: the tracker
   sees tool: rows for write_file and apply_patch too.

3. A DIFF OF PATCH FILES BREAKS THE OBVIOUS PARSER. These ports' payloads
   ARE patches, so a line reading "++++ CMakeLists.txt" is an added line
   whose content starts with +++. Excluding "+++" the way a diff-header
   check would drops real content. Counting only inside a hunk is what
   makes that safe, and the file headers sit before the first @@.

4. Status comes off git's own file-mode lines, not from the hunks: a
   file whose every line changed is still M, one created empty is still
   A, and emit_diff's --intent-to-add bracket is what makes a
   never-committed payload file show as A at all.

5. The occurrence link was the smallest part and the most overdue: the
   summary card now has an Occurrence row linking job -> bundle ->
   artifact reader, beside the bundle directory it used to print as text.

render.render_diff renders every pane. No second diff renderer was
written, per the description.
close_reason: Closed

title: Attempt strip: one segmented track per attempt, so the wall clock is visible
description:
One track per attempt under the now-bar, segmented by what consumed the wall
clock, with an axis. On llvm19: two dsynth builds at 41 and 44 minutes and a
rounding error of model turns. That shape is what a reader needs first and a
reverse-chronological table cannot show it at all.

Segments by kind (model turns, fast tools, dsynth build/test, failed), the
running attempt marked as running. Clicking a segment says what it was.

Needs poly-qqx9.2: spans need a start and an end, and today only the end and
duration_ms are stored. Without it the bars would be inferring their own left
edges, which is a chart that lies.

Colour is the epic's AA-corrected palette, not the mock's raw values
(--cyan #06688c, --green #19754b, --faint #5b6874).
notes:
FROM THE AUDIT (poly-qqx9.1, third pass): the strip exists only for patch
and convert. triage, verify and confirm write no attempt_start/attempt_end
at all, so for those the strip should be ABSENT, not an empty chart.
AFTER READING THE CODE (second pass):

1. IT CANNOT BE BUILT FROM THE STREAM. poly-qqx9.5 windowed the page to
   200 rows; an attempt's start row is the only place its left edge is
   recorded and sits hundreds of rows back. Three new SQL aggregates do
   it over the whole job: attempt_boundaries, attempt_tool_totals
   (GROUP BY attempt, tool, ok with SUM(duration_ms)) and
   attempt_turn_totals.

2. MODEL TIME IS NOT MEASURED ANYWHERE. A tool row carries duration_ms;
   an llm_turn row does not -- the dispatcher never passes one. So the
   model segment is the REMAINDER, wall clock minus the tools, and it
   carries the loop's own overhead with it. The legend says exactly that
   rather than labelling it "model turns" as if it had been timed. Making
   llm_turn carry a duration would be a runner change and a separate
   bead; the remainder is honest without one.

3. THE TWO CLOCKS DISAGREE. Tool durations are measured per call; an
   attempt's span is two timestamps. The sum of the first can exceed the
   second, and it does on real data. An attempt's length is now
   max(span, measured) so the segments always fit the track -- a bar that
   runs off its own axis is a chart that lies. Both numbers are kept
   (elapsed_ms and span_ms).

4. A RUNNING ATTEMPT'S REMAINDER IS NOT THINKING TIME: the tool running
   right now has no duration until it returns, so its elapsed time is
   inside the remainder. It renders as in-progress, hatched, not as
   model time.

5. build and test needed different colours. Both are dsynth and both are
   40 minutes; one amber for both made the split invisible in the only
   place it matters. build stays amber, test takes green -- both from
   this sheet's AA-corrected palette, per the description.
close_reason: Closed

title: Show the last 5 turns and route to the full transcript, instead of fetching 500 rows
description:
The page renders the last five turns, newest first, and links out to the full
transcript grouped by attempt. At 442 events in one attempt a full stream is
the mess being replaced, and five is what fits above the working tree without
scrolling.

This makes the page CHEAPER, not dearer: agentic_job_detail currently takes
limit=500 by default (capped 5000) and renders every row it gets. Five turns
is a small LIMIT; the expensive query only runs when someone follows the link.

The full-transcript surface is the existing review view — the attempt
accordion that already groups terminal jobs — reached by a route rather than
by state, so a running job can show it too.

Measure it: today's render time for a job with a few hundred events, and the
new one. The shell_facts_seconds memo exists because the worklist band
projection measured 25.8ms per render; this page's number should be written
down the same way.
notes:
A QUEUED OPERATOR NOTE IS NOT ONE OF THE FIVE. It pins to the top of the
list until it is delivered, whatever the window holds — a note that scrolls
out of its own window before the agent has read it is the failure this
surface exists to prevent. Once delivered it takes its place in sequence and
falls out of the window like any other turn. See poly-qqx9.11.
AFTER READING THE CODE (second pass, before implementing):

1. THE FULL-TRANSCRIPT SURFACE NAMED HERE NO LONGER EXISTS. The
   description points at "the existing review view — the attempt
   accordion that already groups terminal jobs". poly-qqx9.4 deleted it:
   cards are now the reading view for both job states, and attempt
   structure is carried by boundary cards in the stream. So the
   transcript is the SAME card stream unwindowed, at its own route
   (/agentic/jobs/{job_id}/transcript) — which is what "reached by a
   route rather than by state" asked for, in the new vocabulary.

2. MEASURED FIRST, as asked. Seeded a poly-up2f-shaped job: 4 attempts x
   75 turns = 908 activity rows. Today, at the route's limit=500
   default:
       median 33.07 ms per render, 535,651 bytes of HTML
   (20 renders after 3 warm-ups, TestClient, seeded sqlite). The two
   ordinary seeded jobs (94 and ~100 events) render in 7.5 and 7.0 ms.
   The new numbers go in the same commit.

3. The route's `limit` also bounds job_events_for_job (the lifecycle
   transitions table) — lowering the default lowers both. Transitions
   are a handful of rows per job, so nothing is lost.

4. The live fragment endpoint must window IDENTICALLY, or the 3s swap
   would replace five cards with the whole stream. One constant, read by
   both call sites.

5. The queued-operator-note rule from the notes is implementable now
   even though poly-qqx9.11 has not landed: window_cards keeps any
   undelivered note card whatever the window holds. Cheaper to build the
   guard with the window than to reopen this later.

BUILT. The page shows the last five turns and links to
/agentic/jobs/{job_id}/transcript, which renders the same cards
unwindowed plus the flat table.

MEASURED, on the 908-row bench job (4 attempts x 75 turns):
    before   33.07 ms   535,651 bytes
    after     4.65 ms    50,235 bytes
    transcript 41.40 ms  917,186 bytes (paid by whoever asks for it)
7x the speed and 10x less HTML on the page an operator leaves open
while a job runs. The number lives in window_cards' docstring, the way
shell_facts carries its 25.84 ms.

Three things the measurement forced that the description did not
foresee:

- THE FLAT TABLE MOVED TO THE TRANSCRIPT. Windowing the cards alone got
  the page to 10.41 ms / 159,771 bytes -- and 78KB of that was 200 rows
  of a table inside a collapsed <details> that nobody had opened. It is
  on the transcript now, with its filter pills and row select, where the
  reader has already said they want every row. poly-qqx9.4 had put it on
  the job page; this supersedes that placement.
- THE TURN COUNT IS QUERIED, NOT COUNTED. Counting turn cards in the
  fetched window offered "all 67 turns" on a job that took 300. New
  count_llm_turns_for_job does it over the whole job.
- AN ATTEMPT_END CARD WHOSE START IS OUTSIDE THE WINDOW NO LONGER PRINTS
  ITS COUNTS. Summed over the rows in hand it read "66 turns" on an
  attempt of 75. It now says "counted in full on the transcript" and
  carries partial=True. poly-qqx9.9 is where real per-attempt figures
  come from.

Also: the route's default row budget is 200 (was 500), the transcript's
is 2000 capped at 5000, and the decision row's action/tier/
classification fields ride its stage card -- they were in the flat
table's detail cell and would have left the job page with it.

The queued-operator-note rule from the notes is implemented and tested
ahead of poly-qqx9.11: window_cards pins any card with kind="note" and
delivered falsy above the window.
close_reason: Closed

title: Turn cards replace the live flat table, with the verdict carried by a glyph
description:
Replace the live flat table with one card per model turn, full width.

Each card: the turn's id, its verdict carried by a GLYPH large enough to read
without stopping — passed / tool failed / running / attempt boundary — the
turn's tokens and timestamp, the model's own sentence, and its tool calls
nested inside as rows with name, args, elapsed and outcome. A failed tool
keeps its diagnostic open (the reject text is the interesting part); a
successful one folds. An attempt boundary is a card too, so attempt structure
stays visible without an accordion.

This component exists twice already — the console mock's session viewer
(.turn / .toolcalls / .toolresult) and the tracker's own
agentic_session.html turn cards. Reuse that vocabulary rather than inventing
a third.

Two things to carry over from the current page rather than lose: the table's
sortable token column is how a 690k-token turn gets found (poly-9hjm), so
either the cost band names the largest turn outright or the raw table stays
behind a `raw events` toggle; and 442 events in one attempt (the poly-up2f
exemplar) means cards need windowing or per-attempt paging — they are heavier
than rows.

Depends on what poly-qqx9.1 finds about the card's sentence and the tool args:
both are prose today, not fields.
notes:
Two of the cards are not model turns and share the same glyph grammar: the
ATTEMPT BOUNDARY card, and the OPERATOR NOTE card in its two states —
queued (waiting on the running tool) and delivered (stamped with the turn it
landed in). Both are full-width cards in the same stream, not a separate
lane. See poly-qqx9.11.
FROM THE AUDIT (poly-qqx9.1, third pass): THE CARD IS A PATCH/CONVERT SHAPE.
Decide the other three here rather than leaving them to be discovered.

  triage   llm_turn rows only — no tool rows, no attempts. Cards render with
           an empty tool list and no attempt grouping. Works, but check it
           does not look broken.
  verify   no turns at all. verify_fix.py has no on_event; the job's activity
           is flat operational stages (verify_branch_checkout,
           verify_complete, verify_failed, ...).
  confirm  same as verify.

So for verify/confirm the band either renders those stages as a simpler list
or says plainly that this job type has no turns. An empty 'Turns' heading on
every confirm job is the failure mode to avoid.

Also: `ok` is always present as a key on a tool row, sometimes None
(steps.py:154). None means no verdict, not failure — do not colour it red.
AFTER READING THE CODE (second pass, before implementing):

1. There is no single "live flat table" — _job_activity.html renders TWO
   views off the same rows: the live flat table (job_is_active) and, for
   terminal jobs, an attempt accordion built by
   render.group_activity_by_attempt. Cards replace BOTH. Leaving the
   accordion would give the page two vocabularies for one stream, and the
   description already says the attempt boundary is a card "so attempt
   structure stays visible without an accordion".
   Consequence: the accordion's per-attempt header (outcome, billable
   tokens, tool count) must not be lost — it moves onto the attempt_end
   boundary card. group_activity_by_attempt and its four unit tests go;
   the poly-0g0 lesson it carries (sum BILLABLE, never the re-billed
   total) moves into the new function as a comment.

2. The sortable token column is kept by keeping the table, inside a
   collapsed "raw events" <details> under the cards, for both job states.
   That satisfies the description's first carry-over without a second
   layout. The filter pills and the limit select move in there with it,
   and keep their present server-side semantics unchanged.

3. THE LIVE REFRESH CONTRACT CHANGES. Today /api/jobs/{id}/activity-
   fragment returns <tr> markup and agentic-job.js PREPENDS each row.
   A new tool row has to land INSIDE an existing card, so prepending no
   longer works. The endpoint gains cards_html (the whole rendered
   window) and the client swaps the container, keeping rows_html so the
   raw table still streams as it does now. Two guards: the endpoint
   returns changed=false when since_id has not advanced (the 3s poll
   then costs one cheap query, not a re-render), and open <details> are
   restored across the swap by data-key. The unbounded re-render is what
   poly-qqx9.5 fixes; until then the route's own limit is the bound.

4. Joining tool rows to their turn: by (extra.attempt, extra.turn), which
   both event shapes carry from the same loop variables; fall back to the
   open turn card for rows that lack them. Ordering is guaranteed —
   tool_loop emits llm_turn (line ~339) before the dispatch loop (~399).

5. The completion row does NOT carry the tool name in extra; only
   tool_start does. For a completion the name comes from the stage,
   which is "tool:<name>". Pair tool_start to completion by call_id,
   falling back to the first unfinished entry of the same name for rows
   written before poly-qqx9.2. A start with no completion IS the
   running state.

6. Triage llm_turn rows carry turn but no attempt (triage.py emits
   phase="triage"), so cards key on (None, turn) there and no boundary
   card appears. Matches what the audit found.

7. Non-turn rows (decision, observations_masked, attempt_workspace_reset,
   api_error, and every verify/confirm operational stage) render as
   compact one-line STAGE entries in the same stream rather than full
   cards. That is the answer to the empty-"Turns"-heading failure mode
   for verify/confirm: their stages read as a checklist, and patch's own
   non-turn rows stay in chronological place instead of disappearing.

NOT in this bead: the 5-turn window and the full-transcript route
(poly-qqx9.5), the segmented attempt track (.6), the working-tree band
(.7), the in-row dsynth tail (.8), the operator-note card (.11). The
card kinds are open so those attach without reshaping this.

BUILT. render.group_activity_into_cards folds the rows into three card
kinds (turn / boundary / stage); _turn_cards.html renders them; the CSS
lives in progress.css scoped under .turn-stream so the session viewer's
own inline block still owns that page.

What landed beyond the description:
- The accordion is gone. Its per-attempt header moved onto the
  attempt_end card: turns, tool calls, billable tokens, wall clock.
  group_activity_by_attempt and its four unit tests went with it.
- The raw table survives inside a collapsed "Raw events" section-collapse
  under the cards, for BOTH job states, with its sortable token column,
  filter pills and limit select intact.
- /api/jobs/{id}/activity-fragment now returns cards_html (the whole
  re-rendered window) alongside html (the new rows), plus changed=false
  when since_id has not moved so an idle poll renders nothing. The client
  swaps the card container and carries open <details> across by data-key.
- dur_ms rolls into hours above 60 minutes: an attempt's wall clock read
  "171m36s" before, which is not a number anyone parses at a glance.

Verified against specimen 06 by rendering both: a seeded live patch job
(3 attempts, 94 events, a running dsynth_test, a failed tool) and a
seeded terminal one, light and dark. The failed tool keeps its reject
text open in red with rc; the successful ones fold to one line.

Deliberate divergences from the design:
- Verdict words are 12px, not the mock's 11px: tests/test_design_tokens
  fails anything under 12px, and that floor wins over the mock.
- No per-turn duration on the card. The design showed "1.74s" but
  steps.py never passes duration_ms on an llm_turn row, so there is
  nothing to render. Tokens and timestamp only.

Still open, by design: the window. The stream renders whatever the
route's limit gives (default 500 rows), so a long job re-renders a lot
of cards on every changed poll. poly-qqx9.5 is the fix.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pinned now-bar: attempt, turn, the tool running now, and spend against the tier budget
description:
The header says `patching` and stops. The one "attempt" on the page is the
summary card's `Recent attempts 0/3 failures in last 2h`, which is
port_attempt_summary over runner.attempt_window_hours — the PORT's budget,
not this job's position. Two different things, near-identical names, and the
one an operator wants is findable only by scrolling the stream for the last
attempt_start row.

Pin one bar at the top of the page carrying: attempt n of
runner.max_patch_attempts; turn number; the tool running right now with a
ticking elapsed and its phase; and spend against the tier's budget
(policy.tier_budgets[<tier>].max_tokens — AUTO 30k, ASSIST 120k, CONVERT
150k; MANUAL never runs the agent, so a MANUAL job shows no bar rather than
a zero one).

Rename the existing row to say what it is — the port's budget over a window —
so the two stop colliding.

Where a value is genuinely absent (no tool running; a job type with no
attempts), render it absent, never as a zero. That rule is poly-0e02's, from
the farm-telemetry correction, and it applies here unchanged.
notes:
FROM THE AUDIT (poly-qqx9.1, third pass): the denominator is stored, not a
setting. attempt_start carries `iterations` alongside `budget`, and the
dispatcher persists the whole event (steps.py:139). Read N from that row —
it is the value the run actually used. runner.max_patch_attempts at render
time would misreport any job that ran under a different setting.
AFTER READING THE CODE (second pass):

1. The note is right and it matters more than it looks: attempt_start
   carries iterations AND budget AND tokens_used_so_far, so nothing in
   this bar needs a setting read at render time.

2. BUT THE PAGE CANNOT SEE THAT ROW. poly-qqx9.5 windowed the fetch to
   200 rows, and a 75-turn attempt's start row is ~375 rows back. The
   denominators come from a new query, latest_activity_extra(job, stage),
   not from the stream.

3. TWO TOKEN SCOPES THAT LOOK LIKE ONE — the real find of this bead.
   `budget` on attempt_start is tier.max_tokens, which attempt_loop
   enforces across the WHOLE JOB (its gate is budget -
   total_usage.billable_tokens, and total_usage.add runs per attempt at
   attempt_loop:613). A turn's `cumulative_billable_tokens` comes from
   tool_loop's own accumulator, created fresh at tool_loop.py:264 — so it
   counts THIS ATTEMPT only. Rendering the second against the first
   reports attempt 3's spend against the job's budget and understates by
   roughly two attempts' worth.
   The bar shows tokens_used_so_far + this attempt's cumulative. Both
   billable; the provider total re-bills the cached prefix and reads up
   to 21x high (poly-9t9).

4. Only the NEWEST turn can hold a running tool. The loop dispatches
   serially, so an older turn's call is finished by definition — and a
   runner that died mid-call leaves a tool_start with no completion
   forever, which scanning further back would report as "running" for
   all time.

5. The bar has to stream: the tool it names is the thing that changes.
   The fragment endpoint returns nowbar_html alongside cards_html, and
   the page keeps a #now-bar-slot the swap replaces.

BUILT. render/nowbar.py builds the bar, _now_bar.html renders it, and it
sticks to the top of the job page. It carries attempt n/N, turn, tier,
the tool running now with a ticking elapsed clock, and the job's billable
spend against the tier budget. The live fragment returns nowbar_html so
the tool and the clock stay current without a reload.

"Recent attempts" is now "Port retry budget", reading "1/3 failed jobs
for this port in the last 2h" -- it was never this job's attempt.

The spend scope correction (note 3 above) is the substantive change: the
bar adds tokens_used_so_far to this attempt's cumulative, because the
budget is the job's and the turn's cumulative is the attempt's.

Absent is not zero, everywhere: no tool running renders "no tool
running"; no iterations recorded renders "attempt 3" with no
denominator; no cumulative billable on any turn renders no spend cell.
A MANUAL job gets no bar; so does a job with no turns (verify, confirm).
Tested, including a template-level test that no absent value comes out
as a 0.

The elapsed clock shows two units, never three: 1h53m, 42m18s, 9s.
close_reason: Closed

title: agent notes are only readable in tool_trace.jsonl: the handoff, bundle page and Prior Attempts omit them, the activity feed clips them
description:
note(text) (poly-hnk3) records why a build failed, but the only place the
full text survives in a readable form is the next attempt's hand-over.
Everything an operator or a later job reads either clips it or omits it.

WHERE NOTES ARE TODAY

  runner.log / activity feed   tool:note rows, text clipped to 300 chars
                               (runner.py:3995)
  session page                 one-line args preview, full text only on
                               hover (agentic_session.html:216); written
                               per attempt, so nothing until one ends
  tool_trace.jsonl             full text, attempt and turn; written at
                               job end; no view renders it as notes
  retry hand-over              last 20, 500 chars each (attempt_loop.py:289)
  manual_handoff.md, patch.md,
  bundle page                  absent (manual_handoff.py:109 sections)
  later job, Prior Attempts    last 12 trace events, a note renders as
                               "tool note ok:" with no text
                               (context.py:851, 876)

OBSERVED (www/qt6-webengine, 2026-09-17)

The first job recorded 25 notes, including one per dropped patch with
the upstream reason (libevent removed, vulkan-loader gutted, ...). Those
reasons are what make its 27-file diff reviewable, and reading them
meant fetching tool_trace.jsonl and parsing JSON. Attempts 3-8 each
added a near-identical "freetype2 missing, environmental" note, so the
list also needs to show which attempt wrote what.

DESIGN

- manual_handoff.md and the bundle page get a Notes section: every note,
  full text, labelled A<attempt>.T<turn>, oldest first. It is the
  agent's own account of its choices, which is what a reviewer needs
  next to the diff.
- Prior Attempts renders a note's text instead of "tool note ok:", and
  notes do not compete for the 12 trace-event slots with tool calls.
- The activity feed keeps its one-line summary; the job page links to
  the full list.
- Identical text from consecutive attempts collapses to one entry with
  the attempts listed, in the hand-over too, so a repeated wrong
  conclusion reads as repeated rather than as five independent findings.

title: the dsynth compiler cache lives inside the env, so destroy discards it and envs cannot share one; mount it from the host like distfiles
description:
dev_env.dsynth_ccache (d514b1a, poly-dei7) points Directory_ccache at
/work/dsynth/ccache, which lives in the env's writable area
(dsynth.py:38-46). `dev-env destroy` deletes it, so every recreate starts
from a cold cache, and each env (this quarter, the next, a second
concurrent env) keeps its own. For a port like chromium that is the cost
the cache exists to avoid.

Only a directory is needed. With Directory_ccache set, dsynth adds
WITH_CCACHE_BUILD=yes and CCACHE_DIR=/ccache to each slot's make.conf and
nullfs-mounts the directory (dsynth build.c:2047, mount.c:243). The ports
framework then adds BUILD_DEPENDS on devel/ccache (Mk/bsd.ccache.mk), so
slots install ccache from dsynth's own packages. Nothing in the env root
is used.

REFERENCE

An existing dsynth bulk-build cache on another host: 5.3 GB used of a
25 GB max_size, 20.4M files, 68% hit rate, ccache 3.x stats format (the
same devel/ccache slots install). Its max_size is set in ccache.conf
inside the cache directory.

DESIGN

- dev_env.host_ccache_dir (path), next to dev_env.host_distdir
  (config.py:65). Empty keeps today's in-env directory.
- prepare_root_runtime nullfs-mounts it at <root>/work/dsynth/ccache the
  way it mounts host_distdir at usr/distfiles (runtime.py:94-97), after
  /work is mounted. Directory_ccache stays the in-chroot path; dsynth
  mounts it into slots from there, the same two-level chain distfiles
  already goes through.
- Do not write ccache.conf. The limit belongs to the operator and lives in
  the shared directory, so every env mounting it inherits it. Warn when
  the directory has no ccache.conf: ccache then defaults to 5 GB, which a
  large port outgrows.
- destroy is already safe: it unmounts everything under the env and
  refuses to delete while a mount survives (cli.py:779-786).
- Several envs writing one cache at once is fine; ccache locks its own
  files, and a hit depends on compiler and preprocessed input, not on the
  env.

title: the malformed-patch guard only checks dragonfly/patch-* names, so a hand-edited .diff a port applies itself is never validated
description:
worker.py:849. _reject_malformed_patch_write returns early unless the
basename starts with "patch-". Its docstring's reason: other files under
dragonfly/ are `file materialize` sources, not diffs, and must not be
parsed as one.

A port can ship diffs under any name and apply them itself.
misc/py-onnx (2026-09-16) staged four
dragonfly/abseil-20230125.3-*-dragonfly.diff files and applied them with
patch(1) from a post-extract script, because the abseil tree only exists
once CMake's FetchContent unpacks it.

The agent hand-edited config.diff's hunk header (edit_file at T68, T69,
T106, all ok). patch(1) rejects the result: "malformed patch at line 11".
_validate_unified_diff, run on the final file, already says so:

  hunk header '@@ -424,7 +424,7 @@' declares 7 old / 7 new line(s) but
  the body carries more (8 / 7)

The check exists; the name kept it from running.

DESIGN

Decide by content as well as name: under dragonfly/, also validate a write
named *.diff or *.patch, or whose text opens with a ---/+++ header pair.
poly-dq5 is the bar a wider match has to clear (one over-strict rule cost a
whole job), so run it across DeltaPorts' dragonfly/ trees before shipping
and count what it flags.

title: the agent cannot read a distfile the port does not extract, so it runs whole builds to print source into the log
description:
The read tools only reach /work (worker.py:209). Distfiles are in
/usr/distfiles inside the env (dev-env dsynth.py:58, 69), and make_extract
unpacks only what the port's own extract phase does.

So source a port unpacks later, during the build, cannot be read without
building. misc/py-onnx (2026-09-16): abseil-cpp 20230125.3 is a distfile
that CMake's FetchContent unpacks mid-build. To read four abseil files the
agent added temporary overlay.dops targets that print source into the
build log, then built to see it. 4 of its 11 builds (T30, T38, T44, T65)
did nothing else. A build round is the most expensive step the agent has
(poly-7ska).

DESIGN (options, not decided)

- A read-only tool that lists a port's distfiles (make -V DISTFILES) and
  reads one member (tar -xOf), windowed like get_file.
- make_extract(origin, all_distfiles=true), unpacking every distfile into a
  scratch dir under /work so get_file and grep reach it.

The second reuses the existing read tools; the first does not unpack a
large tarball to read one file.

title: a raised patch job's handoff reports the previous job's status and tokens next to its own rescued files
description:
When the harness raises, steps.py:1505-1512 writes the handoff with
patch_result=None. build_handoff_ctx then falls back to the bundle's
analysis/patch_audit.json (manual_handoff.py:314-331). A raised job never
writes one: services.write_patch_audit is on the success path
(steps.py:1529). So the audit it reads belongs to whichever earlier job on
the bundle finished, and nothing in the audit names its job.

The rest of the handoff is this job's: poly-be6o's rescue writes
changes.diff before the handoff, so Files Touched is current.

OBSERVED (misc/py-onnx, 2026-09-16)

  Reason:  patch agent gave up
  Detail:  harness raised before producing a result: Error code: 400
  Last Patch Attempt
    Status: success
    Attempts: 1
    Tokens used: 744736        <- the earlier, successful job
  Files Touched: the five abseil files this job wrote

The job that raised ran 138 turns and about 2.1M billable tokens.
analysis/patch_result.json is stale the same way.

DESIGN

With patch_result=None the step knows this job raised; do not read another
job's audit. Say the attempt raised, and take attempts and spend from this
job's trace events, which the dispatcher already holds.

RELATED
  poly-4cil    the raise path skips artifact persistence
  poly-cg6u.1  a raised attempt's spend is discarded
  poly-6e4     the handoff's token line carries no unit

title: devel/smake's dragonfly patch is authored on the slave, where DFLY_PATCHDIR cannot read it
description:
devel/smake ships `dragonfly/patch-lib_getexecpath.c`, but its DFLY_PATCHDIR
resolves to `devel/schilybase/dragonfly`, so do-patch never reads it. The
payload is authored where the build cannot see it.

Probed against the live @2026Q3 compose root, not read from Makefiles: the
static scan that first flagged this was wrong on two of the four ports it
predicted. smake is the only confirmed one.

This is an overlay in the wrong place, not a mechanism defect. The fix is to
move the file to `ports/devel/schilybase/dragonfly/`.

## Why it was held back

schilybase has a dozen-odd slaves (cdrtools, star, smake, sunpromake,
schilyutils, tartest). A patch on the master applies to all of them, so the
move must be proved by a sibling build rather than made by hand on the
strength of a probe.

poly-lt5q landed that gate: verify_fix.sibling_origins_for plus `--also`
through dev-env apply-and-build, so a master and its slaves build in one
dsynth run. What is not established is whether it works here —
poly-lt5q.1 says verify cannot compose a slave with no overlay directory,
and most schilybase slaves have none. Check that before moving the file.

## Acceptance

The patch is read during do-patch for devel/smake, and a sibling build over
schilybase and its slaves is green.

title: A running verify is invisible in the worklist: fix_status returns before it reads the job state
description:
Reported from a live instance 2026-09-13 and verified two ways.

Click Verify on an occurrence and the job runs for minutes. The worklist row does not change at all -- it stays 'agent fixed - verify' in the Needs verify band, indistinguishable from one nobody has touched. The only trace anywhere in the queue is the ops strip's global 'Runner: N in flight', which does not name the port.

MECHANISM

fix_status() reads (resolution, verification_status, job.state) and its FIRST branch is:

    if r == RESOLUTION_AGENT_FIXED:
        if v == VERIFIED:            return verified
        if v == VERIFICATION_FAILED: return verify_failed
        return FixStatus('needs_review', 'agent fixed - verify', 'built')

It returns before ever reaching the job-state check, which is only reachable in the 'resolution is NULL' branch further down. So for an agent_fixed bundle a running verify can never change the status. The data is already there -- _OCCURRENCE_JOB_STATE puts the newest job's state on every occurrence row -- it is simply never consulted on this path.

MEASURED on the running demo, same row through three states:

  before the request:      band=verify  pills=['agent fixed - verify x2', 'seen x2']
  request pending:         band=verify  pills=['agent fixed - verify x2', 'seen x2']
  job state=verifying_fix: band=verify  pills=['agent fixed - verify x2', 'seen x2']

Byte-identical throughout.

ACCEPT IS FINE, contrary to the report: accept writes resolution='accepted' synchronously, so the row moves ready -> confirming with the pill 'confirm build queued' on the next render. Checked.

FIX

fix_state already owns this question. verify_state() reconciles a verify from the request's status, the job's state and whether verification_at postdates the request, and it already has VERIFY_QUEUED ('verify queued') and VERIFY_RUNNING ('verifying'). The worklist must not invent a second notion of 'a verify is happening' -- it should reach the same answer with the same words.
acceptance_criteria: An occurrence with a verify in flight reads differently in the queue from one that has not been asked for, using verify_state's own vocabulary. A request the runner has not picked up is also distinguishable, because if the runner is down that verify will never run and the queue should not look identical either way. The row stays findable.
notes:
Fixed 2026-09-13. Five distinct states where there was one.

fix_status's agent_fixed branch now consults, before falling through to needs_review: the job state already on the occurrence row (in-flight -> 'verifying'), then the newest verify request's status ('pending' -> 'verify queued'). Both labels are verify_state's own words, so the queue and the workspace cannot describe the same verify differently -- that projection owns the reconciliation and this only has to agree with it.

The job state needed no query change; it was already there as job_state and simply never read on this path. The request status is one new correlated subselect on _OCCURRENCE_SELECT, the same one-indexed-lookup-per-row shape as the job state beside it.

BUCKETING: both stay in the verify lane rather than going to bucket None the way in_progress does. Hiding them is defensible -- a job holds it, nothing to decide -- but build_issue_worklist DROPS a bucket-None issue entirely, so the port you just clicked Verify on would vanish from the queue and from a filter search for it. Being unable to find what you just acted on is worse than a band label that is a shade too strong. Flip it by mapping the two keys to None if that trade reads the other way.

MEASURED end to end on the running demo, a single-occurrence issue so the band moves cleanly:

  1. untouched        band=verify (Needs verify)      ['agent fixed - verify']
  2. Verify clicked   band=verify (Needs verify)      ['verify queued']
  3. job running      band=verify (Needs verify)      ['verifying']
  4. verify passed    band=ready  (Ready to accept)   ['verified']

A finished verification still beats a stale job row -- checked both ways -- because the result posts back to the bundle and the verification branches come first.

The operator guide's chapter 6 picked both up on its own, which is what generating it from the projection was for. _MATRIX_CASES became dicts to carry the new field.

7 tests in test_repairs_view.py, including the end-to-end walk.
close_reason: Closed

title: The .control button does not centre its own text, so every link-shaped control is top-aligned
description:
Reported from a live instance 2026-09-13: 'Open issue' and 'Port history' in the occurrence workspace have their text jammed against the top edge of the button.

Measured in a real browser at 1600x1000, on .repair-detail .heading-actions .control:

  box=32.0  textH=16.0  gapAbove=-1.0  gapBelow=17.0

The text overlaps the top border and there are 17px of empty box below it.

MECHANISM

.control sets 'min-height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; font: 500 13px/1' and NO display and no vertical centring. On a <button> the UA centres the content, so it looks right. On anything else the box is 32px tall because min-height applies (flex containers like .heading-actions blockify their children) while the line box is 13px and sits at the top.

Every other control class in the sheet already does this correctly -- .action, .section-nav a and .result-filter are all 'display: inline-flex; align-items: center'. .control is the one that was missed, and it is the one used on anchors.

WHERE IT SHOWS

Anywhere .control is on something that is not a <button>:
- _cockpit.html: 'Open issue', 'Port history'
- _list_controls.html: 'Clear', 'Previous', 'Next'
- agentic_compare.html: the two 'Open <bundle>' links

ALSO AN ACCESSIBILITY BUG

The coarse-pointer block raises '.action, .control, .btn' to min-height 40px for touch. Without a display that centres, that just makes the dead space below the text taller -- the tap target grows but the thing that looks tappable does not.
acceptance_criteria: A .control renders identically whether it is an <a> or a <button>: same height, text centred. Selects and text inputs keep their own box model. A test asserts the centring rather than the height.
notes:
Fixed 2026-09-13, measured both ways in a real browser.

.control gains 'display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center', plus text-decoration:none and white-space:nowrap since it is worn by anchors. select.control / input.control / textarea.control opt back out to inline-block, because a select keeps its native arrow and an input centres its own value -- neither wants to be a flex container.

  BEFORE  box=32.0 textH=16.0 gapAbove=-1.0 gapBelow=17.0   (text on the top border)
  AFTER   box=32.0 textH=16.0 gapAbove=7.5  gapBelow=8.5    CENTRED

Swept .control/.action/.btn/.wl-btn across /agentic/issues, /agentic/bundles, /agentic/compare and /builds looking for any label whose gap above and below differ by more than 1.5px: none left.

ALSO FIXED, latent: .cockpit-tab had the same shape -- min-height: 36px with nothing centring inside it. It is only ever a <button> today so the UA was hiding it, which is exactly how .control survived until an <a> wore it.

The guard is in test_ui_quality.py and is parameterised over the five classes that draw a button, asserting each centres its own label rather than asserting a height. The old failure mode was invisible to every test in the suite because the height was right and only the text inside it was wrong.
close_reason: Closed

title: The Repairs work queue drifted from the mock: no filter, rows 2x too tall, a per-row button the mock does not have
description:
Measured against the mock at 500 issues (the tracker's own _WORKLIST_CAP) on 2026-09-13. The shipped rail shows 3 issues per screen at 1600x1000; the mock shows 9.

WHAT THE MOCK SPECIFIES AND THE RAIL DOES NOT

- .repair-search, a full-width filter over origin and fingerprint, directly under the queue heading. The rail has no filter at all; agentic_index passes no q and issues_with_occurrences' search= is never used from this page. Finding a port means scrolling.
- Band chips FILTER the list (data-band, repState.band). The rail's chips are #wl-<band> anchors that jump within the scroll container, so every band stays rendered.
- .repair-item is two compact lines, ~67px: origin + age on top, then status pill, times_seen, systemic/regressed, target. The rail's .wl-row is ~132px because at 372px it trips the same collapse the 760px phone breakpoint uses, stacking rollup, mid and actions onto separate lines.
- No per-row action button. The row is a selector; Verify/Accept/Reject/Retry live in .repair-actions, a bar pinned to the bottom of the detail pane and always in view. The rail puts a per-band action button on every row, and it is a link to ?occ=, so it names an action it does not perform.
- .repair-band is a thin uppercase strip with a count. The rail uses an h2 plus a bordered card per band.
- The queue is 352px and carries nothing but the queue. The rail is 372px and also carries Resolved, Muted, an h2 'Environment health' with a six-column table, and drill-down links -- below the whole queue.

At 500 issues with a per-row button added to the mock, origins truncate (textproc/xorg-serv...) and rows with a longer meta line wrap to a third line. The button costs the row its identity.
design: Mock: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2c556aa9-ed25-499f-b88d-64b86272aa9a -- the published version now carries two footer switches, 'queue at 500' and 'show row buttons', so the queue can be read at the real cap and with/without a per-row action.
acceptance_criteria: The queue filters. Rows fit one issue in ~67px. Band chips narrow the list rather than jumping to it. Environment health is not inside the queue's scroll column. Whatever the row's action affordance ends up being, it does not name an action it cannot perform.
notes:
Implemented 2026-09-13. Five of the six divergences closed; the sixth is deliberate and recorded below.

- FILTER. agentic_index takes q, passes it to issues_with_occurrences(search=) and count_issues(search=), which already supported it and were never called with it from this page. A plain GET form, so it works with no JS and the result is a URL. Matches origin, issue_key and fingerprint.
- BAND CHIPS FILTER. agentic_index takes band; the chips are links built with the existing _query_for helper rather than #wl-<band> anchors. Every chip keeps its own count while one is selected, because the chips are the only place the other bands are visible. An unknown band falls back to the whole queue rather than erroring.
- ROW HEIGHT. ~132px to ~66px, measured at 420px. The row is two lines: the port alone on the first with its age and the action, state on the second. The old five-track grid collapsed in a narrow rail into four stacked lines, and that collapse rule is gone -- the row is compact at every width now, so the 760px phone override went with it.
- NO PER-BAND VERB. One 'Review ->' on every row. wl-btn-accept / -verify / -decide / -take are deleted; wl-btn-review replaces them.
- ENV HEALTH. The h2, the table and the active-env picker moved to /agentic/runner, whose lede already explains that the runner pauses itself on a broken env. The queue keeps the one-line glance, because a broken env is why the queue is not moving, and it now links to the runner page.
- RAIL WIDTH. 372px -> 420px.

NOT DONE, and it is the load-bearing one: the queue still expands a multi-occurrence issue into child rows, which the mock does not have -- there, occurrences live in the detail pane's occurrence bar. Closing that would delete the group/child structure poly-x3pg.6 just fixed, and it changes where an operator picks which occurrence to act on. Filed separately rather than folded in here.

Two things found while measuring that the bead did not predict: the rollup pill and times_seen both render as 'xN' and sat adjacent on the new line two, reading as a duplicated number -- times_seen is now labelled 'seen xN'. And a badge that wraps inside itself costs the row a third line, so wl-x and wl-recur are flex:none/nowrap and the port name absorbs the squeeze instead.

title: hooks-status prints every installed hook as 'x' and exits 0 when all of them are stale
description:
hooks-status detects staleness correctly and then reports it in two ways
that read as "fine". Found by a sonnet agent following a deploy runbook: it
had to consciously override what the output looked like and trust the
summary line instead.

1. EVERY PRESENT HOOK PRINTS AS `x`

hooks.py:312-316

    for name in info["present"]:
        marker = " (stale: source is newer)" if name in info["stale"] else ""
        print(f"  x  {name}{marker}")
    ...
    print(f"  {'✓' if info['conf_present'] else 'missing:'} {CONF_TARGET}")

So `x` means installed, and `✓` -- used four lines later, in the same block,
for the same meaning -- means present too. A reader sees nine `x` rows and
one `✓` and concludes nine things are broken and one is fine. It is the
exact inverse.

2. THE EXIT CODE IGNORES STALENESS

hooks.py:324

    return 0 if missing == 0 else 1

Nine of nine stale exits 0. Anything gating on `$?` -- a deploy script, a
CI step, an agent runbook -- sails straight past a fully stale env. This is
not hypothetical: acemagic was in exactly that state after the 2026-09-10
upgrade, 9 installed / 0 missing / 9 stale, exit 0.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN COSMETICS

poly-440 concludes the remedy is informational because "detection already
exists (hooks-status, which computes staleness by mtime)". It does compute
it. It then presents it as a pass. So the documentation fix that bead asks
for lands an operator on a command whose output argues against the thing
the documentation just told them to look for.

The hooks are the whole bundle-raising protocol -- bundle id, log distill,
blob upload, job enqueue -- on the path between a failing build and a job
existing at all. A stale set speaks the old protocol silently.

FIX DIRECTION

- Give present-and-current a `✓`, stale its own marker, missing an `x`.
  One symbol per state, and the conventional polarity.
- Decide what the exit code means and say so in --help. Either non-zero on
  stale (a gate), or document that it is presence-only and that staleness
  is summary-line-only. Silent 0 is the one option that cannot be relied on.
- Whichever way: a caller must be able to answer "is this env current?"
  without parsing prose.

title: Job view: long tables render at full volume, poor visibility
description:
The job view (/agentic/jobs/{job_id}) renders everything at full volume with
equal weight. An escalated patch job (devel/libcxx22, 442 activity events)
renders ~25,000px tall at 1440px wide. Investigated 2026-09-09 with headless
Chrome screenshots against a live tracker.

Findings:

1. Manual handoff dumps the whole artifact inline (agentic_job.html): the
   pkg-plist diff and the failing-build tail render as hundreds of open lines
   before the transitions/activity sections. The operator-facing prose
   (Reason, Detail, Triage, Suggested Fix, Operator Question) is ~15 lines.
2. Timestamps are 33 chars (2026-09-08T22:56:00.894306+00:00) in the first
   column of every table; microseconds+offset are noise at reading time.
3. Lifecycle transitions: the raw dict dump in Detail starves the other
   columns, so Event/From/To/Actor wrap mid-word ("hook_enq ueued",
   "queu ed", "runne r").
4. Activity Message column: dominant row type is tool:grep with a long
   pattern; the 240-char expand threshold in _activity_row.html misses most
   of them, so patterns dominate the table.
5. Four numeric token columns per llm_turn row (Prompt/Compl/Total/Cum);
   per-row values rarely matter and the aggregate lives in the Token usage
   card.
6. The default-open attempt group renders all its rows (442 here); the
   stage-filter pills exist only in the live view, not the review view.
7. No wayfinding: no sticky table headers, no jump links, on a 25k-px page.

Task (roughly in payoff order):

- Collapse handoff bulk: put Changes Diff + Last Failing Build behind
  <details> or cap at max-height ~300px with overflow:auto (same shape as
  .tool-diagnostic pre).
- Short timestamps: render HH:MM:SS with full value in title=, date printed
  only when it changes between rows. Applies to activity + transitions
  tables (and the JS-rendered live rows in agentic-job.js must match).
- Transitions table: nowrap the narrow columns; render Detail as key=value
  lines dropping keys already in the summary card (path, bundle_id).
- Tool-row messages: one-line ellipsis clamp with expand; indent tool rows
  under their llm_turn.
- Token columns: keep Total + Cum, drop Prompt/Compl to hover/expand; give
  Total a proportional background bar scaled to the largest turn.
- Attempt groups: default-open shows last ~30 events with a "show all N"
  expander; add stage-filter pills to the review view.
- Wayfinding: sticky thead on activity tables; jump-link row under the h1
  (Summary / Handoff / Transitions / Activity / Tokens / Prior attempts) —
  .section-nav in progress.css looks reusable.

Files: dportsv3/tracker/templates/agentic_job.html, _job_activity.html,
_activity_row.html, _job_summary.html; dportsv3/tracker/static/progress.css,
agentic-job.js. Live rows are rendered client-side to match the server
render, so _activity_row.html changes need the agentic-job.js twin updated.

Secondary (jobs list, may split out): the job-id column repeats
Type/Origin/Target/Created; a shorter display label would tighten the table.

Implemented on master (uncommitted, pending review). All seven items landed:

nowrap + key=value detail rendering, tool-row one-line clamp + indent, token
columns 4->2 with 200k-scaled background bar, attempt fold to last 30 with

Contract change: data-sort prompt/completion dropped; the split moved to the
Tokens cell title. test_tracker_job_filter_sort.py updated to pin the new

Jobs-list job-id duplication remains open (secondary note in description).
Re-review (partial: 3 of 6 verifiers survived an API session limit, all

review-view filter pill now reveals every fold first, since the toggle's

REVIEWED 2026-09-22. Closed.

CORRECTION to the first line of these notes: not uncommitted. Two commits

  47f8ee0 tracker: job view visibility rework (poly-up2f)

title: Delivery: an accepted fix reaches a PR, or says why not
description:
Accept commits a decision and performs a side effect in one action, and
every failure mode of the side effect is either invisible or unrecoverable.
Five beads, no parent. Measured 2026-09-04: 17 bundles whose newest
bundle_review_requests row is create_failed are all bundles.resolved.

            run again
  poly-8e2  the issue reads 'resolved' anyway, and no view shows the gap
