title: A harness exception early-returns before artifact persistence, so changes.diff/patch.md/tool_trace are lost for attempts that did real work
description:
steps.py, patch step. When the harness raises, the handler writes the
handoff and returns immediately (steps.py:1283-1301):

    outcome = _err(str(exc), ..., JobEvent.PATCH_GAVE_UP, transient=...)
    if not outcome.detail.get("requeued"):
        _try_write_handoff(..., patch_result=None)
    return outcome

Everything that persists the attempt's output sits BELOW that return:

    ctx.state["patch_result"] = result
    ctx.state["trace_events"] = list(dispatcher.trace_events)
    services.write_patch_audit(...)          # patch_audit.json
    ...                                      # patch.md, changes.diff,
                                             # rebuild_proof.json,
                                             # tool_trace.jsonl

So a bundle that dies on an API error keeps only triage.md,
triage_result.json, manual_handoff.md and the session dumps. The session
dumps survive because they are written per-attempt during the run, not at
the end.

OBSERVED

1. x11_libinput-20260831-003435Z -- API 500, 0 attempts. Nothing to save;
   correct behaviour by accident.

2. www_firefox-20260908-091737Z -- API 400 during attempt 3, after TWO
   completed attempts (~1.9M billable). Lost: changes.diff, patch.md,
   patch_audit.json, rebuild_proof.json, tool_trace.jsonl.

   The second case is the argument. Attempt 2 had reached a correct,
   verified root cause (that firefox's set_define mechanism cannot
   override libc++'s unconditional _LIBCPP_HIDE_FROM_ABI), written ~30
   lines of analysis into overlay.dops, and deliberately un-materialized a
   patch it had proved could not work. All of it was discarded by the
   post-job workspace reset with no diff captured.

   It was recoverable only because the agent had happened to call
   emit_diff, whose tool result is embedded in the session dump. Had it
   not, 1.9M of reasoning would have been unrecoverable.

Note the give-up path is also reached for non-harness give-ups, which DO
get changes.diff (devel/gn, net/vde2, math/dune-common all have it). The
gap is specific to the raise path.
design:
changes.diff does not depend on the harness result. Per steps.py:1345 it is
branch-vs-base -- a git operation against the env's DeltaPorts checkout. It
can be produced whether or not `result` exists.

Minimal fix: on the raise path, before returning, capture what does not
need `result`:

  - changes.diff  (git, always available)
  - tool_trace.jsonl from dispatcher.trace_events, which is already
    populated at that point -- the line below the return reads
    `list(dispatcher.trace_events)`.

patch.md, patch_audit.json and rebuild_proof.json genuinely need `result`
and should stay skipped. A short marker in manual_handoff.md saying which
artifacts are absent and why would save the next reader guessing.

Also worth considering: the workspace reset that follows (steps.py:1371,
"changes.diff is the canonical ...") discards the env state. If
changes.diff cannot be captured for some reason, the reset should be the
thing that is skipped, not the capture -- an un-reset env is recoverable
by hand, a reset one is not.

RELATED

Two API failures in three days (a 500 on 2026-08-31, a 400 on 2026-09-08)
suggests this path is reached often enough to matter. The 400's message
was "The request contains invalid parameters", which may itself be worth
investigating -- a malformed request built by the harness rather than a
provider fault.

title: min_attempt_budget_fraction caps attempts at 1/frac regardless of max_tokens, so max_iterations above 4 is unreachable and silently misleading
description:
attempt_loop gates each retry on a floor that is a FRACTION of the budget,
not a constant (attempt_loop.py:92):

    def _min_attempt_budget(budget: int) -> int:
        frac = float(settings.get("runner.min_attempt_budget_fraction"))
        return int(budget * frac)

and gates at attempt_loop.py:462:

    if budget and attempt_idx > 1 and remaining < _min_attempt_budget(budget):

runner.min_attempt_budget_fraction defaults to 0.25 (settings.py:313).

CONSEQUENCE

Because the floor scales with the budget, the reachable attempt count is
1/frac and is INDEPENDENT of max_tokens. At 0.25 an attempt can start with
100%, 75%, 50% or 25% remaining -- four, and never more, whatever the
pool. Raising max_tokens buys longer attempts, not more of them.

policy.tiers.ASSIST ships max_iterations=4 (settings.py:512), which
matches. But nothing prevents configuring more, and the live config here
was set to max_iterations=8 for www/firefox on the assumption that a
larger pool would buy more retries. It could never have reached attempt 5.

OBSERVED

  1M budget,  floor 250,000    "not starting attempt 3 - 141931 billable
                                left is below the 250000 floor"
  600k budget, floor 150,000   "not starting attempt 3 - 43058 billable
                                left is below the 150000 floor"
  5M budget,  floor 1,250,000  run 4 ended after 1 attempt of 281 turns;
                               no attempt 2 was possible below 1.25M.

The log line is accurate and useful. What is missing is any indication at
configuration time that max_iterations > 1/frac is inert.

The floor itself is well-reasoned -- the message says spending the
remainder "would re-derive context rather than finish the work", which is
right, and attempt 1 is correctly never gated.
design:
Cheapest useful fix: validate at config-check time. `dportsv3 config check`
already reads both values and could say

    policy.tiers.ASSIST.max_iterations = 8 exceeds the 4 attempts
    reachable at runner.min_attempt_budget_fraction = 0.25

Alternatively document the relationship on both settings -- the
min_attempt_budget_fraction help text ("A retry needs this fraction of the
budget still available to be worth starting") does not mention that it
therefore bounds the attempt count.

Worth deciding separately: whether the intended knob for "more retries" is
lowering the fraction rather than raising the budget. On a long porting
run, several short attempts may beat two long ones -- each attempt resets
the context, which is currently the only compaction that exists (see
poly-hnk3). At 0.10 the same pool would allow ten attempts.

Not proposing a default change here; the current value is defensible. The
bug is that the interaction is invisible until you read attempt_loop.

title: The tracker UI rewrite is undocumented: no doc names Pipeline, Repairs or repair-identifiers
description:
Branch tracker-ui-migration is 44 commits, 139 files, +16003/-2329, and
changes nothing under docs/.

What is now unwritten:

- The three views. grep over docs/*.md for "Repairs", "Pipeline" or
  "/pipeline" finds nothing. docs/agentic-operator-loop.md and
  OPERATOR_SETUP.md describe an operator loop that no longer matches the
  screens it is describing.
- `dportsv3 tracker repair-identifiers [--apply]`. The docs list the
  older subcommands (serve, failures, diff, compare-builds,
  record-result, finish-build); this one is new and is the documented
  remedy the server prints at startup when it finds a legacy id.
- Three settings: tracker.shell_facts_seconds (15),
  tracker.preflight_refresh_seconds (300),
  tracker.runner_heartbeat_stale_seconds (60). All have defaults, so no
  install needs editing -- but `config show` is now the only place they
  are explained.

Not a blocker for merging: every default is right and the UI is
self-describing. It is a blocker for anyone but the author operating it.

Smallest useful version: one operator-facing page that names the three
views and what each answers, plus the repair command in whatever doc
already lists tracker subcommands. Not a rewrite of the loop docs.
notes:
Implemented 2026-09-13, the bead's 'smallest useful version'. Re-checked against the tree first: all three gaps were still open. No doc named Repairs or the Pipeline view (the one grep hit in v3-refactor.md is a filename, compose/pipeline.py); repair-identifiers appeared nowhere under docs/; and none of the three settings appeared outside settings.py.

- docs/tracker-ui.md (new). Names the three views, what each answers, and which route serves it, with each view's secondary destinations. Deliberately short: the six-chapter guide shipped by poly-9u7 explains the MODEL from inside the UI, so this page's job is to say the views exist and point at it, not to re-explain issues versus occurrences in prose nobody opens.
- docs/dportsv3-user-guide.md gains repair-identifiers in the tracker subcommand list, with the note that the reporting form comes first, and its dashboard-pages section now names the three views and links the new page instead of listing only the build-side routes.
- docs/OPERATOR_SETUP.md's 'with hooks live, watch' list gains /agentic, and points at the new page and the ? guide. That is the doc an operator reads while standing up a box, so it is where the pointer earns its place.
- The three settings are in a table with their defaults and what each one costs, which is what config show could not say.

Not done, and the bead says not to: no rewrite of agentic-operator-loop.md or AGENTIC_BUILDS.md. The new page says explicitly that it describes the screens and those describe the loop.
close_reason: Closed

title: An epic with a design source should name it, and closing should require the comparison
description:
poly-0e02 shipped all 22 planned children and did not look like the mock
it was drawn from. Two of its three views were different applications:
Pipeline was six cards where the design is a flow with a feedback loop
and a drawer, and Repairs was two pages where the design never leaves
one. Fixing it took a second epic (poly-x3pg) and five more beads.

WHY IT GOT THAT FAR

The children described CONTENT AND BEHAVIOUR and never layout. UI-1 said
"shell, primary nav, per-view secondary nav, breadcrumbs", which
describes a document; the design is a fixed-viewport application with a
status rail. UI-6 listed the cockpit's contents and even specified the
occurrence selector as "a collapsible list, not a horizontal card strip"
-- built correctly -- but never said it sits in the right pane of a
split. UI-4 said six stages and "must not read as one row advancing
through six linear states", and the implementer read that as a
prohibition and deleted the diagram the sentence was captioning.

Every child was built faithfully. The beads had already dropped the
design's structural ideas without recording that they were dropping
anything, and nothing downstream could notice: the audits measured
contrast, overflow, landmarks, touch targets and empty states across 26
pages, and not one of them ever opened the design.

WHAT TO CHANGE

Two things, both cheap.

1. An epic that is built from a design names it -- URL and version -- in
   its description. poly-0e02 did not, which is why the mock was found by
   asking rather than by reading the board, and why the version I
   analysed may not be the current one.

2. Closing such an epic requires a side-by-side. Render the design and
   the built views at the same width and put them next to each other.
   It took about ten minutes with headless Chrome and a two-column HTML
   page; it would have caught this after Phase 2.

Worth considering and NOT obviously right: making the comparison
automatic. A screenshot diff would be noisy -- sample data differs, and
every deliberate divergence would light up forever. The value here came
from a human reading two pictures, so the requirement is to produce the
pictures, not to assert on them.

ALSO WORTH RECORDING

Where the built views and the design still differ, every difference is
now a decision with a measurement or a bead behind it, listed in each
poly-x3pg child's close note. That is the shape the divergences should
have been in from the start: not absent, but written down.
notes:
Implemented 2026-09-13. Both changes, plus the correction the bead's own premise needed.

CORRECTION: 'poly-0e02 did not [name its design source]' is not quite right -- the URL WAS in a REFERENCES block at the foot of its description. What it lacked was the VERSION, which is the half that matters: without it, 'does this still match?' cannot be answered later because the source moves. And it did move: the artifact was republished 2026-09-13. Both epics now record which version they were built from and which version to compare against now.

1. CLAUDE.md gains 'Built from a design? Name it, and compare before closing'. URL and version with the date, in the description rather than a footnote; the side-by-side at the same width as a closing requirement; produce the pictures and do not assert on them, for the reason the bead gives -- sample data differs and every deliberate divergence would light up forever; and a surviving divergence is a decision that gets written down with its measurement.

It carries poly-0e02's failure as the argument. A rule with no evidence behind it reads as ceremony and gets skipped.

2. Applied to both epics as notes: poly-0e02 says it was built from the 2026-09-05 version, poly-x3pg says it measured against that version on 2026-09-07, and both say the artifact is now at 2026-09-13.

EVIDENCE IT WORKS, from today: doing exactly this comparison for Repairs -- rendering the mock at the tracker's real 500-issue cap beside the built queue -- produced six divergences. Five were defects (no filter, band chips that jumped instead of narrowing, rows at 132px against 67px, a per-band button naming an action it could not perform, an env-health table inside the queue's scroll column) and are fixed in poly-x3pg.7. The sixth is a real design decision and is now poly-x3pg.8 rather than an accident. The switches that made the comparison possible were added to the artifact itself, so the next person can repeat it.

STILL OWED: Pipeline has not had the side-by-side. poly-x3pg cannot close until it does, and its note now says so.
close_reason: Closed

title: M4 Repairs is two pages where the mock never leaves one
description:
The biggest interaction gap. In the mock you pick an issue on the left
and work it on the right, and both are on screen the whole time. We
navigate: /agentic is the worklist, /agentic/bundles/<id> is the
cockpit, and you lose the queue to get to the work.

WHAT THE MOCK HAS

  .view[data-layout="cockpit"] {
    grid-template-columns: 352px minmax(650px, 1fr);
    grid-template-rows: 43px minmax(0,1fr); }

A 352px .repair-queue rail and a .repair-detail pane, side by side under
one section nav.

The rail:
* .repair-head -- an overline ("10 need you" for an operator, "14 open"
  for a reader), h1 ("Work queue" / "Repairs"), one line of prose. Both
  strings change with audience.
* .repair-search -- filter by origin or fingerprint, 42px, full width,
  inset cyan underline on focus.
* .band-chips -- All + one per band with its count, zero bands greyed.
  Chips FILTER the list rather than jumping to an anchor.
* .repair-list -- .repair-band headers, then .repair-item rows: a 9px
  diamond signal (rotate(45deg), coloured per band -- green ready, amber
  verify, red decide, cyan owned, faint done), origin in mono, age
  right, then a meta line of pills.

The detail:
* .repair-detail-head -- .repair-overline ("ISSUE i-7f2a91c4
  PATCH-ERROR:CONFIGURE:LDFLAGS" + state pill), .repair-title (750 23px
  mono) with a target pill, a prose summary, then .issue-facts:
  Seen x4 / First / Last / From build #1842 / Port history all runs.
* .occ-bar -- the occurrence selector, collapsed to one line
  ("OCCURRENCES · 4  b-9a41  09-05 03:00 · verified · reached rebuild
  green   CHANGE v") expanding to .occ-list. We built this; it matches.
* .repair-tabs -- Fix / Evidence / Chat / History. We built these.
* .repair-content -- .repair-grid, a 1.35fr/0.65fr split: the artifact
  on the left, stacked fact panels on the right (Why this is open /
  Verification / Occurrence).
* .repair-actions -- a 62px bar pinned at the bottom of the pane:
  a status line on the left, then Verify / Accept / Reject / Take over /
  Retry / Discard from the projection. Accept renders disabled with a
  title when verification is not verified, rather than being absent.

Section nav is Work Queue | Issues, context "Issue is the unit ·
bundles are occurrences". Ours is Worklist | Issues | Occurrences,
context "Repair workspace".

ANONYMOUS, which the mock handles better than we do

  .repair-actions.anon replaces the whole bar with:
  "Operator actions hidden -- Accept, reject, retry, take over and
   discard need an operator session."

The comment above it is the design rule: "The action surface is ONE
separable region, never interleaved with status -- that is what makes it
omittable." We satisfy the rule (poly-0e02.12) but say nothing, so a
reader sees a page with a hole in it.

WHAT TO BUILD

The split. The rail is the worklist we already render, narrowed and
given chips that filter instead of anchoring. The detail is the cockpit
we already built (poly-c9ir), moved into the right pane and given the
fact-panel column and the pinned action bar.

Selection is a URL, /agentic?issue=<key>&occ=<id>&tab=fix, so it is
linkable and survives a reload; without JS every rail row is a link that
reloads the page with the right pane filled in. The tabs already work
that way.

Keep /agentic/bundles/<id> working. It is linked from Builds, from the
pipeline drawer and from anywhere else that knows a bundle and not an
issue; it should redirect into the split with that occurrence selected.

CONSTRAINTS

Below 760px the split has to become one column -- the mock's own media
block does this and the rail moves above the detail. UI-7 stands: one
<main> around the pair, the skip link ahead of both, the rail is a
scrolling region with its own overflow, and the audit reruns at
1440/500/coarse.

The action surface stays whatever fix_state.bundle_actions() and
issue_state.issue_actions() return. Do not reimplement the gating to
match the mock's hardcoded sample; the mock shows Accept disabled with a
title, which IS an improvement on hiding it, and that part is worth
copying.
close_reason: Committed. /agentic is the split: queue rail plus the selected occurrence's workspace, both on screen, selection carried in the URL (?occ= or ?issue=) so it is linkable and needs no JS. The cockpit is one partial and one context builder, rendered by both the split and the standalone page, which is kept because Builds, the pipeline drawer and every deep link point at it. Arriving with no selection fills the pane from the queue's first row; an empty tracker collapses the split; a stale ?occ= lands on the queue rather than 404ing. The anonymous pane now names the five hidden actions instead of leaving a hole. 17 tests; audited 1440/500/coarse seeded and blank, 0 findings. Caught in review: two h1 on the split, and .occ-h1 defined in a <style> the split does not include.

title: M3 A pipeline count links away where the mock opens the rows in place
description:
UI-4 made every count a link to a filtered list page, reasoning that a count with no way through to its rows is an assertion nobody can check. The mock answers the same objection without leaving the page. WHAT THE MOCK HAS .pipeline-drawer below the flow: a 51px .drawer-head and a scrolling body. Selecting a node repaints it. The head carries three things:

Issues

14 fingerprints ... source: issues_with_occurrences() That right-hand label is the point. Each node declares the query behind it -- list_bundles(limit=200), issues_with_occurrences(), list_jobs(), build_issue_worklist(), open_delivery_bundle_ids(), "issues WHERE state='resolved'" -- and the drawer prints it. UI-4's bead said "every number needs a named real query"; the mock puts the name on the screen. Per node the body is: * failures -- bundles: Bundle / Origin / Target / Recorded / State, each routing to that occurrence's Fix tab. * issues -- the shared issues table. * automation-- the shared jobs table. * operator -- TWO panels: worklist bands (band, count, "open queue ->" per row) and open manual escalations. * delivery -- Issue / Origin / Provider / Pull request / Status. * outcome -- Issue / Origin / Resolved / Proven by (the confirm build, linked) / State. WHAT TO BUILD The drawer, driven by the selected node, with the source label. Selection has to survive a reload and be linkable, so it is a query parameter (/pipeline?stage=issues), not JS state. Without JS the page still renders one stage's rows -- the default -- and every node is a plain link that reloads with a different one. Progressive enhancement, same as the cockpit tabs. The drawer is a page of rows, not all of them. It needs a cap, a total, and a link to the full filtered list -- which is what we built for UI-4 and should keep. The mock slices at 20 with no total and no way onward; that is a mock being a mock. "Proven by" wants the confirm build. green_head_run_id is a watermark, NOT a build id -- the confirm build runs inside the dev-env with the dsynth hooks off and never lands in build_runs at all (see green_head_watermark's docstring). The mock links it as "confirm #", which would 404 or, worse, link the wrong run. Either render it as the watermark it is or leave the column out; do not invent the link. MEASURE FIRST Six drawer bodies, one per render. Five reuse queries that already exist (list_bundles, issues_with_occurrences, list_jobs, worklist bands, list_deliveries) and only one is needed per render. Confirm that the drawer costs one query and not six before wiring it, and put the figure in the close note.
close_reason: Committed. ?stage= selects one of six drawer bodies under the flow, headed with the query that produced it. Selection is a URL, so it is linkable and needs no JS; an unknown stage falls back rather than 404ing. One body per render -- measured 0.09-4.2 ms each, against ~7 ms to fetch all six. The operator drawer is the mock's two panels; the outcome drawer keeps the dead-job split and the poly-h6c note the cards carried. Unlike the mock every drawer is capped, says so, and always offers the list. 'Proven by' is left out: green_head_run_id is a watermark, not a build id, so the mock's confirm-#N link would 404. 14 new tests; six stages audited at 1440/500/coarse plus blank, 0 findings.

title: M2 The pipeline is six cards where the mock is a flow with a feedback loop
description: Same six stages, same numbers, near-identical prose, completely different device. This is the widest gap in the epic. WHAT THE MOCK HAS A .source-strip above the flow: "Source / failures enter from these runs", then one button per unfinished run -- "#1842 @main / 47 failures · release" -- each routing to that run. It answers "where is this coming from", which nothing on our page does. Then .pipeline-panel, a dot-grid canvas (radial-gradient(circle, var(--grid-dot) 1px, transparent 1px), 20px), holding: * the caption, verbatim: "Work branches here -- it is not one row advancing through six states. Triage and patch are separate jobs; a failed verification or new operator context enqueues fresh work; an issue can reopen after it resolved. Every figure below is an inventory count, not a rate." * .pipeline-flow -- grid-template-columns: repeat(6, minmax(0,1fr)), gap 22px, min-width 980px, the panel scrolls x. * six .pipe-node buttons, each: .pipe-code "01 / Build failures" (uppercase mono, own header band), .pipe-value (800 27px mono, tabular), .pipe-unit ("bundles"), .pipe-sub ("ingested from 3 active runs"). * connectors as pseudo-elements: ::after is a 31px green rule at top 55px left 100%, ::before the arrowhead. nth-child(3) turns both amber -- automated work to operator work is a different kind of transition. * .retry-loop -- a dashed amber rule at 39% offset, "retry / re-triage" ... "← feeds back". * .pipeline-health INSIDE the panel, below the flow, above the border. Ours is a separate strip above everything. Node tint carries state: .alert red-soft, .warning amber-soft, .success green-soft, driven by the value (bundles>0 -> alert, issues>0 -> warning, outcome -> success). Selected/hover gets a 2px cyan ring. Nodes are BUTTONS -- selection drives the drawer (M3). WHAT WE HAVE Six .stage cards in a 3x2 auto-fit grid, unnumbered, flat, unconnected, not selectable, health strip above, no source strip, no loop. WHAT TO BUILD The flow. Source strip, six numbered nodes in one row with the connectors and the amber transition, the retry loop, the tint, health inside the panel. Undo two things UI-4 did on purpose and got wrong: * test_no_stage_is_numbered asserts no heading starts with a digit, reasoning that "numbering encodes a sequence and there isn't one". The mock numbers them AND says it branches AND draws the loop. The numbers are addresses, not an ordering claim. Delete the test. * the caption is currently a substitute for the diagram rather than a caption for it. Restore the mock's shorter wording once the diagram is under it; the long version exists to do the diagram's job in prose. KEEP Delivery stays two figures, not the mock's one node. The mock's node 05 reads "1 open PRs / awaiting confirm build" and those are different populations (poly-8e2 measured 17 issues resolved with a create_failed delivery). Give the node the open-PR count and the sub-line the confirm figure, named so neither reads as the other. Outcome keeps the dead-job split by retire_reason and the poly-h6c backfill note. The mock has neither, and "dead" without it overstated real failure by 3.1x on the builder. CONSTRAINTS The flow has min-width 980px and scrolls inside .pipeline-panel -- that is UI-7-legal (wide content scrolls in its own container) but the audit has to confirm the BODY still does not scroll sideways at 500px. Every node is a button: 40px minimum under (pointer: coarse), visible focus ring, reachable in tab order. The connectors are decorative pseudo- elements and must not be the only signal that the flow branches -- the caption carries it in text.
notes:
THREE CORRECTIONS AFTER READING THE MOCK'S OWN CODE.

1. The node tint is a census, not a condition. pipeNodes() sets
   cls:bundles ? "alert" : "" and cls:ISSUES.length ? "warning" : "",
   so ANY ingested failure paints node 01 red and ANY fingerprinted
   issue paints node 02 amber -- permanently, on every working system,
   because finding failures is what the farm is for. A tint that is
   always on is not a signal.

   Ours will tint from a condition instead: operator work warns when
   something is actually waiting for a person, automated work alerts
   when work is queued and the runner is not live (queued work nobody is
   doing is a real fault), outcome keeps its green. Ingested and
   Fingerprinted stay neutral.

2. The src labels are the mock's guesses at our function names and
   several are wrong: list_bundles(limit=200) for a count that comes
   from agentic_status(), open_delivery_bundle_ids() for a figure that
   now comes from delivery_counts(), "issues WHERE state='resolved'"
   for one that comes from issue_inventory(). Print the real ones --
   naming the query is the entire point of the label, and naming the
   wrong one is worse than naming none.

3. SCOPE. The mock's node is a button and the rows live in a drawer
   (M3). Doing only the flow here would delete the sub-rows -- Regressed,
   Never reached the provider, Why N dead jobs are dead -- and leave
   nothing in their place until M3 lands.

   So M2 adds the flow ABOVE the existing cards and leaves them as the
   detail. Redundant for one commit, and the alternative is a commit
   that loses information. M3 replaces the cards with the drawer and the
   nodes become the thing that selects it.
close_reason: ed3575b. Source strip, six numbered nodes in one row on a dot-grid canvas with green edges and an amber one at the operator handoff, the dashed retry loop, health moved under the flow, and the mock's shorter caption restored now that the diagram does its job. Each node names the query behind it -- ours, not the mock's three wrong guesses. Tint is a condition (queued work with no live runner, a non-empty operator band) and not the mock's census, which paints every working system red. Delivery gets no tint: a never-sent delivery is stranded work but the rows are historical, and telling today's from last quarter's needs the time-window query this page has none of. The six cards stay below until M3's drawer replaces them. 16 new tests; audited 1440/500/coarse seeded and blank, 0 findings. Caught in review: --faint src label on the always-success-tinted node 06 was 3.98 in dark, and the empty/seeded fixtures shared one database file.

title: M1 The shell is a document where the mock is an application
description:
The mock's shell is a fixed-viewport application. Ours is a scrolling
page with a header on top. Everything else in this epic sits inside
whichever one we pick, so this goes first.

WHAT THE MOCK HAS

  .app { height: 100dvh; display: grid;
         grid-template-rows: 62px minmax(0,1fr) 31px; }
  body { overflow: hidden; }

Three rows: a 62px command bar, the view, and a 31px status rail. The
page itself never scrolls; panes scroll internally (.scroll,
min-height:0 on every grid child). Each view sets its own row template
through [data-layout] -- dash, page3, crumb4, run5, pipe4, full,
cockpit -- so a view declares its own geometry rather than flowing.

Command bar, left to right:
* .brand -- a 32px skewed cyan tile reading "P/", then POLYTROPOS over
  "DeltaPorts Operations". Ours has the wordmark and no tile.
* .primary-nav -- Builds | Pipeline | Repairs, min-width 118px each,
  active gets inset 0 -3px cyan. Ours is close already.
* three .global-fact blocks: Queue <n> jobs, Needs you <n> issues,
  Runner <status>. The runner one has a pulsing square
  (@keyframes blip, 1.6s) and turns green when live. Ours has none.
* an .aud-pill reading "anonymous", shown only for a read-only viewer.
* the theme toggle, which we already have.

Status rail (.footer): "Tracker connected", "Poll 10s builds / 3s jobs",
"Targets <n>", and on the right two demo toggles.

.toast -- fixed bottom-right, role=status aria-live=polite, cyan left
border, 150ms fade. Every operator action in the mock raises one saying
what happened, e.g. "Verify enqueued as job j-10450 -- this takes
minutes. The page will poll until verification_status changes."

WHAT TO BUILD

The frame, the global facts, the status rail and the toast. The mark is
a small thing but it is the only piece of identity in the shell.

The global facts need real queries and must not become a fourth place
that counts things: Queue is agentic_status()["jobs"], Needs you is
worklist_band_counts() minus the runner band, Runner is runner_status()
plus runner_is_live(). All three exist. Every page would then pay for
them on every render -- measure it before wiring it, and if it is not
free, say what it costs in the close note.

The demo toggles in the footer do NOT come across. Audience is
tracker.public_readonly, a setting, not a button; a control that flips
the viewer's own permissions is a mock affordance. Show the real facts
in that space instead. The .aud-pill DOES come across -- an anonymous
reader should be told why the actions are missing.

CONSTRAINTS

Toasts must not be the only report of an outcome: an action's result has
to survive a reload, so the toast is an announcement of a state change
the page already renders, never a substitute for rendering it.

UI-7 holds. The frame does not cost the narrow layout -- the mock itself
drops it below 760px (body{overflow:auto}, .app{height:auto}, facts and
section context hidden) and that media block comes across with it. Keep
one <main>, keep the skip link ahead of everything focusable, keep the
40px coarse-pointer targets, and re-run the audit at 1440/500/coarse on
both installs afterwards.
notes:
MEASURED, on 20k issues / 12.8k open / 51k occurrences / 17k jobs.

  agentic_status()          -> Queue        2.38 ms
  worklist_band_counts()    -> Needs you   23.99 ms
  runner_status + is_live   -> Runner       0.01 ms
  all three, per render                    25.84 ms

25.84 ms on EVERY page, including the ones that need none of it, is not
free -- that is most of what a Builds render costs today. The cheap
substitute is dishonest: COUNT(*) WHERE state='unresolved' takes 0.16 ms
and reads 12,000 against the bands' real 11,227, because a runner-owned
issue is open and does not need you. 7% high in the chrome of every
page is worse than 24 ms.

So: memoise, on tracker.shell_facts_seconds. Same shape as the delivery
sweep (950f4da) and the preflight (d4cc7d9) -- a monotonic throttle, a
process global, and 0 sweeps every call. The topbar fact is a glance,
not a transaction; the page you click through to is the authority, and
it recomputes. Cost falls to one render in the interval.

SCOPE CORRECTION

The bead says "the frame". Doing the mock's frame in full means
body{overflow:hidden} and a [data-layout] grid per view, and a view that
does not declare one clips instead of scrolling. Those grids are
properties of the views -- pipe4 belongs to M2, cockpit to M4 -- so
taking them here would drag both beads into this one and leave every
untouched page broken in between.

M1 does the chrome: fixed topbar and status rail, one scrolling content
region between them, the facts, the mark, the toast, the audience pill.
The content region is one scroller, not per-pane. M2 and M4 subdivide
their own regions on top of it, which is exactly what [data-layout] is
for.
close_reason: 7f3c52a. The frame: command bar, one scrolling content region, status rail, in a viewport-height grid, becoming a document again below 760px. Three system facts in the bar (Queue / Needs you / Runner), memoised on tracker.shell_facts_seconds -- 30.6 ms cold, 15 us warm, because the band projection is 24.5 ms and the shell is on every page; the 0.16 ms substitute answers 7% high. Memo keyed by database (an unkeyed one handed a second tracker the first one's runner) and the compute lock held across the read (claiming and releasing let 8 of 8 concurrent renders compute anyway). Plus the mark, the status rail's inventory, the anonymous pill and an announced toast region. The mock's two footer toggles do not come across -- audience is a setting. 19 tests; audited 1440/500/coarse, seeded and blank, 0 findings. Found on the way: a grid column sizes to its content, so the nowrap chrome rows took the document 188px sideways at 500px.

title: EPIC: Match the operations console mock
description:
The tracker UI migration (poly-0e02) shipped all 22 planned children and
does not look like the mock it was drawn from. Builds is close. Pipeline
and Repairs are different applications.

WHY IT HAPPENED, so the same gap is not reopened

The poly-0e02 beads describe CONTENT AND BEHAVIOUR and never layout.
UI-1 says "shell, primary nav, per-view secondary nav, breadcrumbs" --
that is a document. UI-6 lists the cockpit's contents and specifies the
occurrence selector as "a collapsible list, not a horizontal card strip"
but never says it sits in the right pane of a split. UI-4 says six stages
and "must not read as one row advancing through six linear states" but
never mentions the flow, the arrows, the retry loop or the drawer.

So the migration was built to the beads faithfully, and the beads had
already dropped the mock's structural ideas without recording that they
were dropping anything. Every audit run measured contrast, overflow,
landmarks and touch targets. None compared the result to the mock.

Sharpest instance: the mock's pipeline caption reads "Work BRANCHES here
-- it is not one row advancing through six states." In the mock that is a
CAPTION FOR THE DIAGRAM; the amber arrow and the dashed feedback loop are
how branching is shown. UI-4 paraphrased the sentence, read it as a
prohibition, and deleted the thing it was describing.

SOURCE

Artifact "Polytropos Operations Console",
claude.ai/code/artifact/2c556aa9-ed25-499f-b88d-64b86272aa9a, the
published version dated 2026-09-05, read 2026-09-07. The operator
believes there may be a later version (v8); if so, re-read before
starting and correct these children rather than working from this text.

The mock is a click-through with invented values over the real schema. It
says so itself in the footer: "click-through mock · schema-valid sample
data". Field names and vocabularies are the tracker's; numbers are not.

DELIBERATE DIVERGENCES TO KEEP, not defects to fix

* Delivery is TWO axes, not the mock's one node. The mock shows "1 open
  PRs / awaiting confirm build", which is exactly the conflation poly-8e2
  measured 17 live counterexamples for. Keep them named apart.
* No operator Pause on the Runner page (poly-0e02.8, poly-0w6j).
* The palette is AA-corrected against the surfaces each colour actually
  sits on: --cyan #05749c -> #06688c, --green #1a7a4e -> #19754b, --faint
  #6b7885 -> #5b6874. Do not restore the mock's values.
* A standalone Deliveries list, which the mock has no route for.
* Every UI-7 property holds: one <main>, a skip link, named controls,
  scoped headers, 24px+ touch targets, no sideways body scroll, both
  kinds of empty state. The mock predates all of it and satisfies none of
  it. Where the two conflict, UI-7 wins and the bead says so.

The mock already degrades to a document below 760px -- body{overflow:auto},
.app{height:auto}, global facts and section context hidden -- so the app
frame does not cost the narrow layout.

PROGRESS — branch tracker-ui-migration, nothing pushed

  M1 shell frame            DONE  7f3c52a
  M2 pipeline flow          DONE  ed3575b
  M3 pipeline drawer        DONE  78b60f1
  M4 repairs split          DONE  1a1f9cc
  M5 builds details         DONE  (two declines, one fixture bug)

All five closed. The three views now read as the mock at a glance; every
place they still differ is a decision with a measurement or a bead behind
it, listed in each child's close note.
notes:
DESIGN SOURCE VERSION (poly-ez41).

This epic already names the artifact and says it was read on 2026-09-07 at the published version dated 2026-09-05, which is the standard poly-ez41 asks for and the reason its measurements could be trusted.

Updated: the artifact was republished 2026-09-13 (two footer switches, 'queue at 500' and 'show row buttons'). The design is unchanged; the switches exist so the Repairs queue can be read at the tracker's real 500-issue cap instead of at eight sample issues, which is what made poly-x3pg.7's measurements possible. Compare against the 2026-09-13 version from now on.

The side-by-side poly-ez41 asks for as a closing requirement was done for Repairs on 2026-09-13 and is what produced poly-x3pg.7 and poly-x3pg.8. Pipeline has not had it yet, so this epic is not ready to close.
WHY THE DELIVERIES DIVERGENCE STANDS (poly-x3pg.17, 2026-09-25).

The divergence list says "A standalone Deliveries list, which the mock has no
route for" and does not say why, so a later side-by-side re-found it and filed
a bead. The reason is the bullet two lines above it: delivery is TWO axes, not
the mock's one node, and poly-8e2 measured 17 live counterexamples to that
conflation. Deliveries is the surface where the two are held apart -- its lede
reads "An issue resolves when a build proves the fix, not when a PR merges".
Porting it into the mock would mean redrawing the node this epic has already
decided not to follow.

Also: it is not the mock lagging. The artifact was republished 2026-09-13 and
the copy read 2026-09-24 still has no Deliveries route.

title: Build commercial-matched Polytropos front page
description: Create a standalone responsive Polytropos front page outside the repository in a temporary directory. Match the concept commercial's dark cinematic technical design and problem-to-evidence narrative, use truthful product claims, preserve all existing production assets, and validate desktop/mobile rendering without installing software.
acceptance_criteria: Standalone HTML/CSS/JS and local assets in temp directory; responsive desktop and mobile layouts; visual language matches concept commercial; product claims remain accurate; no repository source changes; accessibility and basic markup validation performed; include README and screenshots when available.

title: A bundle_id containing a slash 500s five pages, and ingest accepts one
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 while writing UI-8's escaping coverage.

/v1/bundles/upsert checks only that bundle_id is non-empty
(ingest_api.py, bundles_upsert). ArtifactStore.upsert_run_bundle does not
check it either. So a hook -- or anything else that can reach the
unauthenticated ingest port -- can write a row whose id contains "/".

Every page that builds a link to that bundle then raises, because
Starlette's `str` path convertor refuses a value with a path separator:

  AssertionError: May not contain path separators
  starlette/convertors.py:28, from request.url_for(...)

Five pages 500 off ONE such row:

  500  /                        (Builds dashboard, "Open repair" link)
  500  /agentic/bundles         (the occurrences list)
  500  /agentic/issues/<key>    (any issue holding that occurrence)
  500  /agentic/jobs/<id>       (any job on it)
  500  /agentic/runs/<id>       (the run it came from)

That is most of the Repairs workspace, and it is not repairable from the
UI, because the pages that would let an operator see or discard the row
are among the ones that fail.

NOT an escaping bug. The same sweep put `"><script>alert(1)</script>` and
`' onmouseover='alert(2)` through every identifier and free-text column on
27 page loads and found no injection: Jinja autoescapes, and the artifact
renderers (markdown, diff, json, log) emit no tag outside their own set
and no event handler. This is purely that an id which cannot appear in a
URL is accepted into a column the URLs are built from.

WHERE TO FIX

Ingest, not the templates. A bundle_id is an opaque token the hook
generates; it has no reason to contain "/", and rejecting it at the door
is one check, where the alternative is remembering to defend every
url_for call site forever. run_id, job_id and issue_key reach path
params the same way and want the same guard. origin is exempt -- its
route uses a `:path` convertor precisely because "cat/port" has a slash.

Worth deciding at the same time: whether an already-stored bad row should
be skipped by the list queries so the workspace stays usable while it is
cleaned up.
notes:
SEVERITY CORRECTED. No shipped writer can produce one of these.

Every minter already sanitises, and I had not checked before filing:

  bundle_id  hook_pkg_failure builds it from sanitize_component(), which
             is `tr '/:@' '___' | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9._-'` -- slash is
             replaced and anything outside the set is stripped.
  run_id     hook_run_start: "run-$(sanitize_component PROFILE)-ts-$$".
  job_id     runner.py:893, origin.replace("/", "_") before the filename.
  issue_key  a sha256 hexdigest, 16 chars.

So the exposure is not "a hook can write one". It is anything else that
reaches the unauthenticated ingest port or the store directly -- the
artifact_store CLI takes --bundle-id verbatim, and so does a hand-rolled
request -- plus any future change to one of those four. The preflight
query on this bead will almost certainly return 0 on the real builder.

Still worth fixing. The failure mode is bad out of proportion to the
input: one row takes down five pages including the ones you would use to
find it, from a port with no authentication, and the check is one guard.
But it is defence in depth, not a live outage, and this bead should not
be read as blocking a deploy.

THE SECOND QUESTION, ANSWERED

The bead asked whether the list queries should skip an already-stored bad
row. No -- a row that is silently absent is one nobody can clean up, and
"invisible" is the failure mode poly-yh9 and the stale-run work keep
running into.

Render it, and make the LINK degrade instead. There is already a pattern
for exactly this: _port_link returns None for an origin that is not
cat/port, so the template prints plain text rather than a broken URL. The
same helper shape for bundle/job/run ids means a legacy bad row shows up,
reads correctly, and simply is not clickable -- which is what keeps the
workspace usable while it is cleaned up.
close_reason: 7f62ffd. Whitelist in dportsv3/db/identifiers.py, enforced at the store's door (upsert_run_bundle, put_blob) rather than at 29 url_for sites; ingest returns 400 instead of 500. Severity was overstated when filed: every shipped minter already sanitises (sanitize_component in the hooks, origin.replace in the runner, a hexdigest for issue_key), so the exposure is the artifact_store CLI, the unauthenticated ingest port, and future changes to those four -- not a live outage. For rows that predate the guard: startup names them, and 'dportsv3 tracker repair-identifiers' renames them carrying all nine referencing tables, dry by default, refusing a collision rather than merging two occurrences. 33 tests, including one that asserts all six pages fail with a bad row present and all six come back after the repair.

title: Compare two occurrences of an issue: what changed between attempt 2 and 3
description:
UI-6 left this out deliberately and it is arguably the question the cockpit
exists to answer: an issue with three occurrences shows three attempts, and
nothing says what is DIFFERENT between them.

What an operator actually wants to know, roughly in order:

* did the error change? bundles.error_signature is per occurrence, and the
  issue key hashes it, so within one issue the signature is by construction
  the same -- the interesting diff is the raw errors.txt, not the digest.
* did the proposed fix change? analysis/changes.diff is an artifact on each
  occurrence, content-addressed, so two shas being equal is a cheap "the
  agent produced the same patch again".
* how far did each get? occurrence_attempts already answers this per
  occurrence (poly-0e02.7) and the selector shows it; what is missing is
  putting two side by side.
* what did the agent try differently? the tool trace and session dump are
  per occurrence and are the expensive read.

Cheapest useful version: pick two occurrences in the selector, show the
artifact shas that differ, and diff the two changes.diff artifacts. The
artifact render cache (poly-0e02.11) is keyed by sha, so both sides are
already cheap to fetch, and identical shas need no fetch at all.

Blocked on nothing. Split out of poly-c9ir rather than growing it.
notes:
Implemented 2026-09-13, the bead's 'cheapest useful version' plus the attempt facts.

/agentic/compare?a=<bundle>&b=<bundle>[&file=<relpath>], template agentic_compare.html, following the /builds/compare precedent.

- render/compare.py: compare_artifacts() unions the two artifact_refs sets and labels each relpath same / changed / only_a / only_b / unknown. sha256 is the blob backend's own key, so 'the agent produced the same patch again' costs no read at all. 'unknown' is for the fs backend, which records no hash -- calling that 'changed' would be a claim the row cannot support.
- default_relpath() opens on analysis/changes.diff when it differs, because 'did the proposed fix change?' is the first question; errors.txt is next, which is 'did the error change?'. The bead is right that the signature itself says nothing here: the issue key hashes it, so within one issue it is equal by construction.
- Only text artifacts both sides produced are offered as a diff. A 40 MB build log is listed with its status and left closed.
- render/artifacts.py gains artifact_raw_text(). artifact_view_data returns a DISPLAY body, and for markdown, diffs, JSON and logs that body is already HTML -- diffing two of those diffs the markup. Same gzip handling and same decompression bound, kept in one place.
- The two attempts' facts sit side by side from occurrence_attempts, which already answered this per occurrence; what was missing was putting two of them together.
- Entry point: the occurrence selector gains one link, defaulting to this occurrence vs the one before it. The selector's rows are <a> elements wrapping the whole row, so a per-row compare link would have meant nesting anchors; the compare page re-picks either side with two selects instead.

Two answers the page has to give and does: two attempts whose artifacts all hash equal say 'Nothing differs -- the agent did the same thing twice', and a stale ?file= falls back to the default rather than erroring, because the status table above it is still the answer.
