title: D1 Direct vs transitive failures
description: D1 Direct vs transitive failures. Mark an issue whose failure is only a failed build-dep as blocked/transitive; surface the root issue first. Prior art: Hydra red-cross vs greyed; pbulk direct vs indirect.

title: D6 Drop dead runs.build_run_id column
description: D6 Drop dead runs.build_run_id column. The sole INSERT INTO runs (artifact_store.py:131) never populates it; always NULL. The confirm-reader joins on (target,origin); no consumer needs build-run provenance. Hard cutover.
close_reason: Obsolete: the premise no longer holds. C3 needs an occurrence's build ordinal to place it against a fix's Green-Head watermark, so runs.build_run_id is now written (hook_pkg_failure sends the tracker run ordinal with the bundle) and read (the occurrence join in agentic_queries.issues). Dropping it would put the regression derivation back on wall clocks.

title: Block B — Stability & atomization: isolate per build, destroy after
description: Move the build path from 'mutate the shared checkout -> reset it' to 'isolate per build -> destroy it'. Warranted on its own merit (deletes verified-gnarly code), NOT a feature prerequisite. dsynth already isolates its own build slots; the shared git checkout is the real contamination point.
design:
Block B — Stability & atomization: DESIGN OF RECORD
(grounded in a read of the real apply/reset/attempt flow; file:line refs inline)

== D1. Granularity = PER-JOB worktree (settled) ==
The codebase already has a per-job git *branch* abstraction; B evolves it into a
per-job *worktree*. Current flow:
- Patch job runs on branch `bundle/<id>`, REUSED across the bundle's job chain
  (triage->patch); created-from-base once, edits left UNCOMMITTED in the shared
  working tree; branch dropped at patch-job end.
  create: checkout_bundle_branch (worker.py:1505) via runner.py:3231
  drop:   drop_bundle_branch/_drop_branch (worker.py:1604) via runner.py:3394
- Verify runs on a THROWAWAY `bundle/<id>-verify`, force-recut with `-B`
  (worker.py:1709/1754), dropped after the verdict (worker.py:1773, runner.py:3574).
- Attempts within a job SHARE the working tree (attempt_loop.py is only the LLM
  conversation; it does not reset between attempts).

B: replace "checkout branch on the ONE shared tree" with "git worktree add a
per-job working dir on that branch". Create at job start (replaces
checkout_bundle_branch / checkout_verify_branch); DESTROY at job end (replaces
drop_bundle_branch / drop_verify_branch and apply_and_build's _post_build_cleanup).
All attempts in a job share that one worktree, exactly as today.

== D2. THE ONE REAL BLOCKER — gitdir prefix split (load-bearing) ==
Git runs on the SAME physical dir through TWO path prefixes:
- IN-CHROOT `/work/DeltaPorts` (via _exec / ChrootRunner): branch ops, reset_port,
  reapply/materialize, apply_and_build. (worker.py:794; chroot.py:29)
- ON THE HOST `<writable>/work/DeltaPorts` (via `git -C`): ONLY the changes.diff
  capture — _git_diff_against_base (worker.py:654) and emit_diff (worker.py:676).
A linked worktree's `.git` file stores an ABSOLUTE `gitdir:` pointer that resolves
under exactly one prefix. So a naive per-job worktree breaks one side.

FIX (default, no version dependency): move the two host-side diff-capture helpers
to run IN-CHROOT via _exec, unifying all git on the `/work/...` prefix. Then a
worktree created in-chroot is self-consistent. (put_file needs NO gitdir — it is a
plain file write; just retarget its write path into the worktree dir.)
ALT: relative-path worktrees (`git worktree add --relative-paths`, git >= 2.48) —
resolves under both prefixes because the worktree->main relative path is identical
in both views. Requires verifying the dev-env git version; prefer the in-chroot fix
to avoid that dependency.

== D3. Scope: serial (B1-B3) isolates the SOURCE only; the rest stays shared ==
Only the DeltaPorts checkout needs per-job isolation for the stability win. These
are per-ENV (shared), NOT under the checkout, and are FINE shared under the single
serial runner — they'd need per-job partition ONLY for concurrency (that is B4):
  - compose tree /work/artifacts/compose/<target>  (dsynth Directory_portsdir)
  - WRKDIR /work/obj  (make_extract, worker.py:927)
  - genpatch staging /work/genpatch-out
  - module dicts _MATERIALIZE_STATE / _WRKSRC_CACHE / _TARGET_CACHE (worker.py:819,940,948)
So B1-B3 = worktree the source overlay ONLY. Do not touch the compose/obj/dsynth
dirs for the serial feature.

== D4. reset_port's fate ==
reset_port's WHOLE-TREE hammer (`git checkout HEAD -- . && git clean -fd`,
worker.py:1331) exists to stop writes that escaped ports/<origin> from poisoning
the NEXT JOB (worker.py:1325-1330). A per-job DISPOSABLE worktree removes that
rationale entirely — destroy, don't reset. The per-ATTEMPT "start clean" reset
(each attempt from branch HEAD) may be kept, but becomes a SAFE, SCOPED op inside
the disposable worktree (no cross-job blast radius). Net: delete the whole-tree /
cross-job cleanup; keep at most a scoped per-attempt reset inside the worktree.

== Task designs ==
B1 (per-job worktree): new worker.create_job_worktree(env, bundle_id, kind) doing
   in-chroot `git worktree add <wt_path> <branch>` (reuse branch for patch; `-B`
   recut for verify). Retarget the job's paths.deltaports to <wt_path>. Move
   diff-capture in-chroot (D2). Replaces checkout_bundle_branch (runner.py:3231)
   and checkout_verify_branch (runner.py:3462).
B2 (delete cleanup): new worker.destroy_job_worktree -> in-chroot
   `git worktree remove --force <wt_path>` (+ optional branch -D). Replaces
   _drop_branch (worker.py:1604), drop_verify_branch (worker.py:1773), and
   apply_and_build._post_build_cleanup (cli.py:383). Delete reset_port's whole-tree
   reset (steps.py:1083 call becomes a no-op or a scoped in-worktree reset only).
B3 (stale sweep): on runner startup, in-chroot `git worktree prune` + remove
   orphaned worktree dirs whose owning job is not live. Name worktrees `wt/<id>`
   and either pidfile them or diff against active jobs. Replaces "SIGKILL ->
   dirty env -> manual reset-port" recovery.

== Open verifications BEFORE coding ==
- git in the dev-env chroot: version (for the --relative-paths option) + confirm
  `git worktree` is available.
- apply_and_build refactor: today it applies --3way into /work/DeltaPorts then
  _post_build_cleanup; confirm it can instead build inside a per-verify worktree.
- product call: keep the per-attempt "clean start" reset, or let attempts build on
  prior state? (Affects whether B2 keeps a scoped in-worktree reset.)

title: A4 Flaky-aware confirmation
description: A4 Flaky-aware confirmation. A single green is provisional; the next scheduled / 2nd independent green confirms. Guards transient build flakiness (network/toolchain). Prior art: ClusterFuzz 2-bot, >=5/10 reproductions.
design:
## Design

Guard against transient build flakiness (network / toolchain): a SINGLE green is
provisional; require N independent greens before resolving. Prior art: ClusterFuzz
2-bot reproduction, >=5/10 threshold.

**Config:** `confirm_green_threshold` (default 2) in config/agentic-policy.json.

**State:** add `confirm_green_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` to `issues`.

**Modifies A2's green handling — first green is NOT terminal:**
- green verdict, `confirm_green_count + 1 < threshold`: stay in `resolving` (the
  "confirming" band — no new state value needed), record the provisional green +
  candidate green-head, and REQUEST ANOTHER build by bumping
  `requested_build_generation` again — so C2 naturally schedules a 2nd INDEPENDENT
  confirm build (reuses the spine; no separate scheduler).
- green verdict, count reaches `threshold`: hand to A2 -> `resolved`; green-head =
  the confirming (last) build.
- 'Independent' = a DISTINCT `build_run_id` / generation, not a re-read of the same
  build result.

**Any red before threshold:** A3 reopen path; reset `confirm_green_count = 0`.

**Depends on A1 + A2** (verdict + resolve path). Optional-ish hardening; the MVP
resolves on a single green until this lands.
acceptance_criteria: 1) confirm_green_threshold config (default 2). 2) issues gains confirm_green_count. 3) First green: issue stays resolving, count=1, requested_build_generation bumped so C2 runs a 2nd INDEPENDENT build (distinct build_run_id/generation). 4) Count reaches threshold -> A2 resolves; green-head = confirming build. 5) Any red before threshold -> A3 reopen + count reset. 6) Test: green,green -> resolved on 2nd; green,red -> reopened + count reset.
close_reason: Implemented + reviewed + committed. Threshold via DP_CONFIRM_GREEN_THRESHOLD env knob (codebase convention) rather than agentic-policy.json.

title: D3 Timestamp skew at source
description: D3 Timestamp skew at the source. Hooks write compact YYYYmmdd-HHMMSSZ; regression checks are naked lexicographic compares that only work because _normalize_ts canonicalizes at the single writer. Emit ISO at the hook source; keep _normalize_ts as a guarded fallback that asserts. (ts_utc is bundle/agentic data, not dsynth build_*.)

title: A3 Red -> auto-reopen + handoff
description: A3 Red -> auto-reopen + manual handoff. On a red confirm build, reopen the issue out of resolving and write analysis/manual_handoff.md instead of leaving a falsely-resolved issue. Prior art: Google TAP auto-rollback (tracker-side).
design:
## Design

On a RED confirm-build verdict (from A1's report-back), do NOT leave a falsely
"resolving" issue — reopen it and hand off to a human. Prior art: Google TAP
auto-rollback.

**Transition (red branch of the confirm-build report-back handler):**
- `state: resolving -> unresolved` — reuse `reopen_issue` (issue_actions.py:127),
  which clears `resolved_at` / `regressed_at` / `delivery_bundle_id`.
- GUARD: only from `state='resolving'` (a muted / already-resolved issue untouched).
- advance `last_confirmed_build_generation = generation`, clear
  `building_generation` — so the C2 loop does NOT re-enqueue this generation and
  spin on a persistently-red fix.

**Manual handoff (not auto-triage):** write `analysis/manual_handoff.md` via the
existing escalation writer (agent/manual_handoff.py) with: which accepted fix
(`delivery_bundle_id`) was built, the red verdict, `build_run_id`, and the log
pointer. A red confirm goes to a HUMAN — it does NOT re-trigger the agent loop.

**Event:** emit `issue_reopened` (or `issue_confirm_failed`) with
`source='build-confirmed'`, `verdict='red'`, `build_run_id`.

**Depends on A1** (verdict + report-back endpoint). Pairs with A2 (green branch).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Red verdict for a resolving issue -> state resolving->unresolved via reopen_issue (resolved_at/regressed_at/delivery_bundle_id cleared); guard only from resolving. 2) analysis/manual_handoff.md written via manual_handoff.py with the failed delivery_bundle_id, red verdict, build_run_id, log pointer. 3) last_confirmed_build_generation advanced + building_generation cleared -> C2 does NOT re-enqueue the persistently-red fix. 4) Does NOT auto-retrigger the agent (manual handoff, not auto-triage). 5) Event emitted. 6) Test: resolving+red -> reopened + handoff file; second C2 pass -> no re-enqueue.
close_reason: Implemented + reviewed + committed 4th A task. Handoff carries generation+log instead of build_run_id (dev-env hooks disabled -> no build_runs row).

title: C3 Two-axis status (regressed derived)
description: C3 Two-axis status. Split resolution axis (unresolved->resolving->resolved->muted) from build-observation axis (green/red at ordinal). `regressed` becomes DERIVED (resolved AND newer build re-emits fingerprint >= boundary), not a stored mode. Prior art: ArgoCD sync-vs-health; Sentry release boundary.
design:
## Design

Split the two axes that are currently conflated in `issues.state`, and make
`regressed` a DERIVED read, not a stored mode. Prior art: ArgoCD sync-vs-health;
Sentry release boundary.

**Two axes:**
- RESOLUTION axis (operator/build intent) — `issues.state` constrained to
  {unresolved, resolving, resolved, muted}. `regressed` is REMOVED as a stored value.
- BUILD-OBSERVATION axis (facts) — `port_status` / `build_results` / the A2
  green-head ordinal (`green_head_run_id`).

**Derive `regressed` in the projection layer (tracker/issue_state.py, which already
layers on fix_state):**
`regressed  ==  state == resolved  AND  a build at ordinal > green_head_run_id
re-emits the same fingerprint` (i.e. resolved on the resolution axis but red past the
known-good boundary on the observation axis). `regressed_at` becomes the
boundary-crossing build's timestamp, also derived.

**Writer change:** the artifact-store path that currently sets `state='regressed'`
on a new occurrence after resolve instead LEAVES `state='resolved'` and lets the
projection derive the regressed badge. One-time migration: existing `regressed` rows
-> `resolved` (the derivation reproduces the badge from the observation axis).

**Depends on A2** (green-head boundary) **and A3**. Touches issue_state.py badge +
worklist bucketing; keep fix_state.py's `merged` dominance intact.
acceptance_criteria: 1) issues.state constrained to {unresolved,resolving,resolved,muted}; 'regressed' no longer a stored value. 2) issue_state.py derives regressed = state==resolved AND a build at ordinal > green_head_run_id re-emits the fingerprint; regressed_at derived from that build. 3) Badge + worklist reflect derived regressed with no stored column; fix_state 'merged' dominance intact. 4) Writer stops setting state='regressed'; existing regressed rows migrated to resolved (derivation reproduces the badge). 5) Test: resolved + newer failing build past green-head -> derived regressed; newer build without re-emit -> stays resolved.
close_reason: Implemented + reviewed. regressed is derived from the Green-Head watermark in issue_state.derived_regression; issues.state is CHECKed to {unresolved,resolving,resolved,muted} and legacy regressed rows migrate on open. effective_state folds the two axes so the badge, action gate and worklist keep their existing shape. An occurrence arriving on a resolving issue no longer reopens it — the confirm verdict owns that exit.

title: C4 Workqueue hygiene
description: C4 Workqueue pacing. The confirm-build feed retries on two paths with no delay between attempts: the bounded machinery-failure path (spends its whole retry budget at loop speed) and the enqueue-failure path (retries forever, uncounted). Add a persisted per-key next_eligible_at with exponential backoff and honour it in the reconcile SELECT. Keying and single-flight already landed with C1/C2. Prior art: controller-runtime workqueue.
design:
## Design

Rewritten against the code after C1/C2/yt7 landed; the original scope was
written before them and three of its four asks no longer describe reality.

**Already delivered, not part of this:**

- Keying by (target, origin, fingerprint) — that triple IS issue_key
  (fingerprint.py:80), and every marker and counter is keyed on it.
- Single-flight per key — _claim_issue_build (runner.py:1046) is a
  conditional UPDATE taken BEFORE the enqueue, so a failed claim cannot
  leave a duplicate.
- 'env busy' requeue-without-penalty — moot rather than done. _gate_blocked()
  returns True on dsynth-busy and the loop continues BEFORE
  process_build_requests runs, so nothing is enqueued and there is nothing to
  forgive.

**Explicitly NOT in scope:** backing off A4 re-requests. A green below the
consecutive-green threshold bumps requested_build_generation inline in the
verdict transaction (runner.py:1388) to schedule an independent build. Those
are successes being repeated on purpose; pacing them only slows confirmation.

**What is actually missing — pacing, on two paths that retry without it.**

1. The bounded path. A confirm build that could not RUN increments
   confirm_failure_count and clears the in-flight marker
   (_record_confirm_failure, runner.py:1246), so the feed retries on the very
   next pass. The bound (DP_CONFIRM_MAX_FAILURES, default 3) is therefore
   spent at loop speed for a fast failure — 'no dev-env', 'could not
   establish fresh confirm/verify branch' raise in seconds, so three tries
   burn in seconds and the issue is reopened with a manual handoff for
   something transient. For a slow failure — 'confirm verdict could not be
   recorded' (runner.py:4412), i.e. the write lost the SQLite lock race after
   the build ran — each retry costs a full dsynth run, so the same three
   tries waste three builds. runner.py:4458 already names this as C4's.

2. The unbounded path. An enqueue failure in process_build_requests
   (runner.py:1502) logs a WARN, releases the claim and continues; the
   level-triggered feed re-derives the same work next pass, roughly every 5s,
   forever, with no counter and no escalation. confirm_failure_count never
   sees it — that counter lives on the job-execution path. The sibling loop
   the docstring claims to mirror does not do this: process_verify_requests
   marks its request 'failed' (runner.py:993) and stops.

**Shape.** A per-key next_eligible_at alongside confirm_failure_count on
issues, and one AND (next_eligible_at IS NULL OR next_eligible_at <= now)
clause on the issues_needing_build SELECT. Backoff is exponential in the
existing failure count, so no second counter is needed for path 1; path 2
starts using the same counter and bound, which also gives it the escalation
it lacks. State is a column, so it survives a runner restart — the startup
sweep clears building_generation only (runner.py:1185), never the tally.

A produced verdict already resets confirm_failure_count (runner.py:1363);
it must reset next_eligible_at with it, or a recovered issue stays parked.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A per-key next_eligible_at persists on issues and is honoured by issues_needing_build, so backoff survives a runner restart. 2) A confirm build that could not RUN backs off exponentially in confirm_failure_count before the feed re-derives it; the bound (DP_CONFIRM_MAX_FAILURES) still reopens the issue with a manual handoff. 3) An enqueue failure in process_build_requests counts against the same budget and backs off the same way, so a persistently unwritable queue escalates to a human instead of logging every 5s forever. 4) A produced verdict clears next_eligible_at along with confirm_failure_count. 5) env busy is untouched: the gate stops the loop before the feed runs, so no penalty is possible. 6) A4 re-requests are not paced. 7) Tests: repeated machinery failures show growing gaps and terminate at the bound; a job becomes eligible once the delay elapses; a green verdict clears the delay.
close_reason: Implemented + reviewed. Per-key next_eligible_at on issues, exponential in the existing confirm_failure_count, honoured by issues_needing_build. Enqueue failures now go through the same budget instead of releasing the claim silently and retrying uncounted forever. Verdicts and give-up both clear the delay. Scope was cut to pacing after re-reading the code: keying and single-flight came with C1/C2, env-busy is handled by the gate stopping the loop, and A4 re-requests are successes that must not be paced.

title: B1 Per-job git worktree for overlay source
description: B1 Per-job git worktree for the overlay source. Each build applies its diff into its own `git worktree add --detach` of /work/DeltaPorts (shared object store, no clone-per-build). Eliminates the shared-checkout collision.
design:
## Design

Replace "checkout branch on the ONE shared /work/DeltaPorts tree" with "git
worktree add a per-job working dir on that branch". Evolves the existing per-job
git *branch* abstraction into a per-job *worktree*. All attempts in a job share the
one worktree, exactly as they share the tree today (attempt_loop.py is only the LLM
conversation; it does not reset between attempts).

**New op:** `worker.create_job_worktree(env, bundle_id, kind)` doing in-chroot
`git worktree add <wt_path> <branch>` — reuse `bundle/<id>` for patch; `-B` recut
for verify. Retarget the job's `paths.deltaports` to `<wt_path>`. Replaces
`checkout_bundle_branch` (runner.py:3231) and `checkout_verify_branch`
(runner.py:3462).

**THE ONE REAL BLOCKER — gitdir prefix split (load-bearing, fold the fix in here):**
git touches the same physical dir through TWO path prefixes — IN-CHROOT
`/work/DeltaPorts` (via _exec/ChrootRunner: branch ops, reset, reapply,
apply_and_build) and ON THE HOST `<writable>/work/DeltaPorts` (via `git -C`: ONLY
the changes.diff capture — `_git_diff_against_base` worker.py:654, `emit_diff`
worker.py:676). A linked worktree's `.git` file stores an ABSOLUTE `gitdir:` pointer
that resolves under exactly one prefix, so a naive worktree breaks one side.
FIX (default, no version dependency): move those two diff-capture helpers IN-CHROOT
via _exec, unifying all git on the `/work/...` prefix. (`put_file` needs no gitdir —
just retarget its write path into the worktree.)
ALT: `git worktree add --relative-paths` (git >= 2.48) — needs a version check;
prefer the in-chroot fix to avoid that dependency.

**Open verifications before coding:** git version + `git worktree` availability in
the chroot; confirm `apply_and_build` can build inside a per-verify worktree.
acceptance_criteria: 1) worker.create_job_worktree does in-chroot 'git worktree add <wt> <branch>' (reuse bundle/<id> for patch, -B recut for verify); job paths.deltaports retargeted to <wt>. 2) Replaces checkout_bundle_branch (runner.py:3231) + checkout_verify_branch (runner.py:3462). 3) Diff-capture (_git_diff_against_base, emit_diff) moved in-chroot so all git shares the /work/... prefix; changes.diff still captured correctly. 4) All attempts in a job share the one worktree. 5) Verified pre-code: git worktree available in chroot; apply_and_build builds inside a per-verify worktree.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED in 5cc4931. Acceptance criteria:

1. create_job_worktree does in-chroot `git worktree add` (reuse bundle/<id>
   for patch, -B recut for verify) and repoints the job's tree — MET, though
   by symlink rather than by retargeting paths.deltaports. See the placement
   note: EnvPaths needs no change under B.
2. Replaces checkout_bundle_branch + checkout_verify_branch — MET at the call
   sites (runner.py:2682, 2762, plus both drop wrappers). The four worker
   functions now have NO production callers but are still defined and still
   have tests. B2 owns deleting them.
3. Diff-capture moved in-chroot — MET, and wider than the design said. It was
   not only _git_diff_against_base + emit_diff: dev-env's _port_dirty_paths
   (cli.py) was a third host-side git consumer the design missed, used by
   apply_and_build's pre-replay check. It also swallowed git failures and
   returned [] — i.e. "clean" — which would have inverted the refusal its
   caller exists to make. Now raises.
4. All attempts in a job share the one worktree — MET by construction: the
   worktree is created at job start and destroyed at job end, attempts do not
   touch it.
5. Pre-code verifications — git worktree in chroot: DONE (2.49.0).
   apply_and_build inside a per-verify worktree: STILL NOT DONE. It needs a
   real dsynth build. Everything around it is verified, but that specific
   claim is not, and B2/B4 lean on it.

VERIFIED ON X6, end to end, five runs covering both the branch-creation and
branch-reuse paths: create -> host-side write through the symlink -> in-chroot
diff helper sees it -> in-chroot dirty check sees it -> destroy -> main
checkout still CLEAN. That last part is the point of B1.

UNEXPLAINED: the very first e2e create returned ok=False and I could not
reproduce it in five subsequent runs, including after deleting the branch to
force the creation path. Cause unknown; recorded rather than guessed at.

Suite 2121 passed. New tests in tests/test_dev_env_job_worktree.py; several
existing tests updated where B1 changed a contract (the diff helpers take an
env, the pre-replay dirty check is now a chroot call, the verify wrapper
returns no ref to restore).
close_reason: Closed

title: B2 Delete whole-tree reset_port + cleanup dance
description: B2 Delete the whole-tree reset_port (worker.py:1331 `git checkout HEAD -- . && git clean -fd`) and the fragile _post_build_cleanup git-reset dance (cli.py:383); replace with 'destroy the worktree'. reset_port comment itself admits escaped writes poison the next job classify/compose.
design:
## Design

With a per-job DISPOSABLE worktree (B1), the whole rationale for the fragile
cleanup dances evaporates — you destroy the worktree instead of scrubbing a shared
tree. reset_port's whole-tree hammer (`git checkout HEAD -- . && git clean -fd`,
worker.py:1331) exists ONLY to stop writes that escaped ports/<origin> from
poisoning the NEXT job's shared checkout (worker.py:1325-1330); a disposable
worktree removes that cross-job blast radius entirely.

**New op:** `worker.destroy_job_worktree(env, bundle_id, kind)` -> in-chroot
`git worktree remove --force <wt_path>` (+ optional branch `-D`). Called at job end.

**Delete / replace:**
- `_drop_branch` (worker.py:1604) and `drop_verify_branch` (worker.py:1773) ->
  replaced by destroy_job_worktree.
- `apply_and_build._post_build_cleanup` (dev-env cli.py:383) — the 3-step git-reset
  dance a SIGKILL skips -> deleted; the worktree is thrown away instead.
- reset_port's whole-tree reset (called at steps.py:1083) -> becomes a no-op, OR at
  most a SCOPED per-attempt reset INSIDE the disposable worktree (safe, no cross-job
  blast radius).

**Orthogonality note (verified):** this does NOT touch dsynth's own ephemeral build
dirs. dsynth self-isolates the compile (Directory_buildbase=/work/dsynth/build +
Number_of_builders -> per-port tmpfs builder slots); the real build never dirties
the base /var /tmp or the checkout. The cleanup we delete was only ever about
source-checkout dirtiness, which the worktree now owns. Two ephemerality layers,
separate: source checkout = our worktree; build sandbox = dsynth's, untouched.

**Product call (open):** keep the per-attempt "clean start" reset (now scoped inside
the worktree) or let attempts build on prior state? Decides whether B2 keeps a
scoped in-worktree reset or removes it outright.
acceptance_criteria: 1) worker.destroy_job_worktree does in-chroot 'git worktree remove --force <wt>' at job end. 2) Deletes/replaces _drop_branch (worker.py:1604), drop_verify_branch (worker.py:1773), apply_and_build._post_build_cleanup (cli.py:383), and reset_port's whole-tree reset (steps.py:1083). 3) dsynth's own build dirs untouched (orthogonal). 4) Per-attempt reset either removed or kept as a scoped in-worktree op per the product call. 5) A SIGKILL that skips cleanup no longer poisons the next job (worktree is disposable).
notes:
CARRIED DEBT DISCHARGED (as far as it can be). apply_and_build DOES run inside
a per-verify worktree: worktree created, link repointed, apply and reapply

title: B3 Startup stale-worktree sweep (crash-safe)
description: B3 Startup stale-worktree sweep (crash-safe). On runner start, sweep leftover per-job worktrees from crashed builds — replaces today SIGKILL -> dirty env -> manual reset-port recovery.
design:
## Design

Crash-safety sweep. Today a SIGKILL mid-job leaves a dirty shared env that an
operator must manually `reset-port` to recover. With per-job worktrees (B1/B2), a
crash instead leaves a STALE worktree — sweep it automatically on runner startup.

**On runner startup:**
1. in-chroot `git worktree prune` (drops worktree admin entries whose dir is gone).
2. Enumerate worktree dirs under the worktree root; for each, decide if its owning
   job is still live. Name worktrees `wt/<bundle_id>` (or `<bundle_id>-verify`) and
   either pidfile them or diff against the set of active jobs (lifecycle ACTIVE work
   states). Remove any orphan via `git worktree remove --force`.

**Replaces:** the "SIGKILL -> dirty env -> operator manually runs reset-port"
recovery path. After this, a crashed runner self-cleans on restart with no operator
action.

**Scope guard:** only sweeps worktrees the runner owns (the `wt/` namespace); never
touches the primary /work/DeltaPorts checkout or dsynth's build dirs.

**Depends on B1 (worktrees must exist to be swept) and pairs with B2 (same
destroy op).**
acceptance_criteria: 1) On runner startup: in-chroot 'git worktree prune' + remove orphaned wt/ dirs whose owning job is not live. 2) Worktrees named wt/<bundle_id>; orphan decided via pidfile or active-job diff. 3) Replaces the SIGKILL->dirty-env->manual reset-port recovery; crashed runner self-cleans on restart. 4) Only sweeps the wt/ namespace; never touches primary /work/DeltaPorts or dsynth dirs.
notes:
RE-REVIEWED 2026-08-23 against the code as B1/B2 actually shipped. The design section is stale in three places and the scope shrank.

STALE:
  * Names worktrees wt/<bundle_id>. B1 shipped job-<kind>-<id> directly under /work (worker.py:1512), so the sweep namespace is /work/job-*.
  * Scope guard says 'never touches the primary /work/DeltaPorts checkout'. After B1 that path is not a checkout, it is the relative symlink. Restate as: never touch /work/ports-main, and repoint the link to the idle target BEFORE removing anything it might point at.
  * 'decide if its owning job is still live' via pidfile or active-job diff — unnecessary under a single runner. With poly-bg1 criterion 4 (exclusive startup lock), at startup no job of ours is live by definition, so every /work/job-* is stale. That remains the cheapest unblock; ownership recording (7d4b337) does NOT unblock this, because B3 must DECIDE liveness, not log it.

ALREADY DONE BY B1, drop from scope: create_job_worktree force-removes and prunes any leftover at the job's exact path before worktree add (worker.py:1572-1577). Path-collision recovery already exists, lazily, per job.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT:
  1. Orphan worktrees for bundles never re-enqueued — nothing ever reclaims them. This is the real remaining item.
  2. Stranded inflight/*.job files. reap_orphans only touches DB rows, so a crash leaves the files behind while their rows go DEAD. Same startup, same crash-safety theme.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER FRAMING: I called a stale /work/DeltaPorts symlink the sharpest remaining item here. On re-review it is not, and it is not a B3 item at all. Every reader of the link runs inside a job that repoints it first (creation at runner.py:3802, 4031, 4183 precedes any worker.* call), and no startup path reads the ports tree — the health probe does not touch it. The plain stale-link case self-heals on the next job. The real hazard is the soft-fail path, filed separately as its own P1; do not bury it in this deferred bead.

MULTI-ENV: the sweep is per-env. poly-s9m makes 'is this worktree live' hard again unless the in-process-pool option wins, where the runner holds its live set in memory. Do not build the sweep in a way that assumes one env.
AUDIT 2026-08-23. Line numbers in the notes above are stale — the runner lock (c67416a) shifted runner.py by ~113 lines. The worktree-creation call sites cited as runner.py:3802/4031/4183 are the calls inside process_patch_job, the verify dispatch, and the confirm path; find them via _checkout_bundle_branch_for_job and _checkout_verify_branch_for_job. Cite functions, not line numbers.

Also: of those three call sites I verified the ordering claim ('creation precedes any worker.* call') by reading the patch and confirm paths. I did NOT read the verify dispatch as carefully. Treat that third one as unconfirmed.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23. Two sweeps, both at startup, both decidable only because the runner lock (poly-bg1) guarantees no other runner and nothing has been claimed yet.

1. sweep_stranded_inflight — moves inflight/*.job to failed/ with an error note. reap_orphans marked the rows DEAD but never touched the files, and claim_next_job_batch only globs pending/, so those files were invisible forever. Moved rather than deleted: the payload is the only record of what the job was.

2. sweep_stale_worktrees / worker.sweep_job_worktrees — removes /work/job-* in the runner's env, restoring the ports link to ports-main FIRST because it may point at a directory about to be removed.

DESIGN POINT THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE: the sweep works on directory NAMES, not bundle ids, so destroy_job_worktree is the wrong tool. _job_worktree_name sanitizes any character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] to '_', so the mapping is lossy and a swept directory name cannot be turned back into the bundle it came from.

SINGLE ENV, deliberately. Sweeping envs the runner does not own would mean rm -rf inside a tree an operator might be sitting in — verified that dev-env shell/exec do NOT mark an env busy, so the lock says nothing about them. When a runner owns several envs (poly-s9m) this loops over the set it owns.

VERIFICATION: the shell is where the risk is, so the generated script is executed against real directories in a test rather than only asserted on as a string — it removes the stale worktrees, keeps the keep-list entry, and leaves ports-main and DeltaPorts alone. Five mutations, each caught: widening the glob to all dirs, ignoring the keep list, ignoring a failed link restore, deleting inflight files instead of moving them, and sweeping with no env resolved.

CORRECTION TO A GUESS I MADE EARLIER: shlex.quote leaves shell-safe names bare, so an assertion that the keep list appears quoted was simply wrong. The test now pins the behaviour (safe name bare, unsafe name quoted) rather than a spelling.

NOT VERIFIED IN A REAL CHROOT (poly-4kr). In particular 'git worktree remove --force' and 'worktree prune' against a real repo are stubbed out in the test; only the glob, keep-list and rm logic run for real.
VERIFIED ON x6 2026-08-23 against the live env 2026Q3-editors_vim.

Stranded inflight sweep: a .job file placed in inflight/ was moved to failed/ with its .error note on the next --once start.

Worktree sweep: simulated a crashed job by creating job-patch-faketest (with content) and job-verify-faketest and pointing /work/DeltaPorts at the patch one. On startup the runner logged 'swept 2 stale worktree(s)', both directories were gone, and the link was back on ports-main. ports-main and polytropos untouched.

Also confirmed the B1 cycle end to end on hardware, which the sweep depends on: create_job_worktree moved the link to job-patch-livetest-b1 and destroy_job_worktree put it back on ports-main.

title: D4 Fingerprint-rule versioning
description: D4 Fingerprint stability. Version the error-line normalization rule; apply new rules only to new occurrences so history doesn't spuriously regroup/regress. Prior art: Sentry grouping versioning; ClusterFuzz frame-based.

title: every write guard is keyed on the /work/DeltaPorts/ prefix, and the job worktree is reachable under its real /work/job-<kind>-<bundle>/ path too
description:
Found by the poly-7pwa.29 review, from code reading (not run on a real env). /work/DeltaPorts is a relative symlink to the job worktree /work/job-<kind>-<bundle>/ (worker.py, create_job_worktree). _resolve_chroot_path accepts any path under /work/, and every write guard tests the literal /work/DeltaPorts/ prefix: the shared-payload guard (.29), _reject_dports_write, the Makefile.DragonFly lock, the orphan-dops check. A put_file or edit_file through /work/job-patch-<bundle>/ports/... passes all of them, and list_dir /work shows that directory.

Fix: resolve the path first (realpath inside the writable overlay) and map anything under the job worktree back to its /work/DeltaPorts/ form before the guards run, or refuse writes outside /work/DeltaPorts/ for DeltaPorts content. Check first whether any agent session has written through the real path (tool_trace search).

title: a Manual Queue row stays pending after the operator takes over, discards, rejects or accepts the bundle: only Retry updates it
description:
Found by the poly-7pwa.28 review. user_context_requests rows are flipped only by POST /api/bundles/{id}/retry (bundle_actions.py) and the runner's retriage sweep. Take-over, discard, reject and accept on the bundle page leave the row 'pending', so the Manual Queue keeps listing work already decided. Live tracker 2026-10-06: 97 pending rows, 1 whose bundle is merged/verified. .28 makes three more escalation paths write rows, so this happens more often.

Also seen, same area, not fixed by .28: a batched patch escalation marks every sibling bundle escalated_manual (_finish_orchestrator_run) but only the lead gets a queue row and handoff, as triage does; confirm_build_red hands off to a human with no queue row.

Fix: each terminal bundle action sets the bundle's pending rows to a closed status (as /retry and discard on /api/manual-requests do).

title: retiring a build line leaves its blocks and dragonfly/@<line>/ folder behind: no command drops them
description:
After poly-7pwa.25 (migrate branch-line), each quarterly adds a target block and a payload folder per multi-line port. When a line stops being built (2026Q3 once 2026Q4 is up), its blocks, its name in target lists and its dragonfly/@<line>/ files stay in DeltaPorts, composing for no one. Today: 8 ports have @2026Q3 blocks, 3 have dragonfly/@2026Q3/ (DeltaPorts d9e321bde6c). special/*/diffs/ already carries @2026Q1 and @2026Q2 leftovers.

Wanted: dportsv3 migrate retire-line --line @2026Q3 [--write], dry run by default, with the same self-check as branch-line: every other line plans exactly what it did before. Drops blocks naming only the line, removes it from lists, deletes payload no remaining op reads.

Optional and separate: collapse a block that every live line has an identical copy of into @any. Needs the list of live lines, which only the operator knows.

title: Env facade: one object for a dev-env's name, paths, build line, exec and caches; move install_patches and materialize_dports onto it
description:
First step of poly-li5w. Add an Env class (dportsv3/agent/, beside worker.py) holding what the 41 env-first functions look up each time: env_paths, the cached build line (peek_env_target/set_env_target), _exec, and the per-env state now in module dicts (_MATERIALIZE_STATE). Existing free functions keep working by delegating to a per-name Env, so no caller has to move at once.

Move install_patches and materialize_dports (and their private helpers: _payload_destination, _committed_paths, _head_text, _overlay_plan_for) onto it, and move their tests (test_install_patches_target_scope.py and the materialize tests) from monkeypatching worker attributes to a fake Env. Done when those tests patch no worker attribute and the suite is green. Measure and record how many worker monkeypatches remain, to size the next child.

title: agent I/O as objects: an Env and a Runner instead of env-threaded functions and module globals
description:
Measured 2026-10-06 (master 744dc5d). The agent's I/O layer is free functions threaded by a string plus hidden module state:

- agent/worker.py: 4254 lines, 87 top-level functions, 41 take env: str first; per-env state in module dicts keyed by the env name (_MATERIALIZE_STATE[(env, origin)], the env-target and env_paths caches).
- agent/runner.py: 5950 lines, 122 functions, 18 take queue_root first; 12 module-level state variables (_state_db_conn, locks, ...) mutated through 12 global statements.
- agent/health.py: 5 more env-first functions.
- Smaller: tracker/db.py (10 conn-first functions), module caches in tracker/shell_facts.py, tracker/delivery_sync.py, settings.py, dev-env config.py.

Cost: tests replace behaviour by patching module attributes -- monkeypatch.setattr on worker 172 times (as worker/worker_mod), on runner ~160 (runner/runner_mod/_runner) -- so private helpers are de facto test API and a rename breaks tests no production caller uses. New code keeps adding to it (poly-7pwa.27 added _committed_paths(env, ...) and _head_text(env, ...)).

NOT IN SCOPE: the engine, scope_check and the parser are pure functions over text on purpose (scope_check's docstring) and stay that way. steps.py already injects its I/O through PatchServices/TriageServices; that is the pattern to extend, not replace.

APPROACH: gradual, never big-bang. (1) An Env object (name, paths, build line, exec, its caches) that the existing worker/health functions delegate to; callers and tests move module by module; then the free functions go. (2) A Runner/queue object owning the state-db connection, locks and queue_root, replacing runner.py's globals. (3) Optionally a repository object over tracker/db.py. Each child lands with its tests moved onto fakes of the new object, and leaves the suite green.

title: guidance written while another run's attempt on the port is active on that build line is never tried
description: Filed 2026-10-04 by the poly-7pwa spec review (round 2). DESIGN holds the problem, the evidence and the change; ACCEPTANCE says when it is done.
design:
STATE, 2026-10-04. Open, not started. Found while measuring
poly-7pwa.17; outside the epic. Write it after poly-7pwa.17 lands: both
candidate fixes build on the run_id that .17 passes into
PortHistory.load. Line numbers are the post-carry tree's (master ab725ac
plus poly-7pwa.21 rows 1-9). poly-7pwa.14 lands before .17 and shifts

:1862 -> :1892, its call :1912 -> :1942), and .17 shifts it by 2 more
below line 914: find runner functions by name.

runner.process_job on the post-carry tree with .17's run key applied,
and over PortHistory.load on master, master with poly-7pwa.10, the run
key and a 2-hour window: the flag is False while the prompt would carry
the context, in all four. The sequence:
  1. run-1's triage of a port escalates. The operator answers its manual
     request: context row (run-1, origin), revision 1, written at T0.
  2. Meanwhile run-2's attempt on the same port and build line is
     active. process_user_context_updates does not enqueue the retriage
     while an active same-origin job exists on the context run's line or
     with no target (_has_active_same_origin_job,
     dportsv3/agent/runner.py:1862-1887, used at :1912-1921; QUEUED
     counts as active), so the request stays pending.
  3. run-2's attempt gives up at T1 > T0. The guard clears, and the
     retriage of run-1 is enqueued with user_context_rev=1.
  4. Its decision: failed_patch_attempts and last_failed_patch_at count
     gave-up attempts for (origin, target) across all runs in the window
     (dportsv3/agent/decision.py:114-133), so the newest is T1 > T0 and
     the context is stale: no promotion, no pardon. A MANUAL
     classification escalates again, and the guidance is never tried,
     though the attempt's prompt would have carried it.
  An attempt on another build line does not cause this: the guard and
  the attempt count are both per line.
  Workaround today: the operator submits the context again; the new
  revision is newer than T1.

CANDIDATE FIXES. Default: (a). It is prototyped, needs no join through
bundles, and keeps today's rule for jobs with no revision. Choose (b)
only if a same-run triage of another flavor should also count the
context as fresh, and then first measure how many patch jobs have no
bundle_id. Record the choice in this bead, and the reason if it is (b).
  (a) The revision the retriage carries. enqueue_triage_job writes
      user_context_rev=<the revision that triggered it> into every
      retriage job file (runner.py:1105) and nothing reads it (grep:
      one hit, the write). Its one caller is process_user_context_updates
      (runner.py:1930), so only operator retriages carry a revision. A
      job whose user_context_rev equals the context_rev of its own
      (run_id, origin) row is, by construction, the retry that revision
      asked for: count the context as fresh whatever the attempt history
      says. Hook jobs carry no revision and keep today's rule.
      - PortHistory.load: a second keyword-only parameter after run_id,
        "context_rev: int | None = None", and a docstring paragraph:

        ``context_rev`` is the revision a retriage job was enqueued for
        (its ``user_context_rev``). When it equals the revision of the
        job's own context row, the job is the retry that revision asked
        for, and the context counts as fresh whatever the attempt
        history says.

      - The context query selects the revision too, and the freshness
        rule gains a first branch:

            SELECT updated_at, context_rev FROM user_context
             WHERE run_id = ? AND origin = ?

            if user_context_at:
                if (context_rev is not None
                        and int(row[1] or 0) == context_rev):
                    has_fresh_user_context = True
                elif not last_failed_patch_at:
                    has_fresh_user_context = True
                else:
                    has_fresh_user_context = (
                        user_context_at > last_failed_patch_at
                    )

      - runner._load_port_history gains "context_rev: int | None =
        None" after run_id and passes context_rev=context_rev.
      - TriageStep.run passes
        context_rev=int(job.get("user_context_rev") or 0) or None
        beside run_id, and the services list in its docstring reads
        load_port_history (target, origin, window_hours, run_id=None,
        context_rev=None) -> PortHistory.
      - tests/test_user_context_is_per_target.py's db fixture: add
        "context_rev INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1," to its user_context
        table, as the real schema has (dportsv3/db/schema.py:321).
        Without it exactly 4 of that file's tests fail, because the
        query names a column the fixture lacks:
        test_context_for_this_target_counts,
        test_the_newest_row_does_not_leak_across_targets,
        test_the_patch_cap_is_not_forgiven_by_the_other_build_line and
        test_context_newer_than_this_target_s_failure_is_still_fresh.
      Prototyped on top of .17 (code decision.py +11 -2, runner.py +4
      -2, steps.py +1, before the docstring line): the test below
      passes, and the two .17 test files give 28 passed.
  (b) A per-run freshness reference. Compute last_failed_patch_at from
      the failed patch jobs of the job's own run (jobs.bundle_id ->
      bundles.run_id), and keep failed_patch_attempts, the cap count, per
      (origin, target) across runs. Not prototyped; UNVERIFIED for job
      rows with no bundle_id.
  They differ on a same-run triage without a revision (another flavor's
  first failure in run-1 after the operator answered): (a) keeps today's
  rule, so the context is stale there; (b) counts it as fresh. Both keep
  "one free retry per context revision" (decide() rule 3): a failed
  retry leaves a gave-up attempt newer than the revision.

TESTS. tests/test_runner_e2e_lifecycle.py, appended after poly-7pwa.17's
section:

title: PortHistory.load swallows sqlite3 errors, so a failed jobs query silently lifts the patch cap and opens MANUAL promotions
description: Filed 2026-10-04 by the poly-7pwa spec review (round 2). DESIGN holds the problem, the evidence and the change; ACCEPTANCE says when it is done.
design:
STATE, 2026-10-04. Open, not started. Split out of poly-7pwa.17's
RELATED note by decision D6; outside the epic, independent of it. The
four clauses below have the same text on master and on poly-7pwa. Land
it on master, after poly-7pwa merges if .21 is in progress (the merge
is --ff-only); never on the branch. If poly-7pwa.17 is pending on the
same tree, the two
edit neighbouring lines of the user_context block and apply in either
order without conflict (measured: both orders give the same tree).

PREMISE, verified 2026-10-04. PortHistory.load
(dportsv3/agent/decision.py) runs four guarded queries, each ending

    except sqlite3.Error:
        pass

(decision.py:111, :132, :153, :180 on master; :111, :132, :177, :204 on
the post-carry tree). A failure reads as no history and nothing is
logged. What each failure does to decide():

    query (name used below)  on failure                  effect
    bundles                  recent_failures 0           the bundle backstop
                                                         (rule 6) never fires
    failed_patch_attempts    failed_patch_attempts 0,    the patch cap never
      (the jobs query)       last_failed_patch_at ''     fires; any context
                                                         row counts as fresh
                                                         whatever its age
    user_context             flag False                  no promotion, no
                                                         pardon (fails closed)
    failure_signature        signature None, count 0     rule 4 never fires;
                                                         rule 5 still
                                                         escalates

  Measured on the real schema with a jobs table that lacks
  retire_reason, five gave-up attempts and a 365-day-old context row in
  the job's run: failed_patch_attempts 0 and the flag True; compile-error
  -> auto_patch instead of escalate_manual (patch_cap); missing-dep ->
  auto_patch with promoted_via user_context. With the jobs query working,
  both escalate.
  CORRECTION to poly-7pwa.17's note ("a real schema fault silently
  suppresses promotions") and poly-7pwa.10's notes ("failing to False"):
  only a failed user_context query fails closed. A failed jobs query
  lifts the cap and opens promotions. After poly-7pwa.17 the opened
  promotion is limited to the job's own run, whose prompt carries the
  text; the lifted cap is not limited.
  Realistic causes: a column a migration has not added yet, "database is
  locked" while the tracker writes the same file, a damaged file.

CHANGE. dportsv3/agent/decision.py only. Add "import logging" and, after
the Action alias:

    _LOG = logging.getLogger(__name__)

    # (query, exception class, message) of every history query failure
    # this process has reported. load() runs on every triage, so each
    # distinct failure is said once; a different failure of the same
    # query is said again.
    _REPORTED_FAILURES: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()


    def _history_query_failed(query: str, exc: sqlite3.Error) -> None:
        """Say once that a PortHistory.load query failed, and what it
        costs.

        load() reads a failed query as no history so that a decision
        can still be made, and that is not a safe default for every
        query: a failed jobs query counts no failed attempt, so the
        patch cap never fires and any operator context counts as fresh
        whatever its age.
        """
        key = (query, type(exc).__name__, str(exc))
        if key in _REPORTED_FAILURES:
            return
        _REPORTED_FAILURES.add(key)
        _LOG.warning(
            "PortHistory.load: the %s query failed (%s: %s); it reads as "
            "no history until this is fixed. Reported once per distinct "
            "failure.",
            query, type(exc).__name__, exc,
        )

  The four clauses become

        except sqlite3.Error as exc:
            _history_query_failed("<name>", exc)

  with the names bundles, failed_patch_attempts, user_context and
  failure_signature, in file order. Every degrade value stays as it is.

  Why the key is (query, class, message): load() runs on every triage,
  so an unkeyed warning floods runner.log; keyed on the query name alone,
  the first failure of a query hides every later, different failure of
  it until the long-running daemon restarts. sqlite's messages are fixed
  strings per cause, so the set stays small.

  Where it goes: nothing in dportsv3 configures logging in the runner
  (logging.basicConfig appears only in the _manual_test scripts, and the
  tracker's _configure_app_logging runs only for tracker serve). After
  importing the runner and litellm the root logger has no handler, so
  Python's last-resort handler writes the WARNING to stderr (measured),
  which daemon -o sends to runner.log (deploy/rc.d/polytropos_runner:79,

title: quarter bring-up: a new build line starts as a copy of @main's own blocks and payload
description: Filed 2026-10-04 by the poly-7pwa spec review (round 2). DESIGN holds the problem, the evidence and the change; ACCEPTANCE says when it is done.
design:
REVISED 2026-10-06, after poly-7pwa.27 (744dc5d). The 2026-10-04 design
below the line is superseded; it is kept for the record.

WHY REVISED. The old design moved FILES only, and assumed the folder
install (poly-u9n4.3: no materialize ops). Under .27 every fix to a port
that already has ops goes into a `target @<line>` block, mk and text ops
included. A quarterly cut from main needs all of @main's own ops, not only
its patches, and none of them reach it: today `target @main` blocks hold
28 ops in lang/rust, 9 in shells/bash-completion, 2 each in ports-mgmt/pkg
and cad/librecad (DeltaPorts d9e321bde6c). The old design needed u9n4.3
first and would have missed every mk/text op.

REJECTED: extend each list (`target @main` -> `target @main,@2026Q4`).
Smallest diff, but every @main op and every dragonfly/@main/ file becomes
shared with the new line. install_patches (.27, row 5a) then cannot re-cut
a @main patch at all: its own copy would be the shared file itself
(held_shared). And a @main job's "change it in your block" (row 3) turns
into override-or-escalate for every op.

CHANGE. The new line starts as a copy of --from, the way a quarterly
branch starts as a copy of main:

  dportsv3 migrate branch-line --from @main --new @2026Q4
      [--write] [--delta-root DIR]

Dry run by default. For each DSL port (compat ports are skipped) with at
least one block naming --from:
- append ONE `target <new>` block at the end of overlay.dops, holding the
  body of every block that names --from (its own and any list it is in),
  in file order, comments included. Existing text is untouched.
- a payload path under <lane>/@<T>/ (file materialize src, patch apply
  path) is rewritten to <lane>/@<new>/, and the file is copied there.
  The new line reads no other line's folder.
- self-check, in code, before any write: the old and new overlays plan;
  every line other than --new plans the same ops as before; --new plans
  exactly --from's ops (scoped paths mapped). A port failing it is skipped
  with the reason, unchanged.
Skipped, with a reason, nothing written: an overlay that names --new
already; one that does not plan; a payload file that is missing, or whose
copy already exists with other bytes.

ALSO. steps._shared_ops_failing (row 6) treats ops with the same payload
in two blocks as shared. After a branch, @main and @2026Q4 hold identical
but independent copies, so an own-block failure on @main would escalate
as "shared". Shared becomes: the same statement (span) under another
line, which is what a target list is.

Code: dportsv3/migration/line_branch.py (branch_overlay, pure over text;
plan_branch; apply_branch), the subcommand in cli.py and
commands/migrate.py, a short section in docs/dportsv3-user-guide.md.

OUT OF SCOPE, filed separately: retiring a line (drop its blocks and
folder; collapse blocks that cover every live line). Creating the new
line's freebsd branch or env. After u9n4.3 deletes materialize ops,
branch-line must copy the whole dragonfly/@<from>/ folder (noted there).

----- 2026-10-04 design (superseded) -----
STATE, 2026-10-04. New, from the epic's D4. A child of poly-7pwa but not
epic-blocking: the epic may close with it open. Write it after
poly-u9n4.3 (the folder is the install, no payload ops) and poly-7pwa.4
(the rule that makes per-line copies).

PREMISE.
- Under D4, a line whose build rejects a shared dragonfly/ patch takes
  its own copy in dragonfly/@<line>/, and the shared copy stays. A new
  quarterly branches from main, so at bring-up it needs @main's copies,
  but the folder rule gives it only the shared ones: it rejects, loudly,
  every shared patch @main has replaced.
- Today (DeltaPorts c030e103838) per-line copies exist on 2 ports.
  lang/rust has 14 files in dragonfly/@main/ and 15 in
  dragonfly/@2026Q3/, none with a shared file of the same name;
  ports-mgmt/pkg has one in each, under different names. Measured with
  find over ports/*/*/dragonfly/@*/.
- No list of build lines is configured (poly-7pwa.8), so the operator
  names them.

CHANGE. A command over a DeltaPorts checkout,
    dportsv3 migrate promote-line-copies --from @main --new @2026Q4 \
        --live @2026Q3,@main [--write] [--delta-root DIR]
--delta-root falls back to $DPORTS_DELTA_ROOT through
paths.resolve_delta_root. --live must include --from. Without --write it
prints the plan and changes nothing.
Code: a new module dportsv3/migration/line_copies.py (the package the
other migrate subcommands live in), registered as a subcommand in
cli.py's _register_migrate_parser, with
    plan_promotion(delta_root, from_line, new_line, live) -> list[Move]
    apply_promotion(delta_root, moves) -> None
where Move is a frozen dataclass (port, name, action, detail) and action
is one of "promote", "copy-to-new" or "skip"; a skip carries its reason
in detail, and apply_promotion changes nothing for it. For each DSL port
(it has overlay.dops; compat ports are skipped) and each file
dragonfly/@<from>/<name>:
- skip it, with a reason, when an explicit file materialize op reads it
  (a custom destination);
- if the shared dragonfly/<name> exists (action "promote"): for every live
  line L other than --from that has no dragonfly/@L/<name>, copy the
  shared file to dragonfly/@L/<name>, so L keeps what it builds today;
  then move dragonfly/@<from>/<name> to dragonfly/<name>; then delete any
  dragonfly/@L/<name> byte-identical to the new shared file;
- else (action "copy-to-new"): copy dragonfly/@<from>/<name> to
  dragonfly/@<new>/<name>. Promoting it would add the patch to live lines
  that never had it.
Afterwards each live line installs the same dragonfly/ files as before,
and --new installs what --from does.

EDGE CASES.
- A shared patch --from removes with a target-block file remove (the
  superseded case of poly-7pwa.4): plan_promotion adds a skip row whose
  detail names the remove op, and nothing changes. The new line inherits
  the shared patch, rejects it loudly and removes it for itself.
- Copies of retired lines (dragonfly/@X/, X neither live nor --new):
  plan_promotion adds a skip row for each (detail "retired line"), and
  nothing is deleted.
- diffs/@T/ is out of scope (diffs are applied by ops).

TESTS. New tests/test_promote_line_copies.py, synthetic DeltaPorts trees
in tmp_path; line names are labels.
1. test_promotion_keeps_every_live_line_and_gives_the_new_one_from: shared
   N holds A, @main/N holds B; --live @2026Q3,@main, --new @2026Q4. After
   apply: shared N holds B, @2026Q3/N holds A, @main/N is gone. Per-line
   installed sets (poly-u9n4.2's folder rule): @main B, @2026Q3 A,
   @2026Q4 B.
2. test_a_file_with_no_shared_copy_goes_to_the_new_line_only: only
   @main/N exists: it is copied to @2026Q4/N and nothing else changes.
3. test_a_live_line_with_its_own_copy_is_not_pinned_again: shared N
   holds A, @main/N holds B, @2026Q3/N holds C. After apply: @2026Q3/N
   still holds C, the shared N holds B, and @main/N is gone.
4. test_an_op_read_file_is_skipped: an overlay op "file materialize
   dragonfly/@main/N -> custom/N" makes plan_promotion return a Move for N
   with action "skip" and a non-empty detail, and apply_promotion leaves
   every file under the port byte-identical.
5. test_without_write_nothing_changes: on test 1's tree, the command
   without --write prints the planned moves (plan_promotion returns at
   least one), and every file under ports/ is byte-identical afterwards.

GATE. On a throwaway DeltaPorts copy, a whole-tree compose of every live
line is byte-identical before and after --write (poly-u9n4.2's parity
gate).

DEPENDS ON. poly-u9n4.3, poly-7pwa.4.

OUT OF SCOPE. Creating the new line's branch or env. Deleting a retired
line's copies. diffs/.
acceptance_criteria:
- dportsv3 migrate branch-line exists as designed (REVISED 2026-10-06),
  dry run by default; branch_overlay, plan_branch, apply_branch in
  dportsv3/migration/line_branch.py.
- tests/test_branch_line.py passes: per-line apply of a synthetic port
  gives the same tree for every old line before and after, and the new
  line's tree equals --from's; the skips; dry run writes nothing; the

- _shared_ops_failing: an identical op in another line's own block is not

- Compose of the touched ports on a throwaway DeltaPorts copy: @main and

- No new environment variable; the full suite passes.

Gate on a throwaway copy of DeltaPorts d9e321bde6c, composing the 4 touched ports (lang/rust, ports-mgmt/pkg, cad/librecad, shells/bash-completion): @main and @2026Q3 byte-identical before/after --write; @2026Q4 (freebsd main as stand-in, only error the expected branch mismatch) identical to @main after, 20 files different before. title: a target list that repeats a selector runs every op under it twice on that build line
description: Filed 2026-10-04 by the poly-7pwa spec review (round 2). DESIGN holds the problem, the evidence and the change; ACCEPTANCE says when it is done.
design:
STATE. New, P3, bug, child of poly-7pwa. Found while measuring
poly-7pwa.3's rule. It lands after poly-7pwa merges to master (wave 3);
it edits the TargetDirective branch of dportsv3/engine/semantic.py, which
.21 row 11 does not touch.

PREMISE, verified 2026-10-04 on master ab725ac plus the seven picks and
row 11's change, against DeltaPorts c030e103838.
- The parser keeps every selector of a comma list (parser.py:221), and
  analyze_document's TargetDirective branch (semantic.py:374-396) checks
  only "@any mixed with others" and each selector's form. So "target
  @main,@main" is accepted, and every op under it expands once per
  selector: twice on @main.
- Effect, with apply_dsl on @main: 'text line-insert-after file files/x
  anchor "A" line "B"' under "target @main,@main" turns "A\n" into
  "A\nB\nB\n" (inserted twice) with ok=True. "mk add USES b" under the
  same directive leaves "USES= a b": token add is idempotent, so only
  ops that are not idempotent show the doubling.
- Reach: 0 of the target directives in the 5087 overlays repeat a
  selector (regex scan of every "target" line). Nothing writes target
  lines automatically today; hand edits and the planned overlay editor
  (poly-fklo) could.
- poly-7pwa.3's dead-op rule deduplicates selectors per statement, so it
  neither reports nor hides this.

CHANGE. dportsv3/engine/semantic.py, analyze_document, TargetDirective
branch: after the loop that checks each selector's form and before
"current_targets = tuple(targets)" (:396 on master ab725ac, :500 once
.21 row 11 has landed; the quoted line is the anchor), add, at that

    # (models.order_ops_for_target): another line's op is

    # A later mk.var op on the same name (mk add after mk set)
    # leaves no literal to compare, so the name is dropped.
    ran = {row.id for row in op_results if row.status == "applied"}
    values: dict[str, str] = {}
    for op in ordered_ops:
        name = op.payload.get("name")
        if (
            op.id not in ran
            or not op.kind.startswith("mk.var.")
            or not isinstance(name, str)

    """The bmake oracle expects what THIS build line's ops left behind.

    apply_plan built the oracle's expectation from every `mk set` in the plan
    that had not failed. Another build line's op is "skipped", not "failed",
    so it counted, and in file order the value written last in the file was
    expected on every line (poly-lt5q's oracle, 3e08487). A later op that
    changes the same variable (`mk add` after `mk set`) leaves no literal to
    compare against either.
    """

    from __future__ import annotations

    import pytest

    import dportsv3.engine.apply as apply_mod
    from dportsv3.engine.api import apply_dsl
    from dportsv3.engine.oracle import OracleResult

    HEAD = 'port x/y\ntype port\nreason "r"\n'


    @pytest.fixture
    def expected(monkeypatch):
        """The ``expect`` mapping apply hands the oracle (bmake stubbed)."""
        seen: dict[str, str] = {}

        def fake(root, *, profile, expect=None, **_):
            seen.update(expect or {})
            return OracleResult(ok=True, profile=profile)

        monkeypatch.setattr(apply_mod, "run_bmake_oracle", fake)
        return seen


    def _apply(tmp_path, text, target, makefile="FOO= upstream\n"):
        (tmp_path / "Makefile").write_text(
            makefile + ".include <bsd.port.mk>\n"
        )
        result = apply_dsl(
            HEAD + text, port_root=tmp_path, target=target,
            oracle_profile="local",
        )
        assert result.ok, result.diagnostics
        return (tmp_path / "Makefile").read_text()


    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "target, want",
        [
            ("@2026Q3", {"FOO": "q3"}),
            ("@main", {"FOO": "main", "BAR": "main-only"}),
        ],
    )
    def test_the_oracle_expects_what_this_build_line_set(
        tmp_path, expected, target, want
    ):
        text = (
            'target @main\nmk set FOO "main"\nmk set BAR "main-only"\n'
            'target @2026Q3\nmk set FOO "q3"\n'
        )
        _apply(tmp_path, text, target)
        assert expected == want


    def test_the_oracle_expects_the_value_that_ran_last(tmp_path, expected):
        """The @any op is written last but runs first on @main (.11)."""
        text = (
            'target @main\nmk set FOO "main"\n'
            'target @any\nmk set FOO "any"\n'
        )
        makefile = _apply(tmp_path, text, "@main")
        assert "FOO= main" in makefile
        assert expected == {"FOO": "main"}


    def test_a_variable_a_later_op_changes_is_not_expected(
        tmp_path, expected
    ):
        """ports-mgmt/pkg's LDFLAGS shape: mk set, then mk add on it."""
        text = 'mk set LDFLAGS "-L/a"\nmk add LDFLAGS -R/b\nmk set KEEP "k"\n'
        _apply(tmp_path, text, "@main", makefile="LDFLAGS= x\nKEEP= y\n")

title: install_patches writes an incremental genpatch diff over the file's existing dragonfly/ patch, so that patch's change is lost
description: Filed 2026-10-04 by the poly-7pwa spec review (round 2). DESIGN holds the problem, the evidence and the change; ACCEPTANCE says when it is done.
design:
STATE, 2026-10-04. Pre-existing on master for canonically named patches;
poly-7pwa.21 row 12 (poly-7pwa.2) extends it to the rest. Frequency
UNVERIFIED.
- flow-patch.md, "Creating a static source patch", step 2 tells the agent
  to run make_patch when the file is already touched by a files/patch-*
  or by an existing dragonfly/* patch; do-patch applies dragonfly/* too,
  and step 3 dupes after it. So the .orig baseline already contains the
  existing DragonFly patch of that file, and genpatch emits only the new
  change.
- install_patches then writes that diff OVER the existing patch: by name
  when the existing patch already has genpatch's name for the file (on
  master; 3889 of the 4235 single-file dragonfly/patch-* sources in
  DeltaPorts are named that way), and after row 12 also through the
  header key for the rest. The existing DragonFly change for that file is
  gone from the overlay. do-patch then applies the incremental diff to a
  tree without it: a reject (loud) or, when the hunks do not overlap, a
  build without the original fix (silent).
- The re-cut flow is not affected: error-prefer's re-cut starts from
  make_extract (the drifted patch rejects, so make_patch cannot run), so
  its genpatch output is the whole patch and replacing it is right.

MEASURE FIRST, read-only, over the builder's patch bundles: count attempts
whose tool log has make_patch, then genpatch of a WRKSRC path P, then
install_patches, on a port whose overlay already materializes a
dragonfly/ patch with the single '+++ ' path P. Zero over the history:
drop to P4 and record the number.

CANDIDATE FIXES, to choose after measuring:
(a) Baseline without DragonFly patches: make_patch gains an option that
    runs do-patch with DFLY_PATCHDIR pointed at an empty directory, so
    dupe snapshots the post-files/ state and genpatch emits the whole
    DragonFly change of the file (UNVERIFIED that the DPorts framework
    honours that override).
(b) install_patches refuses to replace an existing patch of the same file
    when this attempt's make_patch applied it cleanly (the attempt's tool
    log shows it), and says to re-cut the whole patch.
(c) Playbook only: step 2 tells the agent not to build on make_patch for
    a file that already has a dragonfly/ patch. Weakest; prompt cost.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE.
- The measurement is recorded in this bead.
- If a fix is built: a behavioural test drives install_patches with an
  existing dragonfly/ patch of src/a.c and an incremental genpatch output
  for src/a.c produced after make_patch, and the existing change survives
  in what compose installs.
- Otherwise the bead is closed with the number and the reason.
notes: 2026-10-04: not implemented. The design asks to measure first, read-only, over the builder's patch bundles, and leaves the fix (a/b/c) to that number; the tracker and bundles were not reachable from the dev machine. Findings: (a) relies on make's command-line DFLY_PATCHDIR overriding '?=' (DPorts Mk/bsd.port.mk:1384, do-patch.sh:157) but, with dragonfly/ skipped, the working file also lacks the existing DragonFly change, so genpatch would still emit only the new edit unless that patch is re-applied after dupe; the 880:dfly-patch hook is not governed by DFLY_PATCHDIR. (b) needs per-attempt state that install_patches does not have (e.g. make_patch marks (env, origin), reset_attempt_workspace clears it).

title: the collision check covers materialize and copy but not file remove, which is last-wins against them too
description:
poly-7pwa.3 added E_SEM_DUPLICATE_DESTINATION for two 'file materialize'/'file
copy' ops writing one dst. 'file remove dragonfly/x' beside 'file materialize ...
-> dragonfly/x' in one scope plans clean, yet it is last-wins too: fsops
stage_remove pops pending writes and stage_write* discards pending removes, so
whichever op runs last decides whether the file exists.

The check's own message promises 'one writer per destination per build line' and
enforces it for two of the three ops that write one. Deliberate scoping in .3
(remove is not a writer in the same sense) but the gap is real and the message
overpromises.

Decide which: extend the check to treat remove as a writer of the same
destination, or narrow the message. Extending is probably right -- the failure
shape is identical, and 'the file silently is or is not there depending on op
order' is worse for a remove than for a materialize.
design:
STATE. Open, P3. No work of its own: it is implemented by poly-7pwa.3 as
.21 row 11 on branch poly-7pwa, in the same commit, and closes there.
Under the dead-op rule a file remove plays both roles. It removes the
file whole, so it kills an earlier write of that file; and it leaves a
result (the file is absent), so a later write kills it. The description's
"collision check" and its "message that promises one writer per
destination per build line" are a417e00's, which .21 skips (row 5), so
that half of the description is moot.

                                         row fails (missing subject)
    remove on-missing noop, then mat.    AAA, ok
    @any materialize, @main remove       @main absent, @2026Q3 AAA

title: PORTREVISION needs a relative bump op: an absolute value pins every line it applies to, scoped or not
description:
Split out of poly-7pwa.12, which fixed the guidance and deliberately did not
touch the engine. This is the option that would make the hazard impossible
rather than merely documented.

THE PROBLEM. PORTREVISION is the one variable whose correct value is RELATIVE to
what the branch already has. The DSL can only say "set it to N". So:
- `mk set PORTREVISION "N"` in @any writes N to every build line, and branches
  legitimately differ -- a downgrade where another line sits higher.
- scoping the bump per target (what .12's guidance now says) is correct but
  leaves the other lines un-bumped until someone bumps them by hand.

Neither is right; they are two ways of being wrong, and .12 picked the one whose
failure is visible and recoverable.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT: an op that expresses the intent, e.g. `mk bump PORTREVISION`
-- read the current value in the composed Makefile, add one, write it back;
insert `PORTREVISION= 1` when absent. Then one @any op is correct on every build
line, which is what the original guidance wanted and could not express.

WHY IT IS NOT A SMALL CHANGE, and why it is filed rather than done: it is a new
DSL verb. Grammar (parser + lexer), semantic validation, an executor, emit.py,
docs/dsl-v0.md, dops_quickref.md, the playbooks, and a migration story for
existing `mk set PORTREVISION` ops. It also needs a decision about
non-numeric/absent values and about whether the bump is idempotent across
re-composes of the same tree (it must be -- compose runs repeatedly, and an op
that increments every time would walk PORTREVISION upward on every build).
That last point is the real design question: "bump" is not naturally idempotent,
and compose is.

MEASURED FIRST, so nobody assumes urgency: exactly ONE PORTREVISION op exists in
the whole DeltaPorts tree today -- graphics/gdal, value "3", @any scope, in an
overlay with no target-scoped blocks at all. Zero overlays carry PORTREVISION
alongside a non-@any block. So the clobber is not currently happening anywhere;
this is about what the agent will write as multi-target work spreads.

A cheaper interim, if the full verb is not wanted: a semantic WARNING when an
@any `mk set PORTREVISION` appears in an overlay that also carries target-scoped
blocks. Note semantic.py currently has no warning severity at all -- every
diagnostic is an error and `ok=not diagnostics` -- so introducing one is its own
small piece of work, and as an error it would fail graphics/gdal today.
design:
STATE. Open, P3, no code anywhere. Split from poly-7pwa.12, whose
PORTREVISION guidance (221c4eb, carried as .21 row 6 and cut to its rule
by row 6a) this bead replaces. Wave 6: after poly-7pwa.21; after
poly-fklo.2 if both are still pending, so emit's new builder matches its
style. poly-7pwa closes after this bead. Line numbers are the post-carry
tree (master ab725ac plus .21 rows 1,2,3,4,6,7,9) as of 2026-10-04;
re-read them before editing.

PREMISE, verified 2026-10-04.
- mk set writes an absolute value: it replaces the one assignment or
  inserts "NAME= value" before the first target or include
  (engine/executors/mk_ops.py exec_mk_var_set, insert point
  _mk_var_set_insert_line).
- An absolute PORTREVISION pins every line it applies to, scoped or not.
  Compose re-seeds each port from upstream on every run (copy_tree is
  rmtree then copytree, fsutils.py:132-137) and applies the op again, so
  each later upstream bump on that line is reverted until a person
  removes the op. Scoping (.12's guidance) stops the cross-line
  downgrade and leaves the pin on the scoped line; on @main it never
  expires.
- The live pin: graphics/gdal's @any mk set PORTREVISION "3". Upstream
  main (3.13.3) has no PORTREVISION and 2026Q3 (3.13.1) has 2 (git show
  <branch>:graphics/gdal/Makefile on the freebsd-ports refs of
  2026-09-27); both lines compose to "PORTREVISION= 3" (main: inserted
  at line 234; 2026Q3: line 3 replaced).
- Demand: 1 PORTREVISION op in 5087 overlays, and the patch agent wrote
  it. DeltaPorts 2112942abbe (2026-09-16, "graphics/gdal: fix build
  failure on DragonFly"; body "... bumped PORTREVISION") followed the
  playbook this bead replaces: master flow-patch.md:187-189 ("Keep
  PORTREVISION bumps in @any") and :329-338 ("compute <N> from the
  current value", which turned 2026Q3's 2 into 3). That is 1 of 212
  agent delivery commits. The overlay's "auto-converted from compat"
  header comes from the earlier mass conversion (fef107ea6d5), which
  wrote no PORTREVISION op. The convert flow wrote nothing here.
- Idempotency is free: every compose applies ops to a fresh upstream
  copy (copy_tree per origin for --origin composes, per top directory
  for full composes), so a bump computes from upstream's value each time
  and cannot walk upward.
- mk eval can express a relative value only as a shell-arithmetic :=
  that runs on every make parse; not acceptable (this bead's notes).

WHAT A LEXICAL BUMP MEETS. Method: every port Makefile on the
freebsd-ports main and 2026Q3 refs (2026-09-27) read with git cat-file,
continuation lines joined, .if depth tracked; rows in the executor's
check order.

                                           main           2026Q3
    1 slave (MASTERDIR= at top level)   1146   3.3%    1130   3.2%
    2 more than one assignment             4              4
    3 one assignment inside .if            2              2
    4 operator other than = or ?=          0              0
    5 value not an integer                13             11
    6 one integer assignment, =        15471  43.9%   16048  46.1%
      one integer assignment, ?=         121   0.3%     120   0.3%
    7 none, and any quoted .include      461   1.3%     463   1.3%
    8 none                             18016  51.1%   17008  48.9%
    port Makefiles                     35234          34786

Rows 6 and 8 bump or insert: 95.4% on both branches. Every other row
refuses loudly.
- Row 2 is dns/bind9-devel, dns/bind920, math/lapack and www/angie, all
  assigning only inside .if blocks; row 3 is proftpd and u-boot-master.
- Row 1: a lexical bump is wrong for most slaves. On main, 1147 slaves
  set MASTERDIR= at any depth (1146 at top level, the executor's test):
  325 have no value and a master ?= default (an insert drops the master's
  value), 207 have no value and a master = (an insert is silently
  overridden), 62 carry a value the master's = overrides; a lexical bump
  is right for 391 (258 own value under a master ?=, 13 own value and no
  master value, 120 no value anywhere); for 158 the master could not be
  resolved (111) or is missing (47); 4 masters use both = and ?=.
- Row 6 ?=: 121 ports assign it with ?=; at least 88 of them are masters
  of a slave (33 are not, for example audio/libcanberra and
  devel/boost-libs; 111 slaves use MASTERDIR forms the check cannot
  resolve). The bump keeps ?= so a slave can still override.
- Row 7: v1 refuses every port with no assignment and any quoted
  .include, without resolving paths: the executor has no ports root
  (ApplyContext carries source_root and port_root only,
  engine/models.py:128-136), and a dry run's port_root is the upstream
  port. Of the 461, 34 include a file that does assign PORTREVISION: 25
